dab.t:
v. 轻拍；轻涂
n. 少量

e.en: Add a {dab} of butter to the pan before frying the eggs.
e.zh: 煎蛋前在锅里加一小块黄油。

e.en: She used a tissue to {dab} her eyes after the movie.
e.zh: 看完电影后她用纸巾轻轻擦拭眼角。

dabble.t:
v. 涉猎；浅尝
v. 戏水

e.en: He likes to {dabble} in photography on weekends.
e.zh: 他喜欢在周末玩玩摄影。

e.en: She started to {dabble} in stock trading during the pandemic.
e.zh: 疫情期间她开始小试身手地玩起了股票。

dabbler.t: n. 浅尝者；业余爱好者

e.en: He's just a {dabbler} in coding, not a real engineer.
e.zh: 他只是个编程业余爱好者，并不是真正的工程师。

e.en: As a {dabbler} in painting, she sells the occasional canvas.
e.zh: 作为一名业余画家，她偶尔会卖出一幅画。

e.en: A high-quality {DAC} can dramatically improve your headphone sound.
e.zh: 一台高质量的数模转换器能显著提升耳机音质。

e.en: He plugged a portable {DAC} into his laptop's USB port.
e.zh: 他把便携式数模转换器插进笔记本的USB接口。

dacca.t: n. 达卡（孟加拉国首都旧拼写）

e.en: Her flight to {Dacca} was delayed by heavy monsoon rain.
e.zh: 她飞往达卡的航班因强季风雨而延误。

e.en: The old map still labels the city as {Dacca}, not Dhaka.
e.zh: 那张旧地图上这座城市仍标作Dacca，而非Dhaka。

dace.t: n. 雅罗鱼（一种淡水鱼）

e.en: The fisherman caught a small {dace} in the shallow stream.
e.zh: 渔夫在浅溪里钓到了一条小雅罗鱼。

e.en: Schools of silver {dace} darted under the bridge.
e.zh: 成群的银色雅罗鱼在桥下窜来窜去。

e.en: They escaped Moscow's heat at their tiny country {dacha}.
e.zh: 他们到乡下小别墅去躲避莫斯科的酷暑。

e.en: Every weekend the family drives out to their wooden {dacha}.
e.zh: 每个周末全家都会开车去他们的木屋别墅。

e.en: Her tiny {dachshund} barks at every passing squirrel.
e.zh: 她的小腊肠狗见到每只过路的松鼠都要叫。

e.en: The {dachshund} waddled down the hallway with its short legs.
e.zh: 那只腊肠狗迈着短腿摇摇摆摆地走过走廊。

e.en: The poet ended each line with a perfect {dactyl}.
e.zh: 诗人每一行都以完美的扬抑抑格收尾。

e.en: In English verse, a {dactyl} is one stressed plus two unstressed syllables.
e.zh: 在英语诗歌中，扬抑抑格由一个重音和两个轻音构成。

e.en: My {dad} taught me how to ride a bike.
e.zh: 我爸爸教会了我骑自行车。

e.en: He's a proud {dad} of three energetic kids.
e.zh: 他是三个精力旺盛孩子的骄傲爸爸。

dada.t: n. 达达主义（艺术流派）

e.en: The artist studied {dada} movements from early twentieth century Europe.
e.zh: 这位艺术家研究了二十世纪初欧洲的达达主义运动。

e.en: His paintings show a clear {dada} influence in their absurd imagery.
e.zh: 他的画作在荒诞意象中明显带有达达主义的影响。

e.en: The toddler ran shouting {dadda} when the front door opened.
e.zh: 前门一开,小孩就大叫着爸爸跑过去。

e.en: She called her father {dadda} long after she grew up.
e.zh: 长大以后她还是一直叫父亲爸爸。

e.en: All the {daddies} gathered at the school sports day.
e.zh: 所有的爸爸们都聚集在学校运动会上。

e.en: The book features stories about loving {daddies} and their kids.
e.zh: 这本书讲述了慈爱的爸爸们和孩子的故事。

e.en: My {daddy} reads me a bedtime story every night.
e.zh: 我爸爸每晚都给我读睡前故事。

e.en: He became a {daddy} for the first time last week.
e.zh: 他上周第一次当了爸爸。

e.en: The hallway features a wooden {dado} along the lower walls.
e.zh: 走廊下半部墙面装有木制护墙板。

e.en: They painted the {dado} a darker shade than the upper wall.
e.zh: 他们把护墙板漆成比上半墙更深的颜色。

e.en: The {dads} took turns coaching the kids' soccer team.
e.zh: 几位爸爸轮流执教孩子们的足球队。

e.en: Many {dads} struggle to balance work and family time.
e.zh: 许多爸爸都难以平衡工作和家庭时间。

daedalus.t: n. 代达罗斯（希腊神话工匠）

e.en: In Greek myth, {Daedalus} built wings of feathers and wax.
e.zh: 在希腊神话中,代达罗斯用羽毛和蜡造了翅膀。

e.en: The novel borrows its hero's name from {Daedalus}, the master craftsman.
e.zh: 这部小说的主角名字取自巧匠代达罗斯。

daemon.t:
n. 守护进程（后台程序）
n. 精灵；守护神

e.en: The background {daemon} keeps the server logs synchronized.
e.zh: 后台守护进程负责保持服务器日志同步。

e.en: Restart the print {daemon} if your jobs get stuck in queue.
e.zh: 如果打印任务卡在队列中,请重启打印守护进程。

daf.t: n. 达夫（荷兰卡车品牌）

e.en: The factory still produces parts for the classic {DAF} truck.
e.zh: 这家工厂仍在生产经典达夫卡车的零件。

e.en: Drivers praised the {DAF} for its smooth automatic transmission.
e.zh: 司机们称赞达夫卡车的自动变速箱很顺畅。

e.en: A bright yellow {daffodil} bloomed beside the garden path.
e.zh: 一朵亮黄色的水仙花在花园小径旁绽放。

e.en: She painted the wall a soft {daffodil} color for spring.
e.zh: 她把墙漆成柔和的水仙黄,迎接春天。

e.en: My grandma has some {daffy} ideas about modern technology.
e.zh: 我奶奶对现代科技有些古怪的想法。

e.en: The comedy stars a {daffy} detective who solves crimes by accident.
e.zh: 这部喜剧主演是一位糊涂侦探,总是误打误撞破案。

e.en: Don't be {daft} — wear a coat in this cold weather.
e.zh: 别傻了,这么冷的天要穿件外套。

e.en: It sounds like a {daft} idea, but it actually works.
e.zh: 这听起来像个蠢主意,但其实真的管用。

e.en: In Australian slang, calling someone a {dag} can be affectionate.
e.zh: 在澳大利亚俚语中,叫别人土包子可以是亲昵的。

e.en: He's a bit of a {dag}, but everyone loves him anyway.
e.zh: 他有点土气,但大家依然都喜欢他。

e.en: The Ford plant in {Dagenham} once employed thousands of workers.
e.zh: 达格南的福特工厂曾经雇用数千名工人。

e.en: She grew up in {Dagenham}, just east of central London.
e.zh: 她在伦敦市中心以东的达格南长大。

e.en: The museum displays a jeweled {dagger} from the sixteenth century.
e.zh: 博物馆展出一把十六世纪的镶宝石匕首。

e.en: She shot him a look like a {dagger} across the room.
e.zh: 她隔着房间向他投去如匕首般锐利的眼神。

e.en: Lower the {daggerboard} before you sail into deeper water.
e.zh: 驶入更深水域前,先把中插板放下来。

e.en: The small dinghy uses a {daggerboard} instead of a fixed keel.
e.zh: 这种小帆船用中插板代替固定龙骨。

dago.t: n. 南欧佬（蔑称，冒犯语）

e.en: The word {dago} is an offensive slur and should never be used.
e.zh: dago 这个词是带有侮辱性的蔑称,绝不应使用。

e.en: Older novels sometimes contain the slur {dago}, reflecting their era's prejudice.
e.zh: 旧小说中有时出现 dago 这种蔑称,反映了那个年代的偏见。

daguerreotype.t: n. 银版照相法；银版照片

e.en: The museum owns a rare {daguerreotype} of Abraham Lincoln.
e.zh: 博物馆收藏着一张罕见的林肯银版照片。

e.en: Each {daguerreotype} required several minutes of perfectly still posing.
e.zh: 每张银版照片都需要好几分钟一动不动地摆姿势。

e.en: The traveling {daguerreotypist} set up a studio in every small town.
e.zh: 那位巡回银版摄影师在每个小镇都开设工作室。

e.en: As a young {daguerreotypist}, he photographed soldiers heading off to war.
e.zh: 年轻时身为银版摄影师,他为出征的士兵拍照。

dah.t: n. 摩尔斯电码中的长音

e.en: In Morse code, a {dah} is the long signal between dots.
e.zh: 在摩尔斯电码中,长音 dah 介于短音点之间。

e.en: The operator tapped out a quick dit-{dah} pattern on the key.
e.zh: 报务员在电键上快速敲出一串短长音的信号。

dahl.t: n. 印度豆糊；达尔（姓氏）

e.en: Roald {Dahl} wrote some of the most beloved children's books ever.
e.zh: 罗尔德·达尔写出了一些最受喜爱的儿童读物。

e.en: We had warm {dahl} with rice for dinner last night.
e.zh: 昨晚我们晚餐吃了热腾腾的扁豆糊配米饭。

e.en: A bright red {dahlia} bloomed in the corner of the garden.
e.zh: 花园角落里盛开着一朵鲜红的大丽花。

e.en: She arranged a bouquet of {dahlia} blossoms for the table.
e.zh: 她为桌上插了一束大丽花。

dahomean.t:
adj. 达荷美的
n. 达荷美人

e.en: The exhibit features ancient {Dahomean} bronzes and ceremonial masks.
e.zh: 展览展出古代达荷美的青铜器和礼仪面具。

e.en: Her grandmother shared {Dahomean} folktales every summer evening.
e.zh: 她外婆每个夏夜都讲达荷美的民间故事。

daihatsu.t: n. 大发（日本汽车品牌）

e.en: My cousin drives a tiny {Daihatsu} around the narrow city streets.
e.zh: 我表弟开着一辆小巧的大发车在狭窄街道穿行。

e.en: The {Daihatsu} brand is best known for its compact kei cars.
e.zh: 大发品牌以其小巧的轻型车而闻名。

e.en: Grate fresh {daikon} over the grilled fish for extra flavor.
e.zh: 在烤鱼上磨些新鲜白萝卜泥能增添风味。

e.en: Korean stews often include sliced {daikon} simmered until tender.
e.zh: 韩式炖菜常加入切片白萝卜炖至软烂。

e.en: The Irish {Dáil} debated the new housing bill all afternoon.
e.zh: 爱尔兰国会下院整个下午都在辩论新的住房法案。

e.en: She was elected to the {Dáil} for the first time last year.
e.zh: 她去年首次当选爱尔兰下议院议员。

dailiness.t: n. 日常性；每日的特性

e.en: The poem captures the quiet {dailiness} of small-town life.
e.zh: 这首诗捕捉了小镇生活宁静的日常感。

e.en: There's a comforting {dailiness} to brewing morning coffee together.
e.zh: 一起煮晨间咖啡有种令人安心的日常感。

daily.t:
adj. 每日的
adv. 每天地

e.en: I check my email {daily} before starting any other work.
e.zh: 我每天先查邮件再开始其他工作。

e.en: The local {daily} ran a front-page story about the flood.
e.zh: 当地日报头版刊登了关于洪水的报道。

e.en: The royal family arrived in a polished black {Daimler} limousine.
e.zh: 皇室成员乘坐一辆锃亮的黑色戴姆勒豪华轿车抵达。

e.en: He restored a vintage {Daimler} from the 1930s in his garage.
e.zh: 他在车库里修复了一辆 1930 年代的老式戴姆勒。

e.en: She {daintily} picked up the teacup with two fingers.
e.zh: 她用两根手指优雅地端起茶杯。

e.en: The cat stepped {daintily} across the wet kitchen floor.
e.zh: 猫优雅地踮着脚走过湿漉漉的厨房地板。

dainty.t: adj. 精致的；娇小可爱的

e.en: She wore a {dainty} silver bracelet on her wrist.
e.zh: 她手腕上戴着一只精致的银手镯。

e.en: The bakery sells {dainty} little cakes perfect for afternoon tea.
e.zh: 这家面包店卖适合下午茶的精致小蛋糕。

e.en: She ordered a strawberry {daiquiri} at the beach bar.
e.zh: 她在海滩酒吧点了一杯草莓代基里酒。

e.en: The classic {daiquiri} mixes rum, lime juice, and sugar.
e.zh: 经典的代基里酒混合了朗姆酒、青柠汁和糖。

dairies.t: n. dairy 的复数；乳品店、奶牛场

e.en: Several local {dairies} supply milk to the entire region.
e.zh: 几家当地奶牛场为整个地区供应牛奶。

e.en: Small family {dairies} are struggling against larger industrial farms.
e.zh: 小型家庭奶牛场在与大型工业化农场的竞争中举步维艰。

dairy.t:
n. 乳制品；奶牛场
adj. 乳制品的

e.en: I avoid {dairy} because it upsets my stomach.
e.zh: 我不吃乳制品,因为它会让我胃不舒服。

e.en: The {dairy} farm offers tours of its milking parlor every Saturday.
e.zh: 这家奶牛场每周六提供挤奶车间的参观活动。

dairying.t: n. 乳制品业；奶牛养殖业

e.en: The valley's economy has depended on {dairying} for over a century.
e.zh: 这个山谷的经济一个多世纪以来都依赖乳品业。

e.en: Modern {dairying} relies on automated milking systems and careful breeding.
e.zh: 现代乳业依靠自动挤奶系统和精心育种。

e.en: The young {dairymaid} woke before dawn to milk the cows.
e.zh: 年轻的挤奶女工天不亮就起床给奶牛挤奶。

e.en: In old paintings, a {dairymaid} often appears holding a pail.
e.zh: 在旧画作中,挤奶女工常常提着木桶出现。

e.en: The {dairyman} delivered fresh milk to our doorstep every morning.
e.zh: 送奶工每天早上把新鲜牛奶送到我们家门口。

e.en: As a {dairyman}, he knew each of his cows by name.
e.zh: 作为一名乳品工人,他能叫出每头奶牛的名字。

e.en: The speaker stepped onto the {dais} and adjusted the microphone.
e.zh: 演讲者走上讲台并调整了麦克风。

e.en: Award winners gathered on the {dais} for the final photograph.
e.zh: 获奖者们聚在台上拍最后的合影。

e.en: The meadow was covered in white {daisies} all summer long.
e.zh: 整个夏天草地上都开满了白色的雏菊。

e.en: She wove {daisies} into a crown for her little sister.
e.zh: 她把雏菊编成花冠送给妹妹。

e.en: A single {daisy} grew through the crack in the sidewalk.
e.zh: 一朵雏菊从人行道的裂缝中钻出来。

e.en: She picked a {daisy} and tucked it behind her ear.
e.zh: 她摘了一朵雏菊别在耳后。

e.en: The garden bordered with {daisylike} flowers in pale pink.
e.zh: 花园边缘种着一圈淡粉色、形似雏菊的花。

e.en: Sunflowers have a {daisylike} shape but are much larger.
e.zh: 向日葵形状像雏菊,但要大得多。

daiwa.t: n. 大和（日本品牌/公司名）

e.en: He bought a new {Daiwa} reel for his fishing trip.
e.zh: 他为这次钓鱼之行买了一只新的大和渔轮。

e.en: Anglers often praise {Daiwa} rods for their light, sturdy build.
e.zh: 垂钓者常称赞大和鱼竿轻便而结实。

dakar.t: n. 达喀尔（塞内加尔首都）

e.en: We flew into {Dakar} for the start of the West African tour.
e.zh: 我们飞抵达喀尔,开始西非之旅。

e.en: The famous {Dakar} rally now actually takes place in Saudi Arabia.
e.zh: 著名的达喀尔拉力赛如今其实在沙特阿拉伯举行。

dakota.t: n. 达科他（美国州名/族名）

e.en: My family drove across {Dakota} on a long summer road trip.
e.zh: 我们一家在漫长的暑期公路旅行中开车穿越了达科他。

e.en: The {Dakota} people have lived on these plains for centuries.
e.zh: 达科他族人在这片平原上生活了几个世纪。

e.en: I cooked spicy {dal} with rice and naan for dinner.
e.zh: 我煮了香辣扁豆糊配米饭和印度烤饼当晚餐。

e.en: Indian households often serve {dal} as a daily staple dish.
e.zh: 印度家庭常把扁豆糊作为日常主菜。

e.en: We stopped overnight in {Dalby} on the way to Brisbane.
e.zh: 我们在去布里斯班的路上在达尔比过了一夜。

e.en: The town of {Dalby} sits on Queensland's western downs.
e.zh: 达尔比镇坐落在昆士兰州西部丘陵地带。

e.en: The narrow {dale} stretched between two steep grassy hills.
e.zh: 狭长的山谷夹在两座陡峭的青草山之间。

e.en: Sheep grazed peacefully in the green {dale} below the village.
e.zh: 羊群在村庄下方青翠的山谷里安静地吃草。

dalek.t: n. 戴立克（《神秘博士》中的外星人）

e.en: The kids dressed up as a {Dalek} for the convention.
e.zh: 孩子们打扮成戴立克参加这次大会。

e.en: Few villains are as iconic as the {Dalek} from Doctor Who.
e.zh: 很少有反派像《神秘博士》里的戴立克那样具有标志性。

dalgety.t: n. 达尔盖蒂（姓氏/公司名）

e.en: Old farmers still remember when {Dalgety} ran the local wool sales.
e.zh: 老农们还记得达尔格提公司经营当地羊毛拍卖的年代。

e.en: The historic firm {Dalgety} once dominated Australian rural commerce.
e.zh: 老牌公司达尔格提曾在澳大利亚乡村贸易中占主导地位。

e.en: Salvador {Dalí} painted melting clocks in his most famous work.
e.zh: 萨尔瓦多·达利在他最著名的画作中画了融化的钟表。

e.en: The museum's {Dalí} retrospective drew record crowds last weekend.
e.zh: 博物馆的达利回顾展上周末吸引了创纪录的观众。

e.en: {Dalian} is a coastal city in northeast China.
e.zh: 大连是中国东北的一座沿海城市。

e.en: We flew to {Dalian} for a seafood weekend.
e.zh: 我们飞去大连过了个海鲜周末。

dalkeith.t: n. 达尔基思（苏格兰地名）

e.en: {Dalkeith} is a small town near Edinburgh, Scotland.
e.zh: 达尔基思是苏格兰爱丁堡附近的一个小镇。

e.en: She grew up in {Dalkeith} and later moved to London.
e.zh: 她在达尔基思长大,后来搬去了伦敦。

e.en: The conference will be held in {Dallas} next March.
e.zh: 会议将于明年三月在达拉斯举行。

e.en: {Dallas} has a thriving tech and startup scene.
e.zh: 达拉斯的科技和创业氛围十分活跃。

dalliance.t: n. 调情；嬉戏；浪费时间

e.en: His brief {dalliance} with politics ended in scandal.
e.zh: 他短暂涉足政界,最终以丑闻收场。

e.en: The novel describes a summer {dalliance} between two strangers.
e.zh: 小说讲述了两个陌生人之间一段夏日的暧昧。

e.en: Don't {dally} — the train leaves in ten minutes.
e.zh: 别磨蹭了,火车十分钟后就开。

e.en: He likes to {dally} with risky investments.
e.zh: 他喜欢在高风险投资上玩玩花样。

dalmatia.t: n. 达尔马提亚（克罗地亚地区）

e.en: {Dalmatia} stretches along Croatia's stunning Adriatic coast.
e.zh: 达尔马提亚沿着克罗地亚迷人的亚得里亚海岸延伸。

e.en: We sailed around {Dalmatia} for two glorious weeks.
e.zh: 我们在达尔马提亚周边航行了愉快的两周。

e.en: Her {Dalmatian} puppy chewed through three pairs of shoes.
e.zh: 她的斑点狗幼犬咬坏了三双鞋。

e.en: The film features over a hundred {Dalmatian} dogs.
e.zh: 这部电影里出现了一百多只斑点狗。

e.en: Professor {Dalrymple} published a new book on geology.
e.zh: 达尔林普尔教授出版了一本新的地质学著作。

e.en: The {Dalrymple} family has lived here for generations.
e.zh: 达尔林普尔家族已在此居住了几代人。

dalston.t: n. 达尔斯顿（伦敦地区）

e.en: {Dalston} has become one of east London's trendiest neighborhoods.
e.zh: 达尔斯顿已成为东伦敦最潮的街区之一。

e.en: We met for coffee at a café in {Dalston}.
e.zh: 我们在达尔斯顿的一家咖啡馆见面喝咖啡。

dalton.t: n. 道尔顿（姓氏/原子质量单位）

e.en: John {Dalton} proposed the modern atomic theory of matter.
e.zh: 约翰·道尔顿提出了现代物质原子理论。

e.en: Mass is often measured in {daltons} in biochemistry.
e.zh: 在生物化学中,质量常以道尔顿为单位测量。

dam.t:
n. 水坝；堤坝
v. 筑坝拦水

e.en: The {dam} provides electricity to the entire region.
e.zh: 这座水坝为整个地区供电。

e.en: Beavers build a {dam} across the small stream.
e.zh: 海狸在小溪上筑起了一道堤坝。

e.en: The {dama} gazelle is critically endangered in the Sahara.
e.zh: 达马瞪羚在撒哈拉地区已极度濒危。

e.en: In Spanish, {dama} simply means lady or queen.
e.zh: 在西班牙语中,dama 就是女士或王后的意思。

damage.t:
n. 损害；损失
v. 损坏

e.en: The storm caused serious {damage} to coastal homes.
e.zh: 风暴对沿海房屋造成了严重破坏。

e.en: Smoking can {damage} your lungs over time.
e.zh: 长期吸烟会损害你的肺部。

e.en: The package arrived {damaged} after a rough delivery.
e.zh: 包裹经过一路颠簸,送到时已经破损。

e.en: Her reputation was badly {damaged} by the rumors.
e.zh: 她的名声因这些谣言受到严重损害。

damages.t:
n. 损害赔偿金
v. damage 的第三人称单数

e.en: The court awarded her ten thousand dollars in {damages}.
e.zh: 法院判给她一万美元的损害赔偿金。

e.en: Constant criticism slowly {damages} a child's confidence.
e.zh: 持续的批评会慢慢损伤孩子的自信心。

damaging.t: adj. 有害的；造成损害的

e.en: The leaked emails were extremely {damaging} to his campaign.
e.zh: 泄露的邮件对他的竞选造成了极大的损害。

e.en: UV rays are {damaging} to unprotected skin.
e.zh: 紫外线对未做防护的皮肤有伤害。

e.en: The report spoke {damagingly} of the company's safety record.
e.zh: 报告对公司的安全记录作出了极为不利的评价。

e.en: He commented {damagingly} on his rival's character.
e.zh: 他对对手的人品作出了具有杀伤力的评论。

damar.t: n. 达玛树脂（用于清漆）

e.en: Artists mix {damar} resin into varnish for oil paintings.
e.zh: 画家会把达玛树脂调入清漆,用于油画。

e.en: The {damar} tree grows in Southeast Asian rainforests.
e.zh: 达玛树生长在东南亚的雨林中。

damascene.t:
adj. 大马士革的
v. 在金属上镶嵌花纹

e.en: He had a {Damascene} conversion to vegetarianism overnight.
e.zh: 他在一夜之间幡然醒悟,改吃素食。

e.en: The blade features intricate {damascene} patterns on the steel.
e.zh: 刀身的钢面上有精美的大马士革花纹。

e.en: He switched shampoos to deal with his {dandruff}.
e.zh: 他换了洗发水来对付头皮屑。

e.en: Stress can sometimes make {dandruff} worse.
e.zh: 压力有时会让头皮屑加重。

dandy.t:
n. 注重穿着的男子
adj. 极好的

e.en: Everything is just {dandy} on our end.
e.zh: 我们这边一切都好得很。

e.en: He dressed like a Victorian {dandy} for the costume party.
e.zh: 他在化装舞会上打扮成维多利亚时代的纨绔子弟。

dandyish.t: adj. 爱打扮的；纨绔作派的

e.en: He has a slightly {dandyish} taste in waistcoats.
e.zh: 他对马甲有一种略显纨绔的品味。

e.en: The actor wore a {dandyish} velvet jacket on stage.
e.zh: 那位演员在台上穿着一件花花公子风格的天鹅绒外套。

e.en: My neighbor is a {Dane} who moved here for work.
e.zh: 我邻居是个为了工作搬来这里的丹麦人。

e.en: Their Great {Dane} is taller than most children.
e.zh: 他们家的大丹犬比大多数小孩还高。

dang.t: int. 该死（damn 的委婉说法）

e.en: {Dang}, I forgot my keys again.
e.zh: 该死,我又忘带钥匙了。

e.en: That was a {dang} good burger.
e.zh: 那汉堡真他妈好吃。

danged.t: adj. 该死的（damned 的委婉说法）

e.en: The {danged} printer is jammed again.
e.zh: 那台该死的打印机又卡纸了。

e.en: I can't find my {danged} phone anywhere.
e.zh: 我那破手机到处都找不到。

e.en: Hikers were warned of {danger} on the icy trail.
e.zh: 徒步者被警告冰封小径上有危险。

e.en: There's no {danger} of the project being canceled.
e.zh: 这个项目不会有被取消的危险。

e.en: Rodney {Dangerfield} was famous for his self-deprecating jokes.
e.zh: 罗德尼·丹杰菲尔德以自嘲式的笑话闻名。

e.en: The town of {Dangerfield} hosts an annual rodeo.
e.zh: 丹杰菲尔德镇每年举办牛仔竞技赛。

e.en: Driving in this fog is genuinely {dangerous}.
e.zh: 在这种大雾里开车确实很危险。

e.en: He has a {dangerous} habit of skipping his medication.
e.zh: 他有不按时吃药这个危险的习惯。

e.en: The cliff edge was {dangerously} close to the trail.
e.zh: 悬崖边离小径近得令人担忧。

e.en: Our supplies are running {dangerously} low.
e.zh: 我们的物资正减少到危险的水平。

e.en: Judges weigh the {dangerousness} of an offender before sentencing.
e.zh: 法官在量刑前会评估犯人的危险性。

e.en: The report assessed the {dangerousness} of the chemical leak.
e.zh: 报告评估了这次化学品泄漏的危险程度。

e.en: Don't {dangle} your feet over the edge of the platform.
e.zh: 别把脚悬在站台边上晃。

e.en: Recruiters often {dangle} signing bonuses to attract talent.
e.zh: 招聘者常常用签约奖金来吸引人才。

e.en: A loose wire was {dangling} from the ceiling.
e.zh: 一根松动的电线从天花板上垂下来。

e.en: The contract still has a few {dangling} legal questions.
e.zh: 这份合同还有几个悬而未决的法律问题。

e.en: She wore long {dangly} earrings to the gala.
e.zh: 她戴着长长的垂坠耳环去参加晚会。

e.en: The cat keeps batting at the {dangly} string.
e.zh: 那只猫一直在拍打那根晃来晃去的绳子。

danish.t:
adj. 丹麦的
n. 丹麦语；丹麦酥

e.en: I grabbed a cherry {Danish} with my coffee.
e.zh: 我配着咖啡拿了一个樱桃丹麦酥。

e.en: {Danish} design is known for clean, minimal lines.
e.zh: 丹麦设计以简洁极简的线条闻名。

e.en: The basement smelled cold and {dank}.
e.zh: 地下室闻起来又冷又潮湿。

e.en: Teens kept sharing {dank} memes in the group chat.
e.zh: 那些青少年一直在群里分享各种沙雕梗图。

e.en: The cave's {dankness} made our clothes cling uncomfortably.
e.zh: 洞里的潮湿阴冷让衣服黏在身上很不舒服。

e.en: You could smell the {dankness} as soon as the door opened.
e.zh: 门一开就能闻到那股阴冷潮湿的味道。

e.en: Two {Dans} work on my engineering team, which gets confusing.
e.zh: 我们工程团队里有两个叫 Dan 的,挺容易搞混。

e.en: The dojo lists all senior {dans} on the wall.
e.zh: 道场把所有高段位选手的名字都列在墙上。

e.en: {Dante}'s Inferno is still taught in literature classes.
e.zh: 但丁的《地狱篇》至今仍在文学课上讲授。

e.en: My friend {Dante} is studying architecture in Milan.
e.zh: 我朋友但丁正在米兰学建筑。

e.en: We took a riverboat down the {Danube} to Budapest.
e.zh: 我们坐游船沿多瑙河前往布达佩斯。

e.en: The {Danube} flows through ten European countries.
e.zh: 多瑙河流经十个欧洲国家。

e.en: The museum showcases {Danubian} folk costumes and crafts.
e.zh: 博物馆展出多瑙河流域的民族服饰和手工艺品。

e.en: Many {Danubian} cities thrived on river trade.
e.zh: 许多多瑙河沿岸城市靠河运贸易兴起。

danzig.t: n. 但泽（格但斯克旧称）

e.en: The free city of {Danzig} existed between the world wars.
e.zh: 自由市但泽存在于两次世界大战之间。

e.en: My grandfather was born in {Danzig} before 1939.
e.zh: 我祖父在 1939 年前出生于但泽。

daphne.t: n. 女子名；瑞香属植物

e.en: {Daphne} bushes filled the garden with sweet fragrance.
e.zh: 瑞香丛让花园弥漫着甜香。

e.en: In the myth, {Daphne} was transformed into a laurel tree.
e.zh: 神话里,达芙妮被变成了一棵月桂树。

dapper.t: adj. (男子) 衣着整洁的；精干的

e.en: He looked {dapper} in his navy three-piece suit.
e.zh: 他穿着深蓝三件套西装,显得十分潇洒。

e.en: The waiter was unfailingly polite and {dapper}.
e.zh: 那位服务员始终彬彬有礼、衣着考究。

dapple.t:
n. 斑点
v. 使有斑点

e.en: Sunlight began to {dapple} the forest floor.
e.zh: 阳光开始在林地上投下斑驳的光影。

e.en: Shadows {dapple} the courtyard each afternoon.
e.zh: 每天下午,影子都会在院子里投下斑驳光点。

e.en: We hiked through {dappled} sunlight under the oaks.
e.zh: 我们在橡树下斑驳的阳光中徒步。

e.en: The pony had a {dappled} gray coat.
e.zh: 那匹小马有一身花斑灰毛。

e.en: She joined the {DAR} after tracing her family tree.
e.zh: 她在追溯家谱后加入了美国革命之女会。

e.en: Our flight to {Dar} es Salaam leaves at midnight.
e.zh: 我们飞往达累斯萨拉姆的航班午夜起飞。

e.en: We rented a cabin near Lake {Dardanelle} for the weekend.
e.zh: 我们在达达内尔湖附近租了一间小屋过周末。

e.en: {Dardanelle} is a small town along the Arkansas River.
e.zh: 达达内尔是阿肯色河畔的一个小镇。

dare.t:
v. 敢于；胆敢
n. 挑战

e.en: I {dare} you to try the spiciest ramen.
e.zh: 我打赌你不敢挑战最辣的那碗拉面。

e.en: Few people {dare} to question the boss directly.
e.zh: 很少有人敢直接质疑老板。

e.en: She {dared} to ask for a higher salary.
e.zh: 她鼓起勇气要求更高的薪水。

e.en: No one {dared} interrupt the speaker.
e.zh: 没人敢打断那位演讲者。

e.en: The {daredevil} jumped his motorcycle over fifteen cars.
e.zh: 那位特技狂人骑摩托车飞越了十五辆车。

e.en: Her little brother is a total {daredevil} on a skateboard.
e.zh: 她弟弟玩滑板时简直是个亡命之徒。

dares.t: v. dare 的第三人称单数

e.en: Nobody {dares} challenge the champion in this gym.
e.zh: 在这家健身房里没人敢挑战那位冠军。

e.en: At sleepovers we used to swap silly {dares}.
e.zh: 在睡衣派对上我们以前会互相出些傻乎乎的大冒险。

e.en: I {daresay} the meeting will run over an hour.
e.zh: 我猜会议会开过一个小时。

e.en: You'll enjoy the trip, I {daresay}.
e.zh: 我敢说你会喜欢这次旅行的。

daring.t:
adj. 大胆的；勇敢的
n. 胆量

e.en: Her {daring} escape from the burning building made headlines.
e.zh: 她从燃烧大楼里的大胆逃生上了头条。

e.en: That was a {daring} choice of outfit for the gala.
e.zh: 那身礼服在晚会上算是相当大胆的选择。

e.en: She {daringly} jumped off the cliff into the sea.
e.zh: 她大胆地从悬崖上跳进了大海。

e.en: He {daringly} questioned the CEO during the all-hands meeting.
e.zh: 他在全员大会上大胆地质疑了首席执行官。

darjeeling.t: n. 大吉岭（印度地名；红茶）

e.en: I ordered a pot of {darjeeling} at the tea shop.
e.zh: 我在茶馆点了一壶大吉岭红茶。

e.en: The hills of {darjeeling} are famous for their tea plantations.
e.zh: 大吉岭的山区以茶园闻名。

damascus.t: n. 大马士革（叙利亚首都）

e.en: {Damascus} is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities.
e.zh: 大马士革是世界上持续有人居住的最古老城市之一。

e.en: The chef uses a {Damascus} steel knife in the kitchen.
e.zh: 厨师在厨房里使用一把大马士革钢刀。

damask.t:
n. 锦缎；花缎
adj. 花缎般的

e.en: The dining table was covered with a white {damask} cloth.
e.zh: 餐桌上铺着一块白色的锦缎桌布。

e.en: Her dress was made of deep red {damask}.
e.zh: 她的礼服是用深红色锦缎做的。

dame.t: n. 贵妇；女士（英国爵位称号）

e.en: {Dame} Judi Dench delivered another stunning performance.
e.zh: 朱迪·丹奇女爵士再次奉献了精彩的表演。

e.en: In old films, the hero always rescues the {dame}.
e.zh: 在老电影里,英雄总是要拯救那位女士。

daminozide.t: n. 比久（一种植物生长调节剂）

e.en: {Daminozide} was once sprayed on apples to control growth.
e.zh: 丁酰肼曾被喷洒在苹果上以控制其生长。

e.en: Regulators banned {daminozide} after health concerns emerged.
e.zh: 出于健康担忧,监管机构禁用了丁酰肼。

e.en: Jean-Claude Van {Damme} starred in many action movies.
e.zh: 让-克洛德·范达美主演过许多动作片。

e.en: {Damme} is a charming little town near Bruges.
e.zh: 达默是布鲁日附近一座迷人的小镇。

dammed.t: v. 筑坝拦截（dam 的过去式）

e.en: Engineers {dammed} the river to create a reservoir.
e.zh: 工程师们筑坝拦河,建起了一座水库。

e.en: Fallen logs {dammed} the small forest stream.
e.zh: 倒下的树干堵住了林中的小溪。

damming.t: v. 筑坝；拦截（dam 的现在分词）

e.en: {Damming} the river displaced thousands of villagers.
e.zh: 在这条河上筑坝迫使数千名村民搬迁。

e.en: Environmentalists oppose {damming} the last wild canyon.
e.zh: 环保人士反对在最后一段原始峡谷上修建大坝。

dammit.t: int. 该死；见鬼（damn it 的缩写）

e.en: {Dammit}, I left my keys in the car again.
e.zh: 该死,我又把钥匙落在车里了。

e.en: Just answer the question, {dammit}!
e.zh: 你就回答问题啊,真是的!

damn.t:
int. 该死
v. 谴责；诅咒

e.en: That was a {damn} good movie — I cried twice.
e.zh: 那部电影真他妈好看,我哭了两次。

e.en: {Damn}, the printer is jammed again.
e.zh: 该死,打印机又卡纸了。

e.en: He told a {damnable} lie that ruined her career.
e.zh: 他撒了一个该死的谎,毁掉了她的事业。

e.en: The weather has been {damnable} all week.
e.zh: 这一整个星期的天气都糟透了。

e.en: The instructions were {damnably} hard to follow.
e.zh: 那些说明书难懂得让人发指。

e.en: He arrived {damnably} late to his own wedding.
e.zh: 他迟到得离谱,连自己婚礼都赶不上。

damnation.t:
n. 天谴；下地狱
int. 该死

e.en: The preacher warned of eternal {damnation} for sinners.
e.zh: 传教士警告罪人将受永恒的诅咒。

e.en: "{Damnation}!" he muttered when the lights went out.
e.zh: 灯灭了的时候,他低声咒骂了一句。

damndest.t:
n. 最大努力
adj. 最离奇的

e.en: I tried my {damndest} to finish before the deadline.
e.zh: 我拼了老命想在截止日期前完成。

e.en: He's the {damndest} kid I've ever taught.
e.zh: 他是我教过最让人哭笑不得的孩子。

damned.t:
adj. 该死的；可恶的
adv. 非常

e.en: That's a {damned} good question, actually.
e.zh: 说真的,这问题问得太到位了。

e.en: He felt {damned} for betraying his closest friend.
e.zh: 他因为背叛了最亲密的朋友而感到自己罪无可恕。

damnedest.t:
n. 拼尽全力
adj. 最离奇的

e.en: She did her {damnedest} to fix the broken system.
e.zh: 她拼尽全力去修复那个崩坏的系统。

e.en: That's the {damnedest} story I've heard all year.
e.zh: 那是我今年听过最离谱的故事。

damning.t: adj. 确凿不利的（证据）；招致谴责的

e.en: The report contained {damning} evidence of widespread fraud.
e.zh: 报告中包含了大规模欺诈的确凿证据。

e.en: Her silence was the most {damning} response of all.
e.zh: 她的沉默是最致命的回应。

damocles.t: n. 达摩克利斯（希腊神话人物）

e.en: The lawsuit hung over him like a sword of {Damocles}.
e.zh: 那场官司像达摩克利斯之剑悬在他头顶。

e.en: Looming layoffs were a {Damocles} threat to the team.
e.zh: 迫在眉睫的裁员对团队来说是悬顶之灾。

damp.t:
adj. 潮湿的
n. 湿气

e.en: Wipe the screen with a {damp} cloth, not water.
e.zh: 用湿布擦屏幕,别直接用水。

e.en: The basement smells of {damp} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后地下室有一股潮湿的味道。

damped.t:
adj. 阻尼的；减震的
v. 抑制（damp 的过去式）

e.en: Rubber feet {damped} the vibration from the washing machine.
e.zh: 橡胶脚垫减弱了洗衣机传来的震动。

e.en: The bad reviews {damped} her enthusiasm for the project.
e.zh: 那些差评浇灭了她对项目的热情。

e.en: Don't let one bad review {dampen} your motivation.
e.zh: 别让一条差评浇灭你的动力。

e.en: {Dampen} the sponge before wiping the counter.
e.zh: 先把海绵弄湿再擦台面。

dampened.t: v. 抑制；减弱；弄湿（dampen 的过去式）

e.en: The rain {dampened} our plans for a picnic.
e.zh: 这场雨让我们的野餐计划泡了汤。

e.en: She {dampened} a towel and pressed it to her forehead.
e.zh: 她把毛巾打湿,贴在额头上。

e.en: His sour mood was a real {dampener} on the party.
e.zh: 他臭着脸,把整个派对的气氛都搞砸了。

e.en: The shock {dampener} reduces vibration in the engine.
e.zh: 减震器能减少发动机的震动。

dampening.t: v. 抑制；减弱（dampen 的现在分词）

e.en: Rising prices are {dampening} consumer spending this quarter.
e.zh: 物价上涨正在抑制本季度的消费支出。

e.en: She's {dampening} the cloth before ironing the shirt.
e.zh: 她在熨衬衫前先把布弄湿。

dampens.t: v. 抑制；减弱（dampen 的第三人称单数）

e.en: Heavy traffic {dampens} the appeal of city living.
e.zh: 严重的交通拥堵削弱了住在城里的吸引力。

e.en: The thick carpet {dampens} every footstep upstairs.
e.zh: 厚厚的地毯吸掉了楼上每一声脚步。

damper.t: n. 减震器；阻尼器；扫兴的人或事

e.en: The bad news put a {damper} on our celebration.
e.zh: 这个坏消息给我们的庆祝活动浇了一盆冷水。

e.en: Close the {damper} when the fireplace isn't in use.
e.zh: 壁炉不用时记得把风门关上。

damping.t: n. 阻尼；衰减（物理术语）

e.en: Good {damping} keeps the speakers from sounding muddy.
e.zh: 良好的阻尼能让音箱不至于发声浑浊。

e.en: The suspension's {damping} smooths out bumpy roads.
e.zh: 悬挂系统的阻尼能让颠簸路面变得平稳。

e.en: Her hair clung {damply} to her forehead after the run.
e.zh: 跑完步后,她的头发湿漉漉地贴在额头上。

e.en: The towels hung {damply} on the bathroom rail.
e.zh: 毛巾湿乎乎地搭在浴室的挂杆上。

e.en: The {dampness} in the basement is ruining the boxes.
e.zh: 地下室的潮气把那些纸箱都泡坏了。

e.en: He could feel the {dampness} of the morning grass.
e.zh: 他能感觉到清晨草地上的潮湿。

dams.t:
n. 水坝（复数）
v. 筑坝（第三人称单数）

e.en: China has built thousands of {dams} along its rivers.
e.zh: 中国在江河上修建了数以千计的水坝。

e.en: Aging {dams} pose a serious safety risk downstream.
e.zh: 年久失修的水坝对下游构成严重的安全隐患。

damsel.t: n. 少女；年轻姑娘（文学用语）

e.en: The knight rescued the {damsel} from the tower.
e.zh: 骑士把少女从高塔中救了出来。

e.en: She refuses to play the helpless {damsel} in distress.
e.zh: 她拒绝去演那种束手无策的落难少女。

e.en: The bright blue {damselfish} darted around the coral reef.
e.zh: 那条鲜蓝色的雀鲷在珊瑚礁间穿梭。

e.en: {Damselfish} fiercely defend their territory from larger fish.
e.zh: 雀鲷会凶猛地从大鱼手里守住自己的地盘。

e.en: A blue {damselfly} hovered above the pond's edge.
e.zh: 一只蓝色的豆娘在池塘边盘旋。

e.en: The {damselfly} is slimmer than a typical dragonfly.
e.zh: 豆娘比一般的蜻蜓要纤细。

e.en: Grandma made {damson} jam every autumn.
e.zh: 奶奶每年秋天都会做西洋李子酱。

e.en: The {damson} tree out back is finally bearing fruit.
e.zh: 后院那棵西洋李子树终于结果了。

dan.t: n. 段位（武术、围棋）；丹（男子名）

e.en: He earned his black belt third {dan} last year.
e.zh: 他去年获得了黑带三段。

e.en: She trains hard to reach the next {dan} ranking.
e.zh: 她刻苦训练以达到下一段位。

e.en: {Dana} hosted the team meeting this morning.
e.zh: 达娜今早主持了团队会议。

e.en: My cousin {Dana} just moved to Berlin.
e.zh: 我表姐达娜刚搬到柏林。

e.en: {Danby} makes affordable compact refrigerators for small apartments.
e.zh: Danby 生产适合小公寓的实惠紧凑型冰箱。

e.en: The painter Thomas {Danby} was known for romantic landscapes.
e.zh: 画家托马斯·丹比以浪漫风景画闻名。

dance.t:
v. 跳舞
n. 舞蹈；舞会

e.en: They love to {dance} at weddings.
e.zh: 他们喜欢在婚礼上跳舞。

e.en: The school is hosting a winter {dance} on Friday.
e.zh: 学校周五要举办冬季舞会。

e.en: The new album has a really {danceable} beat.
e.zh: 这张新专辑的节奏非常适合跳舞。

e.en: Her latest single is catchy and {danceable}.
e.zh: 她的新单曲朗朗上口又适合跳舞。

danced.t: v. 跳舞（dance 的过去式）

e.en: We {danced} all night at the wedding.
e.zh: 我们在婚礼上跳了一整晚的舞。

e.en: Sunlight {danced} on the surface of the lake.
e.zh: 阳光在湖面上闪烁跳跃。

e.en: She trained for years to become a professional {dancer}.
e.zh: 她苦练多年才成为职业舞者。

e.en: The lead {dancer} sprained her ankle before the show.
e.zh: 首席舞者在演出前扭伤了脚踝。

e.en: The {dancers} took a bow after the final number.
e.zh: 舞者们在最后一支舞结束后鞠躬致谢。

e.en: Backup {dancers} rehearsed the routine for hours.
e.zh: 伴舞们排练了好几个小时这套动作。

dances.t:
n. 舞蹈（复数）
v. 跳舞（第三人称单数）

e.en: He {dances} salsa every Thursday night.
e.zh: 他每周四晚上去跳莎莎舞。

e.en: The festival features traditional folk {dances} from many regions.
e.zh: 这个节日上演来自各地的传统民间舞蹈。

dancing.t:
n. 跳舞；舞蹈
v. 跳舞（现在分词）

e.en: They went out {dancing} to celebrate her promotion.
e.zh: 他们出去跳舞庆祝她升职。

e.en: The kids were {dancing} around the living room.
e.zh: 孩子们在客厅里手舞足蹈。

e.en: A single {dandelion} pushed through the cracked sidewalk.
e.zh: 一朵蒲公英从开裂的人行道里钻了出来。

e.en: She blew on the {dandelion} and made a wish.
e.zh: 她对着蒲公英吹了一口气并许了愿。

e.en: The lawn was covered in yellow {dandelions}.
e.zh: 草坪上铺满了黄色的蒲公英。

e.en: Bees love feeding on early spring {dandelions}.
e.zh: 蜜蜂喜欢采食初春的蒲公英。

e.en: My allergies act up around cat {dander}.
e.zh: 我一接触猫皮屑就过敏发作。

e.en: That comment really got his {dander} up.
e.zh: 那句评论彻底惹恼了他。

dandle.t: v. 上下轻摇（小孩）；逗弄

e.en: Grandpa likes to {dandle} the baby on his knee.
e.zh: 爷爷喜欢把宝宝放在膝上颠着哄。

e.en: She would {dandle} her niece while singing softly.
e.zh: 她一边轻声唱歌,一边逗弄着小侄女。

dark.t:
adj. 黑暗的；深色的
n. 黑暗

e.en: The room was too {dark} to read without a lamp.
e.zh: 房间太暗了,没有台灯就看不了书。

e.en: She wore a {dark} blue dress to the interview.
e.zh: 她穿了一条深蓝色连衣裙去面试。

e.en: Storm clouds began to {darken} the afternoon sky.
e.zh: 乌云开始让午后的天空变暗。

e.en: His mood seemed to {darken} after reading the email.
e.zh: 他读完那封邮件后心情似乎变得阴沉。

e.en: They sat quietly in the {darkened} cinema.
e.zh: 他们安静地坐在昏暗的电影院里。

e.en: Her expression {darkened} when she heard the news.
e.zh: 听到这个消息时她的表情阴沉了下来。

darkening.t:
n. 变暗
v. 使变暗（进行式）

e.en: We hurried home under the {darkening} sky.
e.zh: 我们在渐渐变暗的天空下匆匆赶回家。

e.en: A {darkening} mood spread through the team after the layoffs.
e.zh: 裁员之后,团队里弥漫着越来越压抑的情绪。

darkie.t: n. 对深肤色者的蔑称（冒犯）

e.en: The word {darkie} is an offensive slur and should never be used.
e.zh: "darkie"这个词是带有冒犯性的蔑称,绝不该使用。

e.en: Old films sometimes contain the term {darkie}, which is now considered racist.
e.zh: 老电影里有时会出现"darkie"一词,如今被视为种族歧视用语。

e.en: She painted the wall a {darkish} shade of green.
e.zh: 她把墙刷成了偏深的绿色。

e.en: The sky turned {darkish} just before the rain started.
e.zh: 下雨前天空变得有些昏暗。

e.en: They walked home through the {darkling} woods.
e.zh: 他们穿过渐渐昏暗的树林走回家。

e.en: A {darkling} beetle scurried across the desert sand.
e.zh: 一只拟步甲虫在沙漠沙地上飞快爬过。

e.en: He smiled {darkly} at the suggestion.
e.zh: 他对那个提议阴沉地笑了笑。

e.en: The novel hints {darkly} at a coming disaster.
e.zh: 这部小说阴郁地暗示着一场即将到来的灾难。

e.en: The power went out and we were left in {darkness}.
e.zh: 停电了,我们陷入一片黑暗之中。

e.en: Her poems explore the {darkness} of grief and loss.
e.zh: 她的诗探索着悲伤与失去的阴暗面。

e.en: He still develops his film in a home {darkroom}.
e.zh: 他至今仍在家里的暗房里冲洗胶卷。

e.en: The photography club built a small {darkroom} in the basement.
e.zh: 摄影社在地下室搭建了一间小暗房。

e.en: Most universities have closed their {darkrooms} since digital cameras took over.
e.zh: 自从数码相机普及后,大多数大学都关闭了暗房。

e.en: The two {darkrooms} on campus are still used by film enthusiasts.
e.zh: 校园里的两间暗房仍被胶片爱好者使用。

darks.t: n. 深色衣物（洗衣分类）

e.en: Wash the {darks} separately to avoid color bleeding.
e.zh: 深色衣物要分开洗,以免染色。

e.en: She sorted the laundry into whites and {darks}.
e.zh: 她把衣服分成浅色和深色两堆。

darky.t: n. 对深肤色者的蔑称（冒犯）

e.en: The term {darky} is a racist slur from older texts.
e.zh: "darky"是旧文本中带有种族歧视意味的蔑称。

e.en: Editors now flag the word {darky} as offensive in reprints.
e.zh: 编辑在再版时会把"darky"一词标记为冒犯性用语。

darling.t:
n. 亲爱的人；宝贝
adj. 可爱的

e.en: Good night, {darling}, sleep well.
e.zh: 晚安,亲爱的,好好睡。

e.en: The young actress quickly became Hollywood's new {darling}.
e.zh: 这位年轻女演员很快成了好莱坞的新宠。

e.en: Tech {darlings} can fall out of favor surprisingly fast.
e.zh: 科技界的宠儿可能会出乎意料地迅速失宠。

e.en: She greeted her grandchildren as her little {darlings}.
e.zh: 她把孙辈们称作她的小宝贝。

e.en: The train from London stopped briefly in {darlington}.
e.zh: 从伦敦开出的火车在达灵顿短暂停靠。

e.en: He grew up in {darlington}, a town in northern England.
e.zh: 他在英格兰北部的小城达灵顿长大。

darmstadt.t: n. 达姆施塔特（德国城市）

e.en: The conference will be held in {darmstadt} this autumn.
e.zh: 这次会议今年秋天将在达姆施塔特举行。

e.en: She studied chemistry at a university in {darmstadt}.
e.zh: 她在达姆施塔特的一所大学学习化学。

darn.t:
int. 该死（damn 委婉说法）
v. 织补

e.en: It's {darn} cold outside this morning.
e.zh: 今早外面冷得要命。

e.en: My grandmother taught me how to {darn} socks.
e.zh: 我祖母教过我怎么织补袜子。

darndest.t: n. 使出最大努力；极不寻常之事

e.en: Kids say the {darndest} things at the dinner table.
e.zh: 孩子们在饭桌上经常说出最让人意想不到的话。

e.en: He tried his {darndest} to finish the marathon.
e.zh: 他拼尽全力想跑完整个马拉松。

e.en: That's a {darned} good question, actually.
e.zh: 说真的,那是个非常好的问题。

e.en: She wore {darned} socks because she hated throwing things away.
e.zh: 她穿着补过的袜子,因为她讨厌丢弃东西。

darnedest.t: n. 最大的努力；极为罕见的事

e.en: He did his {darnedest} to fix the leaking pipe.
e.zh: 他使出浑身解数想修好那根漏水的管子。

e.en: My toddler does the {darnedest} things when no one's watching.
e.zh: 我家小娃在没人看着时会做出最离奇的事。

e.en: Mary, Queen of Scots married Lord {darnley} in 1565.
e.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽于1565年嫁给了达恩利勋爵。

e.en: The history book devotes a chapter to {darnley}'s mysterious death.
e.zh: 那本历史书用一章讲述了达恩利离奇的死亡。

dart.t:
n. 飞镖
v. 猛冲

e.en: She threw a {dart} and hit the bullseye.
e.zh: 她掷出一枚飞镖,正中靶心。

e.en: A squirrel began to {dart} across the road.
e.zh: 一只松鼠开始飞快地穿过马路。

e.en: They hung a {dartboard} on the back wall of the pub.
e.zh: 他们在酒吧后墙上挂了一块飞镖盘。

e.en: My uncle keeps a {dartboard} in his garage.
e.zh: 我叔叔的车库里放着一块飞镖靶。

e.en: A {darter} bird dove into the lake to catch fish.
e.zh: 一只蛇鹈扎进湖里捕鱼。

e.en: The kid is a real {darter}, weaving through defenders easily.
e.zh: 那孩子真是个穿梭高手,轻松绕过防守球员。

dartford.t: n. 达特福德（英国地名）

e.en: The {dartford} crossing connects Kent and Essex via the Thames.
e.zh: 达特福德大桥跨越泰晤士河,连接肯特郡和埃塞克斯郡。

e.en: Traffic on the {dartford} bridge was heavy this morning.
e.zh: 今早达特福德大桥上的车流量很大。

e.en: Small fish were {darting} around the coral reef.
e.zh: 小鱼在珊瑚礁周围飞快地穿梭。

e.en: Her eyes kept {darting} toward the door.
e.zh: 她的目光不停地往门口瞟。

dartmoor.t: n. 达特穆尔（英国地名）

e.en: We hiked across {dartmoor} despite the heavy fog.
e.zh: 尽管浓雾弥漫,我们仍徒步穿越了达特穆尔。

e.en: Wild ponies still roam freely on {dartmoor}.
e.zh: 野生小马至今仍在达特穆尔自由漫步。

dartmouth.t: n. 达特茅斯（地名/大学）

e.en: He was accepted to {dartmouth} College last spring.
e.zh: 他去年春天被达特茅斯学院录取了。

e.en: The harbor town of {dartmouth} is popular with sailors.
e.zh: 达特茅斯这座港口小镇深受水手们喜爱。

e.en: The mill town of {darwen} sits in Lancashire.
e.zh: 工业小镇达温坐落于兰开夏郡。

e.en: She drove through {darwen} on her way to Blackburn.
e.zh: 她在去布莱克本的路上经过了达温。

e.en: {darwin} proposed the theory of natural selection.
e.zh: 达尔文提出了自然选择理论。

e.en: We flew to {darwin} to start our trip across northern Australia.
e.zh: 我们飞到达尔文市,开始了穿越澳洲北部的旅行。

e.en: The startup world feels like a {darwinian} struggle for survival.
e.zh: 创业圈感觉就像一场达尔文式的生存竞争。

e.en: She gave a lecture on {darwinian} evolution to her biology class.
e.zh: 她给生物课的学生讲了一节达尔文进化论。

e.en: Social {darwinism} was used to justify many harmful policies.
e.zh: 社会达尔文主义曾被用来为许多有害政策辩护。

e.en: The textbook explains {darwinism} in simple, accessible language.
e.zh: 这本教材用浅显易懂的语言讲解达尔文主义。

darwinist.t: n. 达尔文进化论信奉者

e.en: He calls himself a strict {darwinist} when discussing evolution.
e.zh: 谈到进化时,他自称是严格的达尔文主义者。

e.en: The biologist defended a {darwinist} view of species change.
e.zh: 那位生物学家捍卫了达尔文主义的物种演变观点。

e.en: The German article {das} is used with neuter nouns.
e.zh: 德语冠词"das"用于中性名词。

e.en: Beginners often confuse der, die, and {das} in German class.
e.zh: 初学者在德语课上常常分不清der、die和das。

dash.t:
v. 猛冲
n. 短跑；破折号

e.en: I had to make a {dash} for the bus this morning.
e.zh: 今早我不得不冲过去赶公交车。

e.en: Add a {dash} of salt to the soup before serving.
e.zh: 上桌前往汤里加一点盐。

dashboard.t: n. 仪表盘；（软件）控制台

e.en: The admin {dashboard} shows real-time user activity.
e.zh: 管理后台仪表盘显示实时用户活动。

e.en: A warning light flashed on the car's {dashboard}.
e.zh: 汽车仪表盘上闪起一盏警示灯。

dashed.t:
adj. 虚线的
v. 猛冲（过去式）

e.en: She {dashed} out the door without her umbrella.
e.zh: 她没拿伞就冲出了门。

e.en: His hopes were {dashed} when he received the rejection letter.
e.zh: 收到拒信时,他的希望破灭了。

e.en: He works as a {dasher} for a food delivery app.
e.zh: 他在一家外卖app当配送员。

e.en: The old butter churn had a wooden {dasher} inside.
e.zh: 那台老式黄油搅拌器里有一根木质搅拌杆。

dashes.t:
n. 破折号（复数）
v. 猛冲（三单）

e.en: The recipe calls for two {dashes} of hot sauce.
e.zh: 这个食谱需要加两小撮辣酱。

e.en: She uses em {dashes} a lot in her writing.
e.zh: 她在写作中经常使用长破折号。

e.en: Most Japanese soups start with a base of {dashi}.
e.zh: 大多数日式汤都以出汁作为汤底。

e.en: He simmered kombu and bonito flakes to make {dashi}.
e.zh: 他用昆布和鲣鱼花熬制出汁。

dashiki.t: n. 西非传统宽松彩色上衣

e.en: He wore a colorful {dashiki} to the cultural festival.
e.zh: 他穿着一件色彩鲜艳的达西基去参加文化节。

e.en: The {dashiki} originated in West Africa and remains popular today.
e.zh: 达西基衫起源于西非,如今仍很受欢迎。

e.en: He looked absolutely {dashing} in his new suit.
e.zh: 他穿着新西装看上去真是潇洒帅气。

e.en: The {dashing} young officer caught everyone's attention.
e.zh: 那位英俊潇洒的年轻军官吸引了所有人的目光。

dashingly.t: adv. 潇洒地；精神抖擞地

e.en: He dressed {dashingly} for the gala dinner.
e.zh: 他为这场晚宴穿得风度翩翩。

e.en: The actor {dashingly} entered the room and bowed.
e.zh: 那位演员潇洒地走进房间,鞠了一躬。

e.en: In old novels, the villain is often called a {dastard}.
e.zh: 在老小说里,反派常被称作懦夫恶棍。

e.en: He cursed the {dastard} who had betrayed his family.
e.zh: 他咒骂那个出卖了他家人的卑鄙小人。

e.en: The villain hatched a {dastardly} plan to steal the crown.
e.zh: 那个反派策划了一个卑鄙的计划想偷走王冠。

e.en: Newspapers condemned the {dastardly} attack on civilians.
e.zh: 报纸纷纷谴责这场针对平民的卑劣袭击。

e.en: In casual texts, people sometimes write "{dat}" instead of "that".
e.zh: 在随意的短信里,人们有时会把"that"写成"dat"。

e.en: He laughed and said, "Check {dat} out!"
e.zh: 他笑着说:"瞧瞧那个!"

e.en: The app collects {data} on how users interact with each feature.
e.zh: 该应用会收集用户与各功能交互的数据。

e.en: We need more {data} before drawing any conclusions.
e.zh: 在下结论之前我们需要更多数据。

e.en: The hospital keeps a {databank} of donor blood types.
e.zh: 这家医院保存着一个献血者血型数据库。

e.en: Researchers uploaded the survey results to a public {databank}.
e.zh: 研究人员将调查结果上传到公共资料库。

e.en: Our customer {database} now has over a million entries.
e.zh: 我们的客户数据库现在已有超过一百万条记录。

e.en: The app crashed because the {database} connection timed out.
e.zh: 由于数据库连接超时,应用程序崩溃了。

e.en: Modern apps often query several {databases} at once.
e.zh: 现代应用程序经常同时查询多个数据库。

e.en: She manages all the company's internal {databases}.
e.zh: 她负责管理公司所有的内部数据库。

e.en: The pottery is {datable} to the early Bronze Age.
e.zh: 这些陶器可以追溯到青铜时代早期。

e.en: Few of the manuscripts are precisely {datable}.
e.zh: 这些手稿中很少能被精确断代。

e.en: The diagram shows the {dataflow} between the two services.
e.zh: 该图展示了两个服务之间的数据流。

e.en: Engineers redesigned the {dataflow} to reduce latency.
e.zh: 工程师重新设计了数据流以降低延迟。

dataquest.t: n. 数据查询（专有名词）

e.en: She finished a Python course on {dataquest} last month.
e.zh: 她上个月在 Dataquest 上完成了一门 Python 课程。

e.en: Many beginners learn SQL through {dataquest} tutorials.
e.zh: 许多初学者通过 Dataquest 教程学习 SQL。

e.en: The model was trained on a massive image {dataset}.
e.zh: 该模型是在一个庞大的图像数据集上训练的。

e.en: Please clean the {dataset} before running the analysis.
e.zh: 请在运行分析之前清理数据集。

date.t:
n. 日期；约会
v. 约会；注明日期

e.en: What's the {date} of your flight to Tokyo?
e.zh: 你飞往东京的航班是哪一天?

e.en: They went on their first {date} at a coffee shop.
e.zh: 他们的第一次约会是在一家咖啡馆。

e.en: She jotted the meeting into her leather {datebook}.
e.zh: 她把会议记在了她的皮面记事簿里。

e.en: Old-school managers still prefer a paper {datebook}.
e.zh: 老派的经理人仍然偏爱纸质日程本。

dated.t: adj. 过时的；标有日期的

e.en: His haircut looks a bit {dated} these days.
e.zh: 他的发型如今看起来有点过时了。

e.en: The letter was {dated} March third, 1972.
e.zh: 那封信的日期是1972年3月3日。

e.en: The poem expresses a {dateless} love that never fades.
e.zh: 这首诗表达了一种永恒不褪的爱。

e.en: He spent another {dateless} Saturday playing video games.
e.zh: 他又度过了一个没有约会的周六,只顾着打游戏。

dateline.t: n. 国际日期变更线；新闻电头

e.en: The article carried a {dateline} from Beirut.
e.zh: 这篇报道标有发自贝鲁特的电讯日期行。

e.en: Travelers cross the international {dateline} flying to Hawaii.
e.zh: 飞往夏威夷的旅客会跨越国际日期变更线。

dates.t:
n. 日期（复数）
v. 约会（第三人称）

e.en: Please check the {dates} on the milk before drinking it.
e.zh: 喝牛奶之前请查看一下保质期。

e.en: This temple {dates} back to the twelfth century.
e.zh: 这座寺庙可以追溯到十二世纪。

dating.t:
n. 约会；交往
v. 约会中

e.en: She's been {dating} him for almost two years.
e.zh: 她和他交往快两年了。

e.en: Online {dating} apps have changed how people meet.
e.zh: 网络交友软件改变了人们相识的方式。

e.en: Carbon {datings} confirmed the bones were prehistoric.
e.zh: 碳定年结果证实这些骨头属于史前时代。

e.en: Recent {datings} pushed the artifact's age back centuries.
e.zh: 最近的年代测定将这件文物的年代往前推了几个世纪。

datsun.t: n. 达特桑（日本汽车品牌）

e.en: His first car was a rusty old {datsun} hatchback.
e.zh: 他的第一辆车是一辆生锈的老款达特桑掀背车。

e.en: Collectors still hunt for the classic {datsun} 240Z.
e.zh: 收藏家们仍在寻找经典的达特桑 240Z。

datum.t: n. 数据（data 的单数）；基准

e.en: Each {datum} in the survey was checked for accuracy.
e.zh: 调查中的每一个数据点都经过了准确性核查。

e.en: The map uses a different geographic {datum}.
e.zh: 这张地图使用了不同的地理基准。

daub.t:
v. 涂抹；乱画
n. 涂料；拙劣画作

e.en: He used a brush to {daub} paint on the canvas.
e.zh: 他用刷子在画布上涂抹颜料。

e.en: Vandals had {daub}ed graffiti across the wall.
e.zh: 破坏者在墙上涂抹了涂鸦。

e.en: Bingo players each brought their own ink {dauber}.
e.zh: 宾果游戏的玩家都各自带了一支墨水点珠笔。

e.en: The amateur {dauber} sold paintings at the weekend market.
e.zh: 那位业余画匠在周末市场上卖画。

e.en: Critics dismissed the painter as a clumsy {daubster}.
e.zh: 评论家把这位画家贬为笨拙的拙劣画匠。

e.en: Even a humble {daubster} can find joy in painting.
e.zh: 即便是个不入流的画匠也能从绘画中找到乐趣。

e.en: Their {daughter} just started kindergarten this fall.
e.zh: 他们的女儿今年秋天刚上幼儿园。

e.en: My {daughter} loves drawing dinosaurs in her notebook.
e.zh: 我女儿喜欢在笔记本上画恐龙。

e.en: She gets along wonderfully with her {daughter-in-law}.
e.zh: 她和儿媳相处得非常融洽。

e.en: His {daughter-in-law} brought homemade soup to the hospital.
e.zh: 他的儿媳带了自制的汤到医院。

e.en: Both his {daughter-in-laws} attended the family reunion.
e.zh: 他的两个儿媳都参加了家庭聚会。

e.en: Grandma cooks dumplings whenever her {daughter-in-laws} visit.
e.zh: 每当儿媳们来访,奶奶都会包饺子。

e.en: He has three {daughters} and one son.
e.zh: 他有三个女儿和一个儿子。

e.en: The two {daughters} look almost like twins.
e.zh: 两个女儿看起来几乎像双胞胎。

e.en: The size of the project did not {daunt} her at all.
e.zh: 项目的规模丝毫没有让她感到畏惧。

e.en: Difficult exams rarely {daunt} a well-prepared student.
e.zh: 准备充分的学生很少会被难考的考试吓倒。

e.en: She was {daunted} by the long climb ahead.
e.zh: 前方漫长的攀登让她心生畏惧。

e.en: He felt {daunted} when he saw the huge audience.
e.zh: 看到庞大的观众群,他感到有些胆怯。

daunting.t: adj. 令人畏惧的；艰巨的

e.en: Learning a new language can be a {daunting} task.
e.zh: 学习一门新语言可能是一项艰巨的任务。

e.en: The hike up the cliff looked truly {daunting}.
e.zh: 攀登那悬崖的徒步看起来真的令人却步。

e.en: The mountain rose {dauntingly} above the small village.
e.zh: 那座山令人生畏地耸立在小村庄之上。

e.en: The exam was {dauntingly} long but fair.
e.zh: 考试长得让人发怵,但题目还算公平。

e.en: The {dauntless} firefighters rushed into the burning building.
e.zh: 无畏的消防员冲进了燃烧的大楼。

e.en: She showed a {dauntless} spirit throughout the long expedition.
e.zh: 在漫长的探险中她始终展现出无畏的精神。

daunts.t: v. 吓倒（第三人称单数）

e.en: Public speaking still {daunts} even experienced executives.
e.zh: 即使是经验丰富的高管也仍会被公开演讲吓到。

e.en: Nothing {daunts} her when she sets a goal.
e.zh: 一旦她定下目标,什么也吓不倒她。

e.en: The young {dauphin} was crowned king of France.
e.zh: 年轻的太子被加冕为法国国王。

e.en: Historians still debate the fate of the lost {dauphin}.
e.zh: 历史学家至今仍在争论那位失踪太子的命运。

e.en: Grandma fell asleep on the velvet {davenport}.
e.zh: 奶奶在天鹅绒大沙发上睡着了。

e.en: They moved the old {davenport} into the guest room.
e.zh: 他们把那张旧大沙发搬进了客房。

daventry.t: n. 达文特里（英国地名）

e.en: We stopped for lunch on the way through {daventry}.
e.zh: 途经达文特里时,我们停下来吃了午饭。

e.en: {Daventry} is a small market town in England.
e.zh: 达文特里是英格兰的一个小集镇。

e.en: {David} won the science fair with his volcano model.
e.zh: 大卫凭借他的火山模型赢得了科学博览会。

e.en: Michelangelo's statue of {David} stands in Florence.
e.zh: 米开朗基罗的大卫雕像矗立在佛罗伦萨。

davidic.t: adj. 大卫王的；与大卫有关的

e.en: Many psalms reflect the {davidic} tradition of worship.
e.zh: 许多诗篇反映了大卫王传统的崇拜方式。

e.en: The prophecy promised a future king of {davidic} descent.
e.zh: 该预言承诺将出现一位大卫王后裔的未来君王。

davit.t: n. 吊艇架；起重小吊杆

e.en: Crew members lowered the lifeboat using the ship's {davit}.
e.zh: 船员们用船上的吊艇柱放下救生艇。

e.en: Each lifeboat hung neatly from its own {davit}.
e.zh: 每艘救生艇都整齐地挂在各自的吊艇柱上。

davos.t: n. 达沃斯（瑞士小镇，世界经济论坛举办地）

e.en: World leaders gather every January in {davos}, Switzerland.
e.zh: 世界领导人每年一月都会齐聚瑞士达沃斯。

e.en: The {davos} forum focused on climate change this year.
e.zh: 今年的达沃斯论坛聚焦于气候变化议题。

davy.t:
n. 戴维（男子名）
n. 矿工安全灯

e.en: Sailors said the wreck went down to {davy} Jones's locker.
e.zh: 水手们说那艘失事的船沉入了海底坟墓。

e.en: Old {davy} lamps once protected coal miners from explosions.
e.zh: 老式戴维灯曾保护煤矿工人免受爆炸伤害。

e.en: A {daw} perched on the church steeple at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时一只穴鸦栖在教堂尖顶上。

e.en: The noisy {daw} stole shiny coins from the windowsill.
e.zh: 那只吵闹的穴鸦从窗台上偷走了亮闪闪的硬币。

dawa.t: n. 达瓦（藏语人名，意为月亮）

e.en: They gave him a herbal {dawa} for his cough.
e.zh: 他们给他开了一剂草药来治咳嗽。

e.en: In Swahili, {dawa} simply means medicine or remedy.
e.zh: 在斯瓦希里语中,dawa 就是药或疗法的意思。

dawdle.t: v. 磨蹭；闲荡；虚度时光

e.en: Don't {dawdle} or we'll miss the train.
e.zh: 别磨蹭了,不然我们要赶不上火车了。

e.en: The kids tend to {dawdle} on the way to school.
e.zh: 孩子们上学路上总是爱拖拖拉拉。

dawn.t:
n. 黎明；拂晓
v. 破晓；开始显现

e.en: We hiked to the summit just before {dawn}.
e.zh: 我们在黎明前不久徒步到达了山顶。

e.en: The {dawn} of the internet changed everything.
e.zh: 互联网时代的来临改变了一切。

dawning.t:
n. 破晓；开端
adj. 初现的

e.en: A new era of clean energy is finally {dawning}.
e.zh: 清洁能源的新时代终于即将到来。

e.en: Realization was slowly {dawning} on her face.
e.zh: 她脸上慢慢露出了恍然大悟的神情。

dawns.t:
n. 黎明（复数）
v. 破晓（第三人称单数）

e.en: It suddenly {dawns} on me that I forgot my keys.
e.zh: 我突然意识到我忘带钥匙了。

e.en: Cold winter {dawns} were her favorite time to write.
e.zh: 寒冷的冬日清晨是她最喜欢写作的时光。

e.en: What a beautiful {day} for a picnic in the park.
e.zh: 今天天气真好,适合去公园野餐。

e.en: I drink coffee three times a {day}.
e.zh: 我每天喝三次咖啡。

e.en: The sunny corner held a small wicker {daybed}.
e.zh: 阳光充足的角落里放着一张小藤编卧榻。

e.en: Guests can sleep on the {daybed} in the office.
e.zh: 客人可以睡在书房里的卧榻上。

daybook.t: n. 日记账；流水账；日志

e.en: The shopkeeper recorded every sale in a leather {daybook}.
e.zh: 店主把每笔销售都记在皮面流水账本里。

e.en: She keeps a personal {daybook} of her morning thoughts.
e.zh: 她保留着一本记录晨间思绪的私人日志。

e.en: The fishermen set sail at {daybreak}.
e.zh: 渔民们在破晓时分起航出海。

e.en: By {daybreak}, the storm had finally passed.
e.zh: 到天亮时,暴风雨终于过去了。

e.en: We dropped our toddler off at {daycare} this morning.
e.zh: 今天早上我们把小孩送到了日托中心。

e.en: Affordable {daycare} is hard to find in the city.
e.zh: 在城里很难找到价格实惠的日托。

daydream.t:
n. 白日梦
v. 做白日梦；空想

e.en: She tends to {daydream} during long meetings.
e.zh: 她在冗长的会议中容易走神发白日梦。

e.en: Owning a beach house was always his {daydream}.
e.zh: 拥有一栋海边别墅一直是他的白日梦。

e.en: She {daydreamed} about traveling the world during class.
e.zh: 上课时她幻想着环游世界。

e.en: He {daydreamed} of becoming a famous chef someday.
e.zh: 他幻想有朝一日成为一名著名厨师。

daydreaming.t:
v. 做白日梦（进行时）
n. 空想

e.en: Stop {daydreaming} and finish your homework now.
e.zh: 别再发白日梦了,赶紧把作业做完。

e.en: She caught me {daydreaming} during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时她发现我在走神。

daydreams.t:
n. 白日梦（复数）
v. 做白日梦（第三人称单数）

e.en: His {daydreams} often involve winning the lottery.
e.zh: 他的白日梦经常是中彩票。

e.en: She {daydreams} about quitting her boring job.
e.zh: 她幻想着辞掉这份无聊的工作。

e.en: The room gets plenty of natural {daylight}.
e.zh: 这个房间有充足的自然光。

e.en: We should leave before {daylight} fades.
e.zh: 我们应该趁天还没黑就出发。

daylights.t: n. 魂魄（多用于 scare the daylights out of 等短语）

e.en: The horror movie scared the {daylights} out of me.
e.zh: 那部恐怖片把我吓得魂飞魄散。

e.en: He beat the living {daylights} out of the punching bag.
e.zh: 他把沙袋打得稀里哗啦。

e.en: I packed snacks and water in my {daypack}.
e.zh: 我把零食和水装进了我的日用背包。

e.en: A small {daypack} is perfect for short hikes.
e.zh: 小型日用背包很适合短途徒步。

dayroom.t: n. (宿舍、医院等的) 日间活动室

e.en: Patients gathered in the {dayroom} to watch television.
e.zh: 病人们聚在日间活动室看电视。

e.en: The hospital {dayroom} has board games and books.
e.zh: 医院的日间活动室里有棋盘游戏和书籍。

days.t:
n. 日子；天（day 的复数）
adv. 白天（每天）

e.en: It's been three {days} since I saw her.
e.zh: 我已经三天没见到她了。

e.en: Those were the {days} when life felt simple.
e.zh: 那些日子里生活感觉很简单。

e.en: I prefer studying during the {daytime}.
e.zh: 我更喜欢在白天学习。

e.en: This café only serves food in the {daytime}.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆只在白天供应食物。

e.en: Summer {daytimes} can stretch past nine in the evening.
e.zh: 夏天的白天可以延续到晚上九点之后。

e.en: Winter {daytimes} feel painfully short up north.
e.zh: 在北方,冬天的白天短得让人难受。

dayton.t: n. 代顿（美国俄亥俄州城市）

e.en: She grew up in {Dayton}, Ohio.
e.zh: 她在俄亥俄州的代顿长大。

e.en: The Wright brothers worked on their plane in {Dayton}.
e.zh: 莱特兄弟在代顿研制他们的飞机。

daytona.t: n. 代托纳（美国佛州城市，以赛车闻名）

e.en: He watched the race at {Daytona} last weekend.
e.zh: 他上周末在代托纳观看了比赛。

e.en: The family vacationed on {Daytona} Beach.
e.zh: 全家在代托纳海滩度假。

daze.t:
n. 恍惚；茫然
v. 使茫然；使眩晕

e.en: She walked around in a {daze} after the news.
e.zh: 听到消息后她茫然地四处走动。

e.en: The bright lights left him in a {daze}.
e.zh: 刺眼的灯光让他头晕目眩。

dazed.t: adj. 茫然的；恍惚的；眩晕的

e.en: He looked {dazed} after hitting his head.
e.zh: 撞到头后他看起来神志不清。

e.en: The {dazed} survivors wandered through the rubble.
e.zh: 茫然的幸存者在废墟中徘徊。

e.en: She stared {dazedly} at the broken phone screen.
e.zh: 她茫然地盯着破裂的手机屏幕。

e.en: He stumbled {dazedly} out of the burning building.
e.zh: 他茫然地踉跄着走出着火的大楼。

dazes.t:
v. 使茫然（第三人称单数）
n. 恍惚（复数）

e.en: The sudden flash {dazes} drivers at night.
e.zh: 夜间突然的闪光会让司机眼花。

e.en: Her beauty {dazes} everyone she meets.
e.zh: 她的美貌让每个见到她的人都目眩神迷。

dazzle.t:
v. 使目眩；使惊艳
n. 耀眼的光；魅力

e.en: The fireworks {dazzle} the crowd every year.
e.zh: 烟花每年都让观众目眩神迷。

e.en: She tried to {dazzle} the judges with her performance.
e.zh: 她试图用表演让评委们惊艳。

dazzled.t:
adj. 目眩的；被惊艳的
v. 使目眩（过去式）

e.en: The audience was {dazzled} by her singing voice.
e.zh: 观众被她的歌声深深折服。

e.en: Tourists are {dazzled} by the city's neon lights.
e.zh: 游客被城市的霓虹灯照得眼花缭乱。

dazzler.t: n. 耀眼之物；极出众的人

e.en: That new sports car is a real {dazzler}.
e.zh: 那辆新跑车真是惊艳夺目。

e.en: Her engagement ring is an absolute {dazzler}.
e.zh: 她的订婚戒指简直闪耀夺目。

dazzles.t: v. 使目眩；惊艳（第三人称单数）

e.en: The sunset {dazzles} hikers on the mountaintop.
e.zh: 山顶的日落让徒步者目眩神迷。

e.en: Her smile {dazzles} everyone in the room.
e.zh: 她的微笑让房间里的每个人都为之倾倒。

dazzling.t: adj. 耀眼的；令人惊艳的

e.en: She gave a {dazzling} performance on stage.
e.zh: 她在舞台上表演得令人惊艳。

e.en: The diamond necklace was simply {dazzling}.
e.zh: 那条钻石项链简直光彩夺目。

dazzlingly.t: adv. 耀眼地；令人惊艳地

e.en: The chandelier shone {dazzlingly} above the ballroom.
e.zh: 吊灯在舞厅上方耀眼地闪烁着。

e.en: She was {dazzlingly} beautiful in her wedding gown.
e.zh: 她穿着婚纱美得令人目眩神迷。

dbase.t: n. dBase（早期数据库管理系统）

e.en: Old companies still maintain legacy {dBase} files.
e.zh: 老牌公司仍在维护遗留的 dBase 文件。

e.en: He learned programming using {dBase} in the eighties.
e.zh: 他在八十年代用 dBase 学的编程。

dbms.t: n. 数据库管理系统（database management system）

e.en: Choosing the right {DBMS} affects your app's performance.
e.zh: 选择合适的数据库管理系统会影响应用性能。

e.en: PostgreSQL is a popular open-source {DBMS}.
e.zh: PostgreSQL 是一种流行的开源数据库管理系统。

dce.t: n. 数据电路终端设备（data circuit-terminating equipment）

e.en: The router connects to the {DCE} via a serial cable.
e.zh: 路由器通过串行电缆连接到数据通信设备。

e.en: Older telecom networks rely on {DCE} equipment.
e.zh: 较旧的电信网络依赖 DCE 设备。

dcf.t: n. 现金流折现（discounted cash flow）

e.en: Analysts use {DCF} to estimate a company's intrinsic value.
e.zh: 分析师用现金流折现法估算公司的内在价值。

e.en: The {DCF} model assumes steady future cash flows.
e.zh: DCF 模型假设未来现金流稳定。

dci.t: n. 重症监护（depending on context，常指 digital cinema initiatives 或潜水减压病）

e.en: The {DCI} led the murder investigation team.
e.zh: 那位高级警探领导着凶杀案调查小组。

e.en: Cinemas use {DCI} standards for digital projection.
e.zh: 电影院采用 DCI 标准进行数字放映。

deanery.t: n. 教长的职位或辖区

e.en: The old {deanery} has been converted into a charming guesthouse.
e.zh: 那座古老的教长宅邸已被改造成一家迷人的客栈。

e.en: The bishop visited every parish in the {deanery}.
e.zh: 主教走访了教区内的每一个堂区。

dear.t:
adj. 亲爱的；昂贵的
n. 亲爱的人

e.en: My {dear} friend, I miss you so much.
e.zh: 我亲爱的朋友，我好想你。

e.en: Fresh seafood is quite {dear} in this city.
e.zh: 在这座城市里，新鲜海鲜挺贵的。

e.en: Don't worry, {dearie}, the bus will come soon.
e.zh: 亲爱的，别担心，公交车马上就来。

e.en: The old shopkeeper called every customer {dearie}.
e.zh: 那位上了年纪的店主把每位顾客都叫作宝贝。

dearly.t: adv. 深切地；付出高昂代价地

e.en: She loved her grandmother {dearly}.
e.zh: 她深深地爱着自己的奶奶。

e.en: He paid {dearly} for ignoring the warnings.
e.zh: 他因为无视警告而付出了惨重代价。

dears.t: n. dear 的复数；对他人的昵称

e.en: Come along, {dears}, dinner is ready.
e.zh: 来吧，亲爱的们，晚饭做好啦。

e.en: The grandmother smiled at her two little {dears}.
e.zh: 奶奶对着她那两个小宝贝微微一笑。

e.en: There is a {dearth} of qualified nurses in rural areas.
e.zh: 农村地区严重缺乏合格的护士。

e.en: The film suffers from a {dearth} of original ideas.
e.zh: 这部电影最大的问题就是缺乏新意。

deary.t: n. 亲爱的（昵称，同 dearie）

e.en: Oh {deary} me, I forgot my keys again.
e.zh: 哎呀我的天，我又忘了带钥匙。

e.en: Sit down, {deary}, and I'll fetch you some tea.
e.zh: 坐下吧亲爱的，我去给你倒杯茶。

e.en: His sudden {death} shocked the entire community.
e.zh: 他的突然离世震惊了整个社区。

e.en: The novel explores themes of love and {death}.
e.zh: 这部小说探讨了爱与死亡的主题。

deathbed.t: n. 临终之床；临终时刻

e.en: On his {deathbed}, he finally apologized to his son.
e.zh: 在临终前，他终于向儿子道了歉。

e.en: She made a {deathbed} promise to care for her sister.
e.zh: 她在病榻前许下承诺，要照顾自己的妹妹。

e.en: The scandal dealt a {deathblow} to his political career.
e.zh: 那桩丑闻给他的政治生涯带来了致命一击。

e.en: Rising costs delivered the {deathblow} to the small bookstore.
e.zh: 成本上涨给这家小书店带来了致命的打击。

e.en: Shakespeare wrote {deathless} lines that we still quote today.
e.zh: 莎士比亚写下了至今仍被人传诵的不朽诗句。

e.en: The hero achieved {deathless} fame after the great battle.
e.zh: 那位英雄在那场大战之后获得了不朽的声名。

deathly.t:
adj. 死一般的
adv. 极其地

e.en: Her face turned {deathly} pale at the news.
e.zh: 听到这个消息，她的脸色变得惨白如死。

e.en: A {deathly} silence fell over the courtroom.
e.zh: 法庭上陷入一片死寂。

deaths.t: n. death 的复数，死亡人数

e.en: The pandemic caused thousands of {deaths} worldwide.
e.zh: 那场大流行在全球造成了数以千计的死亡。

e.en: Traffic {deaths} have dropped sharply since the new law.
e.zh: 新法律实施后，交通死亡人数大幅下降。

deathtrap.t: n. 极度危险的场所或建筑

e.en: That old elevator is an absolute {deathtrap}.
e.zh: 那部老电梯简直就是个夺命陷阱。

e.en: The intersection became a {deathtrap} after the lights broke.
e.zh: 信号灯坏掉之后，那个路口成了一个死亡陷阱。

e.en: The family kept a quiet {deathwatch} by his bedside.
e.zh: 家人静静地守在他床边等待他离去。

e.en: Reporters began a {deathwatch} outside the hospital.
e.zh: 记者们开始在医院外守候等待消息。

e.en: We spent the weekend at a beach hotel in {Deauville}.
e.zh: 我们在多维尔的一家海滨酒店过了周末。

e.en: The {Deauville} film festival attracts stars from across America.
e.zh: 多维尔电影节吸引了来自全美各地的明星。

deb.t: n. 初进社交界的女子（debutante 缩写）

e.en: She made her {deb} appearance at the spring ball.
e.zh: 她在春季舞会上首次以社交名媛身份亮相。

e.en: My friend {Deb} just got promoted to senior engineer.
e.zh: 我朋友黛布刚刚升任高级工程师。

e.en: The product launch turned into a complete {debacle}.
e.zh: 那次产品发布最终变成了一场彻底的灾难。

e.en: The team is still recovering from last year's financial {debacle}.
e.zh: 团队仍未从去年那场财务惨败中缓过来。

e.en: The court can {debar} a lawyer for serious misconduct.
e.zh: 法院可以因严重不当行为而吊销律师执照。

e.en: New rules {debar} athletes who fail drug tests.
e.zh: 新规定禁止药检不合格的运动员参赛。

e.en: Passengers began to {debark} as soon as the gangway opened.
e.zh: 舷梯一打开，乘客就开始下船了。

e.en: We had to {debark} from the plane onto the tarmac.
e.zh: 我们不得不从飞机直接走下到停机坪上。

e.en: Cheap imitations only {debase} the brand's reputation.
e.zh: 廉价的仿制品只会损害这个品牌的声誉。

e.en: He refused to {debase} himself by begging for the job.
e.zh: 他拒绝去乞求那份工作而自降身份。

debased.t: adj. 被贬低的；品质下降的

e.en: The currency was severely {debased} during the war years.
e.zh: 战争年代里，货币的成色被大幅降低。

e.en: Critics argue that reality TV has {debased} public taste.
e.zh: 评论家认为真人秀拉低了大众的审美。

e.en: The {debasement} of the coinage led to runaway inflation.
e.zh: 货币成色的下降导致了恶性通货膨胀。

e.en: He saw the trend as a {debasement} of journalism.
e.zh: 他将这种趋势视为新闻业品质的堕落。

debatable.t: adj. 有争议的，值得商榷的

e.en: Whether the new policy will work is highly {debatable}.
e.zh: 新政策是否会奏效，还很有争议。

e.en: It's {debatable} whether the movie deserved all those awards.
e.zh: 这部电影是否当得起那么多奖项，还有待商榷。

e.en: The candidates will {debate} education reform tonight on TV.
e.zh: 今晚候选人将在电视上就教育改革展开辩论。

e.en: There is heated {debate} over the new tax law.
e.zh: 围绕这部新税法的争论非常激烈。

debated.t: v. debate 的过去式；被争论的

e.en: Lawmakers {debated} the bill for over six hours.
e.zh: 立法者就这项法案辩论了六个多小时。

e.en: The origins of the painting are still hotly {debated}.
e.zh: 这幅画的来历至今仍备受争议。

e.en: She was the strongest {debater} on her college team.
e.zh: 她是她大学辩论队里最强的辩手。

e.en: A skilled {debater} listens as carefully as he speaks.
e.zh: 一个出色的辩手听得和说得一样用心。

debates.t: n./v. debate 的复数或第三人称单数

e.en: The class often {debates} climate policy on Friday afternoons.
e.zh: 这个班经常在周五下午辩论气候政策。

e.en: Watch the presidential {debates} live on the news app.
e.zh: 在新闻应用上观看总统辩论直播。

debating.t:
v. debate 的现在分词
n. 辩论（活动）

e.en: They are still {debating} whether to launch the feature.
e.zh: 他们还在讨论是否要上线这个功能。

e.en: She joined the school {debating} club last semester.
e.zh: 她上学期加入了学校的辩论社。

debauch.t:
v. 使堕落，放纵
n. 纵欲

e.en: The novel warns against habits that {debauch} young minds.
e.zh: 这部小说警告人们不要沾染腐蚀年轻人心灵的习气。

e.en: Critics said the show would {debauch} public taste.
e.zh: 评论家说这档节目会败坏大众品味。

e.en: The emperor lived a {debauched} life of endless parties.
e.zh: 那位皇帝过着夜夜笙歌的放荡生活。

e.en: Reporters described the mansion as a {debauched} playground.
e.zh: 记者把那座豪宅形容为荒淫的游乐场。

e.en: The film depicts the {debauchery} of Roman elites.
e.zh: 这部电影描绘了罗马精英阶层的荒淫无度。

e.en: Las Vegas is often associated with weekend {debauchery}.
e.zh: 拉斯维加斯常被与周末的纵情享乐联系在一起。

e.en: In Spanish class we learned that {debe} means must.
e.zh: 在西班牙语课上,我们学到 debe 意思是“必须”。

e.en: The bank statement listed each {debe} entry in red.
e.zh: 银行对账单上每笔借方记录都用红色标出。

e.en: The company issued a ten-year {debenture} to raise funds.
e.zh: 公司发行了一张十年期债券来募集资金。

e.en: Investors prefer a secured {debenture} over common stock.
e.zh: 投资者更青睐有担保的债券而不是普通股。

e.en: Long working hours can {debilitate} even the healthiest employees.
e.zh: 长时间工作会使最健康的员工也变得虚弱。

e.en: Sanctions are designed to {debilitate} the country's economy.
e.zh: 制裁旨在削弱该国的经济。

e.en: The flu left her {debilitated} for almost two weeks.
e.zh: 那场流感让她虚弱了近两周。

e.en: Years of drought have {debilitated} the local farming industry.
e.zh: 多年干旱已削弱了当地的农业。

debilitating.t: adj. 让人虚弱的；使人衰弱的

e.en: She suffers from {debilitating} migraines several times a month.
e.zh: 她每月都会犯几次让人难以承受的偏头痛。

e.en: The lawsuit had a {debilitating} effect on the startup.
e.zh: 这场诉讼对这家初创公司造成了严重打击。

e.en: Doctors warned of gradual {debilitation} if treatment was delayed.
e.zh: 医生警告说若延误治疗会逐渐衰弱。

e.en: The report studied the {debilitation} caused by chronic stress.
e.zh: 该报告研究了长期压力造成的身体衰弱。

e.en: Researchers study the {debilitative} effects of sleep deprivation.
e.zh: 研究人员研究睡眠不足带来的削弱性影响。

e.en: The drug has surprisingly {debilitative} side effects on memory.
e.zh: 该药物对记忆有出人意料的削弱性副作用。

e.en: Old age brought a noticeable {debility} to his stride.
e.zh: 年老让他的步伐明显变得无力。

e.en: The patient recovered from his {debility} after months of therapy.
e.zh: 经过几个月的治疗,病人从虚弱中恢复过来。

debit.t:
n. 借方；扣款
v. 从账户扣款

e.en: I paid for the coffee with my {debit} card.
e.zh: 我用借记卡付了咖啡钱。

e.en: The bank will {debit} your account every month automatically.
e.zh: 银行每月会自动从你的账户扣款。

debited.t: v. debit 的过去式，已记入借方

e.en: The subscription fee was {debited} from my account today.
e.zh: 订阅费今天已从我账户扣除。

e.en: Five dollars was {debited} for the overdraft fee.
e.zh: 五美元的透支费已被扣除。

e.en: The accountant {debites} expenses to the correct ledger account.
e.zh: 会计将各项费用借记到正确的分类账户中。

e.en: Each transaction {debites} one account and credits another.
e.zh: 每笔交易都会借记一个账户并贷记另一个账户。

debiting.t: v. debit 的现在分词，记入借方

e.en: The app keeps {debiting} my card without permission.
e.zh: 这个应用一直未经允许就从我卡上扣款。

e.en: Stop {debiting} my account for the canceled subscription.
e.zh: 请停止从我账户扣取已取消订阅的费用。

debits.t: n./v. debit 的复数或第三人称单数

e.en: Check your statement for any unfamiliar {debits} this month.
e.zh: 查看本月对账单上有无陌生的扣款记录。

e.en: The ledger showed three large {debits} on Monday.
e.zh: 账本上显示周一有三笔大额借方记录。

dcm.t:
n. 数字通信模块（缩写）
(罕用)

e.en: Medical scanners save images in {DCM} format.
e.zh: 医学扫描仪将图像保存为 DCM 格式。

e.en: The radiologist opened the {DCM} file for review.
e.zh: 放射科医生打开 DCM 文件进行查阅。

dcs.t: n. 分布式控制系统（Distributed Control System）

e.en: The factory upgraded its {DCS} for better automation.
e.zh: 工厂升级了分布式控制系统以提升自动化水平。

e.en: Engineers monitor the plant through the {DCS} console.
e.zh: 工程师通过分布式控制系统的控制台监控工厂。

ddr.t: n. DDR 内存（双倍数据速率）

e.en: This laptop uses the latest {DDR} memory modules.
e.zh: 这台笔记本使用最新的 DDR 内存条。

e.en: Upgrading {DDR} RAM significantly boosted my computer's speed.
e.zh: 升级 DDR 内存大幅提升了我电脑的速度。

e.en: Many countries banned {DDT} due to environmental concerns.
e.zh: 由于环境问题,许多国家禁用了滴滴涕。

e.en: Farmers once sprayed {DDT} on crops to kill insects.
e.zh: 农民过去常在作物上喷洒滴滴涕灭虫。

ddu.t: abbr. 未完税交货（贸易术语）

e.en: The team plans a {DDU} shipment to the buyer's warehouse.
e.zh: 团队计划以未完税交货方式发货到买方仓库。

e.en: Under {DDU} terms, the buyer handles import duties.
e.zh: 根据 DDU 条款,买方负责进口关税。

dea.t: n. 美国缉毒局（Drug Enforcement Administration）

e.en: The {DEA} arrested several drug traffickers yesterday.
e.zh: 美国缉毒局昨天逮捕了几名毒贩。

e.en: He works as a special agent for the {DEA}.
e.zh: 他在美国缉毒局担任特别探员。

e.en: The {deacon} greeted families at the church entrance.
e.zh: 执事在教堂门口迎接家庭们。

e.en: He was ordained as a {deacon} last Sunday.
e.zh: 他上周日被任命为执事。

e.en: The {deaconess} organized the food drive for the homeless.
e.zh: 女执事为无家可归者组织了食物募捐。

e.en: She served as a {deaconess} for over twenty years.
e.zh: 她担任女执事二十多年。

deactivate.t: v. 停用；关闭；注销（账号）

e.en: Please {deactivate} your account before deleting the app.
e.zh: 请在删除应用前停用你的账户。

e.en: You can {deactivate} the alarm using this code.
e.zh: 你可以用这个密码解除警报。

e.en: Account {deactivation} takes effect within 24 hours.
e.zh: 账户停用将在 24 小时内生效。

e.en: The {deactivation} of the old system caused some confusion.
e.zh: 旧系统的停用造成了一些混乱。

dead.t:
adj. 死的；无效的；无电的
adv. 完全地

e.en: My phone battery is completely {dead} again.
e.zh: 我的手机电池又彻底没电了。

e.en: The streets were {dead} quiet at midnight.
e.zh: 午夜时街道死一般寂静。

deadbeat.t: n. 赖账者；游手好闲的人

e.en: Her ex-husband turned out to be a {deadbeat} dad.
e.zh: 她的前夫原来是个不负责任的爸爸。

e.en: The landlord evicted the {deadbeat} tenant last month.
e.zh: 房东上个月赶走了那个赖账的租客。

e.en: Thick curtains help {deaden} street noise at night.
e.zh: 厚厚的窗帘有助于夜间隔绝街上的噪音。

e.en: Doctors gave him medication to {deaden} the pain.
e.zh: 医生给他用药来减轻疼痛。

e.en: The carpet {deadened} the sound of footsteps.
e.zh: 地毯减弱了脚步声。

e.en: Years of grief had {deadened} her emotions.
e.zh: 多年的悲伤让她的情感变得麻木。

deadening.t: adj. 令人麻木的；使减弱的

e.en: The {deadening} silence in the room felt unbearable.
e.zh: 房间里令人窒息的沉默让人难以忍受。

e.en: He found office work spiritually {deadening}.
e.zh: 他觉得办公室工作让人精神麻木。

deadens.t: v. 减弱（第三人称单数）

e.en: The thick foam {deadens} sound inside the studio.
e.zh: 厚实的泡沫材料隔绝了录音棚内的声音。

e.en: Routine work slowly {deadens} her creativity.
e.zh: 日复一日的工作慢慢消磨着她的创造力。

deadfall.t: n. 倒下的树木；压杀陷阱

e.en: The hiker tripped over a hidden {deadfall} in the woods.
e.zh: 徒步者被林中一根隐蔽的倒木绊倒了。

e.en: Trappers used a {deadfall} to catch small animals.
e.zh: 猎人用木石陷阱来捕捉小动物。

deadhead.t:
n. 空驶车辆；铁杆粉丝
v. 空车返回

e.en: You should {deadhead} the roses to encourage new blooms.
e.zh: 你应该剪掉残花以促进玫瑰再次开花。

e.en: The truck had to {deadhead} back without a load.
e.zh: 那辆卡车不得不空车返回。

deadline.t: n. 截止日期；最后期限

e.en: The project {deadline} has been moved to Friday.
e.zh: 项目截止日期被推迟到了星期五。

e.en: I'm working overtime to meet the {deadline}.
e.zh: 我正在加班以赶上截止日期。

e.en: Tight {deadlines} make me really anxious at work.
e.zh: 紧迫的截止日期让我在工作中非常焦虑。

e.en: Journalists constantly juggle multiple {deadlines}.
e.zh: 记者不断地应付多个截稿期。

e.en: Scientists studied the {deadliness} of the new virus.
e.zh: 科学家研究了这种新病毒的致命程度。

e.en: The {deadliness} of the venom shocked the researchers.
e.zh: 这种毒液的致命性让研究人员震惊。

e.en: The negotiations reached a {deadlock} after six hours.
e.zh: 谈判在六小时后陷入僵局。

e.en: Two threads can cause a {deadlock} in your program.
e.zh: 两个线程会导致程序出现死锁。

deadlocked.t: adj. 陷入僵局的；僵持的

e.en: The jury was {deadlocked} after three days of deliberation.
e.zh: 陪审团经过三天审议后陷入僵局。

e.en: Congress remained {deadlocked} over the budget bill.
e.zh: 国会在预算法案上仍然僵持不下。

deadly.t:
adj. 致命的；极度的
adv. 非常地

e.en: The virus turned out to be {deadly} for older patients.
e.zh: 事实证明这种病毒对年长患者来说是致命的。

e.en: She has a {deadly} aim with a basketball.
e.zh: 她投篮的准头堪称一绝。

e.en: The crane operator released the {deadman} switch and everything stopped.
e.zh: 起重机操作员松开安全开关，一切都停了下来。

e.en: Engineers installed a {deadman} anchor to secure the cable.
e.zh: 工程师安装了一个固定锚来固定缆绳。

e.en: The {deadness} in her voice worried her friends.
e.zh: 她声音里的那份死气让朋友们很担心。

e.en: He noticed a strange {deadness} in his fingertips after the cold.
e.zh: 受冻之后他发觉指尖有种奇怪的麻木感。

deadpan.t: adj. 面无表情的（冷面笑话）

e.en: She delivered the joke with a perfectly {deadpan} expression.
e.zh: 她以一脸严肃的表情把笑话说了出来。

e.en: His {deadpan} humor took a while to appreciate.
e.zh: 他那种面无表情的幽默要过一阵子才能品出味来。

e.en: The old equipment became a {deadweight} on the company's budget.
e.zh: 那些旧设备成了公司预算上的累赘。

e.en: Lifting his {deadweight} body off the floor took two people.
e.zh: 把他那毫无知觉的身体从地上抬起来用了两个人。

e.en: The new manager cleared out the {deadwood} from the team.
e.zh: 新经理把团队里的冗员清理掉了。

e.en: We collected {deadwood} from the forest for the campfire.
e.zh: 我们从林子里捡了枯木来生篝火。

e.en: My grandfather is going {deaf} in his left ear.
e.zh: 我爷爷的左耳渐渐听不见了。

e.en: The boss was {deaf} to all complaints from staff.
e.zh: 老板对员工的所有抱怨都充耳不闻。

e.en: The fireworks could {deafen} you if you stood too close.
e.zh: 如果站得太近，烟花的声音能把人震聋。

e.en: Loud machinery can {deafen} workers over time.
e.zh: 长期接触吵闹的机器会让工人逐渐失聪。

e.en: The explosion {deafened} everyone in the room for hours.
e.zh: 爆炸把屋里所有人震得好几个小时听不见。

e.en: She was momentarily {deafened} by the jet's takeoff.
e.zh: 喷气机起飞的轰鸣让她一时什么都听不到。

e.en: The crowd's cheers were absolutely {deafening}.
e.zh: 人群的欢呼声简直震耳欲聋。

e.en: His silence on the issue was {deafening}.
e.zh: 他对此事的沉默格外刺耳。

e.en: The concert was {deafeningly} loud from the front row.
e.zh: 在前排听演唱会的声音震耳欲聋。

e.en: The room fell {deafeningly} silent after his announcement.
e.zh: 他宣布之后，房间里陷入一片令人窒息的寂静。

e.en: Years of factory work caused his {deafness}.
e.zh: 多年在工厂工作导致了他的失聪。

e.en: Early treatment can prevent permanent {deafness} in children.
e.zh: 及早治疗可以避免儿童永久性耳聋。

deakin.t: n. 迪肯（人名/澳洲大学名）

e.en: She studies marine biology at {Deakin} University in Melbourne.
e.zh: 她在墨尔本的迪肯大学攻读海洋生物学。

e.en: Alfred {Deakin} served as Australia's prime minister three times.
e.zh: 阿尔弗雷德·迪金曾三次出任澳大利亚总理。

deal.t:
n. 交易；协议
v. 处理；发牌

e.en: They finally closed the {deal} after months of negotiation.
e.zh: 经过数月谈判，他们终于敲定了这笔交易。

e.en: I don't know how to {deal} with his constant complaints.
e.zh: 我不知道该怎么应对他没完没了的抱怨。

e.en: The car {dealer} offered a great discount on last year's models.
e.zh: 那家汽车经销商对去年款的车型给出了很大折扣。

e.en: The {dealer} shuffled the cards and dealt a new hand.
e.zh: 发牌员洗了牌，又发了一轮。

e.en: Local art {dealers} gathered for the annual auction.
e.zh: 当地的艺术品经销商齐聚一年一度的拍卖会。

e.en: Police arrested several drug {dealers} in the raid.
e.zh: 警方在突击行动中逮捕了多名毒贩。

e.en: I picked up my new SUV from the {dealership} this morning.
e.zh: 我今早从经销店把新的 SUV 提回家了。

e.en: The Toyota {dealership} is hiring more sales staff.
e.zh: 那家丰田经销店正在招更多销售人员。

e.en: She is {dealing} with a difficult client this week.
e.zh: 她这周正在应付一个难缠的客户。

e.en: His honest {dealing} earned him a strong reputation.
e.zh: 他诚信的处事方式为他赢得了好口碑。

e.en: The company's {dealings} with overseas suppliers came under scrutiny.
e.zh: 该公司与海外供应商的往来受到了审查。

e.en: I've had no {dealings} with that bank before.
e.zh: 我以前从未跟那家银行打过交道。

dealmaker.t: n. 交易撮合者；谈判高手

e.en: He has a reputation as a tough {dealmaker} on Wall Street.
e.zh: 他在华尔街以强硬的交易撮合者著称。

e.en: Every successful startup needs a skilled {dealmaker}.
e.zh: 每家成功的初创公司都需要一位精明的撮合高手。

deals.t:
n. 交易（复数）
v. 处理（第三人称单数）

e.en: Black Friday {deals} start at midnight on the website.
e.zh: 网站上的黑五优惠从午夜开始。

e.en: This book {deals} with climate change in plain language.
e.zh: 这本书用通俗的语言探讨了气候变化问题。

dealt.t: v. deal 的过去式/过去分词

e.en: The team {dealt} with the bug within an hour.
e.zh: 团队在一小时内解决了那个 bug。

e.en: Life {dealt} her a tough hand, but she persevered.
e.zh: 生活给她发了一手烂牌，但她坚持了下来。

e.en: The {dean} of engineering announced a new scholarship program.
e.zh: 工程学院院长宣布设立一项新的奖学金计划。

e.en: She was promoted to {dean} of students last semester.
e.zh: 她上学期晋升为学生事务主任。

decease.t:
n. 死亡
v. 去世

e.en: The estate passes to the children upon the parents' {decease}.
e.zh: 父母去世后,遗产将由子女继承。

e.en: Please notify the bank promptly after the account holder's {decease}.
e.zh: 账户持有人去世后请及时通知银行。

deceased.t:
adj. 已故的
n. 死者

e.en: Mourners gathered to honor the {deceased} at the funeral.
e.zh: 哀悼者聚集在葬礼上缅怀逝者。

e.en: The will was read a week after she was {deceased}.
e.zh: 她去世一周后,遗嘱被宣读。

e.en: The lawyer reviewed the {decedent}'s will with the family.
e.zh: 律师与家属一起审阅了死者的遗嘱。

e.en: All debts of the {decedent} were settled by the estate.
e.zh: 死者的所有债务都由遗产清偿。

e.en: The whole scheme was built on lies and {deceit}.
e.zh: 整个计划都建立在谎言和欺骗之上。

e.en: She could no longer tolerate his constant {deceit}.
e.zh: 她再也无法容忍他不断的欺骗。

e.en: His {deceitful} smile didn't fool her for a second.
e.zh: 他那虚伪的笑容一秒都没骗到她。

e.en: The salesman used {deceitful} tactics to push the warranty.
e.zh: 那位推销员用欺骗手段推销延保服务。

e.en: Her small {deceits} eventually unraveled the entire friendship.
e.zh: 她的种种小欺骗最终葬送了整段友谊。

e.en: The novel exposes the everyday {deceits} of corporate life.
e.zh: 这部小说揭露了职场生活中种种日常的欺诈行为。

e.en: Don't let the cheap price {deceive} you about quality.
e.zh: 别让低廉的价格让你对品质产生错觉。

e.en: He tried to {deceive} his parents about his grades.
e.zh: 他试图在成绩问题上欺骗父母。

deceived.t: v. 欺骗（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: She felt {deceived} when she discovered the hidden fees.
e.zh: 当她发现隐藏费用时,觉得自己被骗了。

e.en: The phishing email {deceived} thousands of unsuspecting users.
e.zh: 那封钓鱼邮件骗过了成千上万毫无戒心的用户。

e.en: History remembers him as a charming but ruthless {deceiver}.
e.zh: 历史将他记为一个迷人却冷酷的骗子。

e.en: The con artist proved to be a master {deceiver}.
e.zh: 那个骗徒被证明是个行骗高手。

deceives.t: v. 欺骗（第三人称单数）

e.en: The mirror {deceives} the eye into seeing depth.
e.zh: 那面镜子让眼睛产生了纵深的错觉。

e.en: He routinely {deceives} clients with vague contract language.
e.zh: 他经常用含糊的合同措辞欺骗客户。

deceiving.t:
v. 欺骗（现在分词）
adj. 骗人的

e.en: Appearances can be {deceiving} when you shop online.
e.zh: 网购时,外观往往具有欺骗性。

e.en: She caught him {deceiving} the team about the deadline.
e.zh: 她发现他在截止日期上欺骗团队。

e.en: Drivers must {decelerate} smoothly when entering the school zone.
e.zh: 驶入学校区域时司机必须平稳减速。

e.en: Global growth is expected to {decelerate} next quarter.
e.zh: 预计下季度全球经济增长将放缓。

e.en: The car's sudden {deceleration} threw groceries off the seat.
e.zh: 汽车骤然减速,把座位上的杂货都甩了下来。

e.en: Economists warned of a sharp {deceleration} in consumer spending.
e.zh: 经济学家警告消费者支出将急剧放缓。

e.en: We always visit grandma in early {December}.
e.zh: 我们总是在十二月初去看望奶奶。

e.en: Snow blanketed the entire town by mid-{December}.
e.zh: 到了十二月中旬,整个小镇都被白雪覆盖。

e.en: Recent {Decembers} have been unusually warm in our region.
e.zh: 近几年的十二月在我们地区出奇地暖和。

e.en: She remembered all the {Decembers} they spent together skiing.
e.zh: 她记得他们一起滑雪度过的每一个十二月。

e.en: At least have the {decency} to apologize in person.
e.zh: 至少要有当面道歉的起码礼貌。

e.en: Public {decency} laws vary widely from country to country.
e.zh: 各国关于公共礼仪的法律差异很大。

decennial.t:
adj. 十年一次的
n. 十周年

e.en: The {decennial} census helps determine federal funding allocations.
e.zh: 十年一次的人口普查有助于决定联邦资金的分配。

e.en: The university held a {decennial} reunion for the class.
e.zh: 大学为这届毕业生举办了十年聚会。

e.en: The cafe serves a surprisingly {decent} cup of coffee.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆的咖啡出乎意料地不错。

e.en: He's a {decent} guy who always helps his neighbors.
e.zh: 他是个正派的人,总是乐于帮助邻居。

decentered.t: adj. 去中心化的；偏离中心的

e.en: The logo looks {decentered} on the homepage banner.
e.zh: 标志在首页横幅上看起来没居中。

e.en: Modern criticism has {decentered} the author's role in interpretation.
e.zh: 现代批评淡化了作者在文本解读中的核心地位。

decentering.t: v. 去中心化（现在分词）

e.en: The course focuses on {decentering} Western perspectives in history.
e.zh: 这门课着重于淡化历史中以西方为中心的视角。

e.en: {Decentering} the navigation bar broke the site's layout.
e.zh: 把导航栏移离居中位置破坏了网站的布局。

e.en: She sings {decently}, though not professionally.
e.zh: 她唱得还算不错,但够不上专业水准。

e.en: Please dress {decently} for the job interview tomorrow.
e.zh: 明天面试请穿得体一点。

decentralisation.t: n. 去中心化；分权（英式拼写）

e.en: The party campaigned on the {decentralisation} of government powers.
e.zh: 该党以下放政府权力为竞选纲领。

e.en: Blockchain enables true {decentralisation} of financial transactions.
e.zh: 区块链让金融交易实现了真正的去中心化。

decentralise.t: v. 使分权；去中心化（英式拼写）

e.en: The company plans to {decentralise} decision-making across regional offices.
e.zh: 公司计划将决策权下放到各地区办公室。

e.en: Reformers want to {decentralise} the education system entirely.
e.zh: 改革者希望彻底将教育体系去中心化。

decentralised.t: adj. 去中心化的（英式拼写）

e.en: Bitcoin operates on a fully {decentralised} network of nodes.
e.zh: 比特币运行在一个完全去中心化的节点网络上。

e.en: The startup {decentralised} its teams during the pandemic.
e.zh: 这家初创公司在疫情期间将团队分散运作。

decentralises.t: v. 去中心化（第三人称单数，英式）

e.en: This new policy {decentralises} authority over school curricula.
e.zh: 这项新政策将学校课程的决定权下放。

e.en: The platform {decentralises} content moderation across community volunteers.
e.zh: 该平台将内容审核分散给社区志愿者负责。

decentralising.t: v. 去中心化（现在分词，英式）

e.en: They are {decentralising} the data centers for better resilience.
e.zh: 他们正在分散数据中心以提升系统韧性。

e.en: {Decentralising} power can sometimes slow down emergency responses.
e.zh: 权力下放有时会拖慢紧急应对的速度。

e.en: {Decentralization} is a core principle of Web3 technology.
e.zh: 去中心化是Web3技术的核心原则。

e.en: The reform pushed for greater {decentralization} of healthcare services.
e.zh: 这次改革推动医疗服务更大程度的去中心化。

e.en: The CEO wants to {decentralize} hiring across all departments.
e.zh: 首席执行官希望将招聘权下放给各个部门。

e.en: New protocols aim to {decentralize} cloud storage entirely.
e.zh: 新协议旨在彻底实现云存储的去中心化。

decentralized.t: adj. 去中心化的；分布式的

e.en: Ethereum hosts thousands of {decentralized} applications today.
e.zh: 如今以太坊上托管着数千个去中心化应用。

e.en: The company adopted a {decentralized} structure after the merger.
e.zh: 合并之后,公司采用了分散式的组织架构。

decentralizes.t: v. 去中心化（第三人称单数）

e.en: This update {decentralizes} the app's user authentication system.
e.zh: 这次更新让应用的用户认证系统实现了去中心化。

e.en: The new law {decentralizes} tax collection to local councils.
e.zh: 新法律将税收征管权下放给地方议会。

decentralizing.t: v. 去中心化（现在分词）

e.en: They are {decentralizing} customer support to regional teams.
e.zh: 他们正在把客户支持分散给各地区的团队。

e.en: {Decentralizing} the database improved query speed significantly.
e.zh: 将数据库去中心化大大提升了查询速度。

e.en: The investigation uncovered years of corporate {deception}.
e.zh: 调查揭露了多年的企业欺诈行为。

e.en: Magic tricks rely on harmless visual {deception}.
e.zh: 魔术依靠的是无害的视觉欺骗。

deceptive.t: adj. 欺骗性的；易误导的

e.en: The product's marketing was found to be {deceptive}.
e.zh: 该产品的营销被认定具有欺骗性。

e.en: The calm sea was {deceptive}; a storm was approaching.
e.zh: 平静的海面具有欺骗性,一场风暴正在逼近。

deceptively.t: adv. 看似地；具欺骗性地

e.en: The recipe is {deceptively} simple but takes hours.
e.zh: 这个食谱看似简单,实际却要花上好几个小时。

e.en: The lake looks {deceptively} shallow near the shore.
e.zh: 湖水靠岸的地方看着浅,其实很有迷惑性。

decertification.t: n. 取消认证；撤销资格

e.en: The union faced {decertification} after most members withdrew support.
e.zh: 在多数成员撤回支持后，工会面临被取消认证。

e.en: The school appealed the {decertification} of its nursing program.
e.zh: 学校对其护理专业被取消认证提起了申诉。

decertify.t: v. 撤销认证；取消资格

e.en: Regulators voted to {decertify} the lab after repeated violations.
e.zh: 在多次违规后，监管机构投票取消该实验室的认证。

e.en: The board may {decertify} any inspector who falsifies reports.
e.zh: 董事会可取消任何伪造报告的检查员的资格。

e.en: The concert hit nearly 110 {decibels} near the stage.
e.zh: 音乐会舞台附近的音量接近110分贝。

e.en: A whisper measures about 30 {decibels} on average.
e.zh: 耳语的音量平均约为30分贝。

e.en: I can't {decide} what to order for dinner tonight.
e.zh: 我决定不了今晚晚饭点什么。

e.en: One goal could {decide} the entire championship match.
e.zh: 一个进球就可能决定整场冠军赛的结果。

decided.t:
v. 决定（过去式）
adj. 明确的

e.en: She {decided} to quit her job and travel for a year.
e.zh: 她决定辞职去旅行一年。

e.en: There was a {decided} chill in the morning air.
e.zh: 早晨的空气中有一股明显的寒意。

e.en: The new phone is {decidedly} better than last year's model.
e.zh: 这款新手机明显比去年的型号好得多。

e.en: He looked {decidedly} uncomfortable during the interview.
e.zh: 他在面试中显得明显不自在。

e.en: Price was the {decider} for most online shoppers surveyed.
e.zh: 对多数受访网购者来说，价格是决定性因素。

e.en: Game seven will be the {decider} of the series.
e.zh: 第七场将是这轮系列赛的决胜战。

decides.t: v. 决定（第三人称单数）

e.en: The committee {decides} on funding requests every Friday.
e.zh: 委员会每周五对资助申请作出决定。

e.en: Whoever scores first usually {decides} the outcome here.
e.zh: 在这里通常先得分的一方决定胜负。

deciding.t:
adj. 决定性的
v. 决定（现在分词）

e.en: I'm still {deciding} between the red and blue jacket.
e.zh: 我还在红色和蓝色外套之间犹豫。

e.en: Her speech was the {deciding} factor in the election.
e.zh: 她的演讲是这次选举的决定性因素。

e.en: Maples and oaks are common {deciduous} trees in this park.
e.zh: 枫树和橡树是这个公园里常见的落叶树。

e.en: {Deciduous} forests turn brilliant colors every autumn.
e.zh: 落叶林每到秋天就会变成绚丽的色彩。

e.en: Students in the top {decile} qualify for the scholarship.
e.zh: 成绩排名前十分之一的学生可申请该奖学金。

e.en: The report breaks down income by {decile} across regions.
e.zh: 报告按十分位数分析了各地区的收入情况。

e.en: Add one {deciliter} of milk to the batter and stir.
e.zh: 在面糊中加入一分升牛奶并搅拌。

e.en: His blood sugar was 90 milligrams per {deciliter}.
e.zh: 他的血糖值为每分升90毫克。

decimal.t:
n. 小数
adj. 十进制的

e.en: Round the answer to two {decimal} places, please.
e.zh: 请把答案保留到小数点后两位。

e.en: Move the {decimal} point one digit to the right.
e.zh: 把小数点向右移一位。

decimate.t: v. 大量毁灭；严重削减

e.en: The drought could {decimate} this year's wheat harvest.
e.zh: 这场干旱可能会让今年的小麦收成大减。

e.en: Budget cuts threaten to {decimate} the research team.
e.zh: 预算削减可能会让研究团队元气大伤。

decimated.t: v. 重创（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: The storm {decimated} coastal villages along the bay.
e.zh: 风暴摧毁了海湾沿岸的村庄。

e.en: Layoffs have {decimated} the once-thriving newsroom.
e.zh: 裁员让曾经兴旺的新闻编辑部元气大伤。

e.en: The {decimation} of local bee populations alarmed scientists.
e.zh: 本地蜜蜂数量的锐减令科学家们感到震惊。

e.en: Wildfires caused the {decimation} of ancient forests.
e.zh: 山火导致了古老森林的大规模毁灭。

debonair.t: adj. 温文尔雅的；风度翩翩的

e.en: The {debonair} host welcomed everyone with a charming smile.
e.zh: 那位风度翩翩的主持人以迷人的微笑迎接每位来宾。

e.en: He looked {debonair} in his tailored navy suit.
e.zh: 他穿着定制的藏青色西装,显得潇洒迷人。

e.en: Ask the butcher to {debone} the chicken thighs for you.
e.zh: 让肉店帮你把鸡腿肉去骨。

e.en: It takes practice to cleanly {debone} a whole fish.
e.zh: 把一整条鱼干净地剔骨需要练习。

debouch.t: v. 流出；（从狭处）进入开阔地

e.en: The narrow trail will {debouch} onto a sunny meadow.
e.zh: 这条小径会通向一片洒满阳光的草地。

e.en: The river {debouch}es into the bay near the lighthouse.
e.zh: 这条河在灯塔附近汇入海湾。

debridement.t: n. 清创术（清除伤口坏死组织）

e.en: The nurse performed {debridement} to clean the infected wound.
e.zh: 护士对受感染的伤口进行了清创处理。

e.en: Surgical {debridement} is often needed for serious burns.
e.zh: 严重烧伤通常需要手术清创。

e.en: Let's {debrief} after the meeting to share notes.
e.zh: 会议结束后我们碰个头,分享一下笔记。

e.en: The team met to {debrief} the failed product launch.
e.zh: 团队开会复盘了这次失败的产品发布。

debriefing.t: n. 任务汇报；情况复盘
