e.en: Her boss often {discourages} risky experiments at work.
e.zh: 她的老板常常不鼓励工作中冒险的尝试。

discouraging.t: adj. 令人泄气的；使人沮丧的

e.en: The early sales numbers were pretty {discouraging}.
e.zh: 早期的销售数据相当令人沮丧。

e.en: He kept training despite his coach {discouraging} him.
e.zh: 尽管教练一直在打击他，他还是坚持训练。

e.en: Ticket sales remained {discouragingly} low all month.
e.zh: 整个月票房低得令人沮丧。

e.en: She shook her head {discouragingly} at his plan.
e.zh: 她对他的计划丧气地摇了摇头。

discourse.t:
n. 话语；论述；演讲
v. 论述

e.en: Online {discourse} has grown more polarized in recent years.
e.zh: 近年来网络讨论变得越来越两极化。

e.en: The professor will {discourse} on climate ethics tonight.
e.zh: 教授今晚将就气候伦理发表演讲。

discourses.t:
n. 论述（复数）
v. 论述（第三人称单数）

e.en: Her book analyzes political {discourses} on immigration.
e.zh: 她的书分析了关于移民的政治话语。

e.en: He often {discourses} at length about classical music.
e.zh: 他经常滔滔不绝地谈论古典音乐。

e.en: It was {discourteous} of him to leave without saying goodbye.
e.zh: 他不告而别真是失礼。

e.en: The waiter was openly {discourteous} to foreign tourists.
e.zh: 服务员对外国游客明显不礼貌。

e.en: She apologized for her son's {discourtesy} at dinner.
e.zh: 她为儿子在晚餐时的失礼道歉。

e.en: Interrupting elders is considered a serious {discourtesy}.
e.zh: 打断长辈说话被认为是严重的失礼。

e.en: Kids love to {discover} hidden features in new games.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢在新游戏里发现隐藏功能。

e.en: Scientists hope to {discover} life on distant planets.
e.zh: 科学家希望在遥远的行星上发现生命。

discoverable.t: adj. 可发现的；可被找到的

e.en: Make your profile {discoverable} so friends can find you.
e.zh: 把你的资料设为可被发现，朋友才能找到你。

e.en: Email metadata is {discoverable} during a lawsuit.
e.zh: 诉讼期间电子邮件的元数据可被调取。

e.en: She {discovered} a great coffee shop near the office.
e.zh: 她在办公室附近发现了一家很棒的咖啡店。

e.en: Researchers {discovered} a new species in the rainforest.
e.zh: 研究人员在雨林中发现了一个新物种。

e.en: Marie Curie was the {discoverer} of polonium and radium.
e.zh: 玛丽·居里是钋和镭的发现者。

e.en: The {discoverer} of the cave wishes to remain anonymous.
e.zh: 发现这个洞穴的人希望保持匿名。

e.en: Recent {discoveries} have rewritten human migration history.
e.zh: 近年的发现改写了人类迁徙史。

e.en: Some of my favorite music {discoveries} came from Spotify.
e.zh: 我最喜欢的一些音乐都是在 Spotify 上发现的。

e.en: She enjoys {discovering} new restaurants on weekends.
e.zh: 她喜欢在周末发掘新餐厅。

e.en: The team is {discovering} just how complex the bug is.
e.zh: 团队正逐渐发现这个 bug 有多复杂。

discovers.t: v. 发现（第三人称单数）

e.en: In chapter three, the detective {discovers} a hidden letter.
e.zh: 在第三章，侦探发现了一封藏起来的信。

e.en: Every parent eventually {discovers} their child's secret talent.
e.zh: 每位家长最终都会发现孩子的隐藏才能。

discovery.t: n. 发现；新发现的事物

e.en: The {discovery} of penicillin changed modern medicine forever.
e.zh: 青霉素的发现彻底改变了现代医学。

e.en: Self-{discovery} often happens when you travel alone.
e.zh: 独自旅行时常常会有自我发现。

discredit.t:
v. 败坏名声；使怀疑
n. 丧失信誉

e.en: Critics tried to {discredit} the report with personal attacks.
e.zh: 批评者试图用人身攻击来抹黑这份报告。

e.en: One careless tweet can {discredit} years of serious research.
e.zh: 一条随意的推文可能毁掉多年的严肃研究。

discreditable.t: adj. 有损声誉的；丢脸的

e.en: His {discreditable} behavior cost him the promotion.
e.zh: 他不光彩的行为让他失去了升职机会。

e.en: The firm fired her for {discreditable} conduct online.
e.zh: 公司因她在网上的不当行为将她解雇。

discredited.t: adj. 名誉扫地的；不可信的

e.en: The theory has been thoroughly {discredited} by new evidence.
e.zh: 新的证据已彻底推翻了这一理论。

e.en: Once {discredited}, the politician never recovered her reputation.
e.zh: 一旦名誉扫地，这位政客再也没能挽回声誉。

discrediting.t: v. 败坏名声（现在分词）

e.en: Spreading false rumors aimed at {discrediting} the CEO failed.
e.zh: 用谣言抹黑首席执行官的企图失败了。

e.en: The lawyer focused on {discrediting} the witness's memory.
e.zh: 律师重点质疑证人记忆的可信度。

discredits.t: v. 败坏名声（第三人称单数）

e.en: Lying about small things {discredits} everything else you say.
e.zh: 在小事上撒谎会让你说的其他话都失去可信度。

e.en: Her sloppy citation {discredits} an otherwise excellent paper.
e.zh: 草率的引用让一篇本来优秀的论文失了分。

e.en: Please be {discreet} when discussing salary at the office.
e.zh: 在办公室讨论薪水时请谨慎些。

e.en: The hotel offers {discreet} service for celebrity guests.
e.zh: 这家酒店为名人客人提供低调贴心的服务。

e.en: She {discreetly} slipped the note into his pocket.
e.zh: 她悄悄地把纸条塞进了他的口袋。

e.en: The waiter {discreetly} refilled the water glasses.
e.zh: 服务员不动声色地续上了水。

e.en: There's a small {discrepancy} between the receipt and your statement.
e.zh: 收据和你的账单之间有一处小差异。

e.en: The {discrepancy} in their stories made the police suspicious.
e.zh: 他们说法上的出入引起了警方的怀疑。

discrepant.t: adj. 有差异的；不一致的

e.en: The two sensors gave wildly {discrepant} temperature readings.
e.zh: 两个传感器给出的温度读数差异极大。

e.en: Researchers must explain any {discrepant} data in their findings.
e.zh: 研究人员必须解释结果中任何不一致的数据。

e.en: The course is divided into six {discrete} modules.
e.zh: 这门课被分成六个独立的模块。

e.en: Computers store information as {discrete} ones and zeros.
e.zh: 计算机以离散的 0 和 1 存储信息。

e.en: The dataset records temperatures {discretely} every ten minutes.
e.zh: 数据集每十分钟离散地记录一次温度。

e.en: Each layer is trained {discretely} before the model is combined.
e.zh: 在合并模型前，每一层都是单独训练的。

discretion.t:
n. 自主决定权
n. 谨慎；慎重

e.en: Use your own {discretion} when approving small refunds.
e.zh: 批准小额退款时请自行斟酌处理。

e.en: The judge has full {discretion} over sentencing in this case.
e.zh: 法官在本案的量刑上拥有完全的自由裁量权。

discretionary.t: adj. 可自由决定的；酌情的

e.en: Families have less {discretionary} income during a recession.
e.zh: 经济衰退时家庭可自由支配的收入会减少。

e.en: Bonuses are {discretionary} and depend on company performance.
e.zh: 奖金是酌情发放的，取决于公司业绩。

e.en: Different states grant judges varying {discretions} in sentencing.
e.zh: 不同的州给予法官的量刑自由裁量权各不相同。

e.en: Managers must document any {discretions} they exercise on refunds.
e.zh: 经理须记录他们在退款上行使的任何裁量权。

discriminant.t:
n. 判别式（数学）
adj. 区别性的

e.en: The {discriminant} tells you how many real roots an equation has.
e.zh: 判别式可以告诉你方程有多少个实根。

e.en: Linear {discriminant} analysis is common in machine learning.
e.zh: 线性判别分析在机器学习中很常见。

discriminate.t:
v. 区分；辨别
v. 歧视

e.en: Employers cannot {discriminate} based on age or gender.
e.zh: 雇主不得因年龄或性别而歧视员工。

e.en: Babies quickly learn to {discriminate} between familiar voices.
e.zh: 婴儿很快就能分辨出熟悉的声音。

discriminated.t:
v. 歧视（过去式）
v. 区分（过去式）

e.en: She felt {discriminated} against during the hiring process.
e.zh: 她觉得在招聘过程中受到了歧视。

e.en: The expert {discriminated} between genuine and forged paintings.
e.zh: 专家分辨出了真画和伪作。

discriminates.t: v. 区分；歧视（第三人称单数）

e.en: The algorithm unfairly {discriminates} against certain accents.
e.zh: 该算法对某些口音存在不公平的歧视。

e.en: A good chef {discriminates} between fresh and frozen seafood.
e.zh: 好厨师能分辨出新鲜与冷冻的海鲜。

discriminating.t:
adj. 有鉴赏力的
v. 辨别；歧视

e.en: This wine appeals to {discriminating} drinkers with refined taste.
e.zh: 这款酒深受品位讲究的饮家青睐。

e.en: The company was accused of {discriminating} against older applicants.
e.zh: 该公司被指控歧视年龄较大的应聘者。

discrimination.t:
n. 歧视
n. 辨别力

e.en: The law prohibits {discrimination} in housing and employment.
e.zh: 法律禁止在住房和就业中存在歧视。

e.en: Color {discrimination} weakens slightly as people age.
e.zh: 人随着年龄增长，对颜色的辨别能力会略微下降。

e.en: The report documents subtle {discriminations} in workplace promotions.
e.zh: 报告记录了职场晋升中各种隐性的歧视。

e.en: Sommeliers train to make fine {discriminations} between vintages.
e.zh: 侍酒师经过训练能细致辨别不同年份的酒。

discriminative.t: adj. 有区别的；歧视性的

e.en: {Discriminative} models classify inputs rather than generate new data.
e.zh: 判别式模型用于分类输入，而不是生成新数据。

e.en: The test measures students' {discriminative} listening skills.
e.zh: 该测试考察学生的辨听能力。

discriminator.t:
n. 判别器（AI／电路）
n. 歧视者

e.en: In a GAN, the {discriminator} tries to spot fake images.
e.zh: 在生成对抗网络中，判别器负责识别伪造图像。

e.en: Email address is a useful {discriminator} between user accounts.
e.zh: 电子邮箱是区分用户账号的一个有用标识。

discriminatory.t: adj. 歧视性的；差别对待的

e.en: The court ruled the policy {discriminatory} against women.
e.zh: 法院裁定该政策对女性构成歧视。

e.en: Customers complained about the bank's {discriminatory} lending practices.
e.zh: 客户投诉这家银行的贷款做法存在歧视。

discs.t:
n. 碟片；光盘
n. 椎间盘

e.en: He still keeps a stack of old DVD {discs} in the closet.
e.zh: 他衣橱里还放着一摞旧 DVD 光盘。

e.en: Worn spinal {discs} can cause chronic lower back pain.
e.zh: 磨损的脊椎间盘可能引起慢性腰痛。

discursive.t: adj. 漫谈式的；话题跳跃的

e.en: His writing style is {discursive} and hard to follow.
e.zh: 他的写作风格散漫，让人难以跟上思路。

e.en: The lecture was charming but rather {discursive}.
e.zh: 这场讲座很有魅力，但内容颇为离题。

discursively.t: adv. 漫谈式地；东拉西扯地

e.en: The professor spoke {discursively}, jumping from topic to topic.
e.zh: 教授说话东拉西扯，话题跳来跳去。

e.en: She wrote {discursively} about her travels in Asia.
e.zh: 她漫无边际地写下了在亚洲的旅行见闻。

e.en: He threw the {discus} farther than anyone at the meet.
e.zh: 他在那场比赛中铁饼掷得最远。

e.en: The {discus} event is one of the oldest Olympic sports.
e.zh: 掷铁饼是最古老的奥运项目之一。

e.en: Let's {discuss} the project budget at tomorrow's meeting.
e.zh: 我们明天开会再讨论项目预算吧。

e.en: Parents and teachers {discuss} each child's progress every term.
e.zh: 每学期家长和老师都会讨论每个孩子的进步。

discussant.t: n. 讨论人；与会发言者

e.en: The {discussant} offered sharp critiques of the keynote paper.
e.zh: 评议人对主旨论文提出了尖锐的批评。

e.en: Each panel features one moderator and three invited {discussant}s.
e.zh: 每个专题小组配一名主持人和三位特邀评议人。

e.en: We {discussed} the pros and cons over coffee yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天我们边喝咖啡边讨论了利弊。

e.en: The book is widely {discussed} in literary circles right now.
e.zh: 这本书目前在文学圈里被广泛讨论。

discusses.t: v. 讨论（第三人称单数）

e.en: Her latest article {discusses} the future of remote work.
e.zh: 她的最新文章探讨了远程办公的未来。

e.en: The podcast {discusses} new technology every Friday morning.
e.zh: 这档播客每周五早上讨论新科技。

e.en: They are {discussing} how to split the rent fairly.
e.zh: 他们正在讨论如何公平地分摊房租。

e.en: We spent the whole evening {discussing} our travel plans.
e.zh: 我们花了一整晚讨论旅行计划。

e.en: The team had a long {discussion} about next quarter's goals.
e.zh: 团队就下季度的目标进行了长时间的讨论。

e.en: This topic deserves more {discussion} before we decide.
e.zh: 在做决定前，这个话题值得更多讨论。

e.en: Trade {discussions} between the two countries resumed last week.
e.zh: 两国的贸易谈判上周恢复了。

e.en: Late-night {discussions} with friends often turn philosophical.
e.zh: 和朋友深夜的聊天经常变得很哲学。

disdain.t:
n. 蔑视；不屑
v. 鄙视

e.en: She looked at the cheap copy with obvious {disdain}.
e.zh: 她带着明显的轻蔑看着那个廉价仿品。

e.en: Critics treated the new film with cold {disdain}.
e.zh: 影评人对这部新片报以冷漠的鄙视。

disdainful.t: adj. 轻蔑的；不屑一顾的

e.en: He gave a {disdainful} laugh and walked away.
e.zh: 他轻蔑地笑了一声便走开了。

e.en: Her {disdainful} tone made everyone uncomfortable at the table.
e.zh: 她那种轻蔑的语气让全桌人都很不自在。

e.en: He waved the offer away {disdainfully} without reading it.
e.zh: 他看都没看就轻蔑地挥手拒绝了那个提议。

e.en: She glanced {disdainfully} at the messy room.
e.zh: 她轻蔑地扫了一眼凌乱的房间。

disdains.t: v. 蔑视（第三人称单数）

e.en: He {disdains} small talk and prefers serious conversation.
e.zh: 他不屑于闲聊，更喜欢严肃的对话。

e.en: The author {disdains} social media and rarely posts online.
e.zh: 这位作家鄙视社交媒体，很少在网上发帖。

e.en: Heart {disease} remains the leading cause of death worldwide.
e.zh: 心脏病仍是全球的头号死因。

e.en: Vaccines have prevented countless cases of serious {disease}.
e.zh: 疫苗预防了无数严重疾病的发生。

e.en: The gardener removed all the {diseased} branches from the tree.
e.zh: 园丁剪掉了树上所有患病的枝条。

e.en: Doctors carefully removed the {diseased} tissue during surgery.
e.zh: 医生在手术中小心地切除了病变组织。

e.en: Modern medicine can cure many {diseases} that once killed millions.
e.zh: 现代医学能治愈许多曾致命的疾病。

e.en: Mosquitoes spread several dangerous tropical {diseases}.
e.zh: 蚊子会传播多种危险的热带疾病。

diseconomy.t: n. 不经济；规模不经济

e.en: Rapid expansion created a {diseconomy} of scale for the company.
e.zh: 快速扩张给公司带来了规模不经济。

e.en: Traffic congestion is a classic urban {diseconomy}.
e.zh: 交通拥堵是典型的城市不经济现象。

e.en: Passengers will {disembark} from the front of the plane.
e.zh: 乘客将从飞机前舱下机。

e.en: We had to wait an hour to {disembark} the cruise ship.
e.zh: 我们等了一小时才下了游轮。

e.en: Please fill out the {disembarkation} card before landing.
e.zh: 请在飞机降落前填好入境卡。

e.en: {Disembarkation} from the ferry was slow due to bad weather.
e.zh: 由于天气恶劣，渡轮下船过程很缓慢。

disembodied.t: adj. 脱离肉体的；无形的

e.en: A {disembodied} voice came through the airport speakers.
e.zh: 机场广播里传来一个不见其人的声音。

e.en: The film features a {disembodied} hand crawling across the floor.
e.zh: 这部电影里有一只断手在地上爬行。

e.en: The novel explores the {disembodiment} of identity in virtual worlds.
e.zh: 小说探讨了虚拟世界中身份与肉体的分离。

e.en: Online life can create a strange sense of {disembodiment}.
e.zh: 网络生活会带来一种奇怪的脱离躯体之感。

disembody.t: v. 使脱离肉身；使无形

e.en: Some philosophers argue technology will eventually {disembody} human consciousness.
e.zh: 有些哲学家认为科技最终会让人类意识脱离肉体。

e.en: Virtual reality seems to {disembody} the user from physical surroundings.
e.zh: 虚拟现实似乎让使用者脱离了现实环境。

e.en: The chef showed students how to {disembowel} a fish quickly.
e.zh: 厨师向学生演示如何快速给鱼去内脏。

e.en: Ancient warriors would {disembowel} their enemies in battle.
e.zh: 古代战士在战斗中会将敌人剖腹。

disempower.t: v. 剥夺权力；削弱力量

e.en: Strict rules can {disempower} employees and kill creativity.
e.zh: 严苛的规则会削弱员工的能动性，扼杀创造力。

e.en: Bad design choices {disempower} users instead of helping them.
e.zh: 糟糕的设计反而削弱了用户的掌控感。

disempowered.t: adj. 被剥夺权力的；无力的

e.en: Many workers feel {disempowered} by constant micromanagement.
e.zh: 许多员工因长期被微观管理而感到无力。

e.en: The new policy left local councils completely {disempowered}.
e.zh: 新政策让地方议会完全失去了权力。

disempowerment.t: n. 权力被剥夺；无力感

e.en: The report highlights the {disempowerment} of rural communities.
e.zh: 报告强调了农村社区被剥夺权能的问题。

e.en: Constant criticism leads to a deep sense of {disempowerment}.
e.zh: 持续的批评会让人产生深深的无力感。

disenchant.t: v. 使幻想破灭；使清醒

e.en: Years of broken promises eventually {disenchant} even loyal voters.
e.zh: 多年食言最终会让最忠实的选民也感到幻灭。

e.en: Bad service can quickly {disenchant} long-time customers.
e.zh: 糟糕的服务会迅速让老顾客失望。

disenchanted.t: adj. 不再抱幻想的；失望的

e.en: She grew {disenchanted} with city life and moved to the countryside.
e.zh: 她对城市生活感到失望，搬去了乡下。

e.en: Many young voters are {disenchanted} with both major parties.
e.zh: 许多年轻选民对两大政党都感到失望。

e.en: There's growing {disenchantment} with traditional social media platforms.
e.zh: 人们对传统社交媒体平台越来越感到幻灭。

e.en: His {disenchantment} with the job became obvious to everyone.
e.zh: 他对这份工作的失望已让所有人看得出来。

disenfranchise.t: v. 剥夺选举权；剥夺权利

e.en: The new voting law could {disenfranchise} thousands of citizens.
e.zh: 新的选举法可能剥夺数千名公民的投票权。

e.en: Strict ID requirements often {disenfranchise} the elderly and poor.
e.zh: 严格的身份证要求常会让老人和穷人失去投票权。

e.en: The party tries to reach {disenfranchised} young voters online.
e.zh: 该党试图在网上接触被边缘化的年轻选民。

e.en: Many felt {disenfranchised} after their district was redrawn.
e.zh: 选区重划后，许多人感到自己被剥夺了权利。

disenfranchisement.t: n. 选举权／权利被剥夺

e.en: Activists are fighting voter {disenfranchisement} in several states.
e.zh: 活动人士正在多个州争取反对剥夺选民权利。

e.en: The report documented systemic {disenfranchisement} of minority communities.
e.zh: 报告记录了少数族裔社区被系统性剥夺权利的情况。

e.en: It's healthy to {disengage} from social media for a few days.
e.zh: 暂时几天不上社交媒体对身心有益。

e.en: Pull this lever to {disengage} the parking brake.
e.zh: 拉这个杆就可以松开手刹。

e.en: Students who feel ignored quickly become {disengaged} in class.
e.zh: 被忽视的学生很快就在课堂上变得心不在焉。

e.en: The driver {disengaged} the autopilot when traffic got heavy.
e.zh: 车流变密时，司机关闭了自动驾驶功能。

e.en: Employee {disengagement} is costing the company millions each year.
e.zh: 员工的消极怠工每年让公司损失数百万。

e.en: The treaty calls for gradual military {disengagement} along the border.
e.zh: 条约要求边境军队逐步脱离接触。

disentangle.t: v. 解开；理清；摆脱纠缠

e.en: It took an hour to {disentangle} the headphone wires.
e.zh: 花了一个小时才把耳机线理顺。

e.en: Lawyers worked to {disentangle} the complicated business agreement.
e.zh: 律师们努力理清这份复杂的商业协议。

disentitle.t: v. 取消权利；使丧失资格

e.en: Missing the deadline may {disentitle} you to a refund.
e.zh: 错过期限可能会使您失去退款资格。

e.en: Breaking the rules can {disentitle} a player from prize money.
e.zh: 违反规则可能让选手失去领取奖金的资格。

e.en: The sudden news created a {disequilibrium} in global markets.
e.zh: 这条突发新闻让全球市场陷入失衡。

e.en: Inner ear problems can cause dizziness and {disequilibrium}.
e.zh: 内耳问题会引起头晕和身体失衡。

disestablish.t: v. 废除（某机构）的法定地位

e.en: Some politicians want to {disestablish} the official state church.
e.zh: 一些政客希望取消国教的官方地位。

e.en: The reforms aim to {disestablish} outdated bureaucratic systems.
e.zh: 改革旨在废除过时的官僚体系。

disestablishment.t: n. 废除国教；取消官方地位

e.en: The {disestablishment} of the church sparked nationwide debate.
e.zh: 教会与国家分离的提议引发了全国性辩论。

e.en: Activists pushed for the {disestablishment} of the old monopoly.
e.zh: 活动人士推动废除这个旧的垄断机构。

disfavor.t:
n. 不赞成；失宠
v. 不喜欢

e.en: That marketing strategy quickly fell into {disfavor} with management.
e.zh: 那种营销策略很快就不再受到管理层的青睐。

e.en: The minister looked at the proposal with clear {disfavor}.
e.zh: 部长以明显不悦的神情看着这份提案。

disfavored.t: adj. 不受欢迎的；失宠的

e.en: Loud patterns are currently {disfavored} in office fashion.
e.zh: 花哨的图案目前在职场穿搭中并不受欢迎。

e.en: That theory has been {disfavored} by recent research findings.
e.zh: 近期的研究结果让那种理论失去了认可。

disfavour.t: n. 不赞成；失宠（英式拼写）

e.en: The proposal met with general {disfavour} among the committee.
e.zh: 该提案在委员会中普遍不受待见。

e.en: His remarks earned him the {disfavour} of senior colleagues.
e.zh: 他的言论让他失去了资深同事的好感。

e.en: Graffiti tags {disfigure} the historic walls of the old city.
e.zh: 涂鸦把老城的古墙弄得面目全非。

e.en: The fire could {disfigure} him for life without quick treatment.
e.zh: 如果不及时治疗，那场火可能会让他终身毁容。

disfigured.t: adj. 容貌受损的；被损毁的

e.en: The accident left her {disfigured}, but her spirit stayed strong.
e.zh: 事故让她容貌受损，但她依然坚强。

e.en: Vandals {disfigured} the statue with red paint last night.
e.zh: 昨晚破坏者用红漆毁损了那座雕像。

e.en: Modern surgery can reduce the {disfigurement} caused by burns.
e.zh: 现代外科手术能减轻烧伤造成的毁容。

e.en: The charity supports children living with facial {disfigurement}.
e.zh: 该慈善机构帮助面部毁损的儿童。

e.en: She received treatment for the {disfiguring} scar on her cheek.
e.zh: 她接受了治疗，去除脸颊上那道难看的疤痕。

e.en: The disease is rare but often {disfiguring} without early care.
e.zh: 这种病很罕见，但若不及早治疗常会致人毁容。

disfranchise.t: v. 剥夺选举权或公民权

e.en: The court ruled the law would {disfranchise} too many voters.
e.zh: 法院裁定该法律将剥夺过多选民的投票权。

e.en: Critics warned the policy would {disfranchise} immigrant communities.
e.zh: 批评人士警告该政策会剥夺移民社区的选举权。

disgorge.t: v. 大量排出；被迫交出

e.en: The bus stopped to {disgorge} a crowd of tourists downtown.
e.zh: 巴士在市中心停下，吐出一大群游客。

e.en: The court ordered the company to {disgorge} its illegal profits.
e.zh: 法院命令该公司交出非法所得。

disgrace.t:
n. 耻辱；丢脸
v. 使蒙羞

e.en: The scandal brought {disgrace} to the entire family.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻让全家人蒙羞。

e.en: He resigned in {disgrace} after the investigation went public.
e.zh: 调查曝光后，他在耻辱中辞职。

disgraced.t: adj. 名誉扫地的；失势的

e.en: The {disgraced} senator resigned after the corruption scandal broke.
e.zh: 那位名誉扫地的参议员在腐败丑闻曝光后辞职了。

e.en: He felt {disgraced} when his cheating was exposed online.
e.zh: 他作弊行为在网上曝光后感到颜面无存。

e.en: Their {disgraceful} behavior at the wedding shocked everyone.
e.zh: 他们在婚礼上的丢人行为让所有人都震惊了。

e.en: It's {disgraceful} how the company treats its workers.
e.zh: 这家公司对待员工的方式真是可耻。

e.en: He behaved {disgracefully} at the company holiday party.
e.zh: 他在公司年终派对上表现得丢人现眼。

e.en: The team played {disgracefully} in the championship final.
e.zh: 那支队伍在冠军决赛中表现得令人不齿。

disgraces.t:
n. 耻辱（复数）
v. 使蒙羞（第三人称单数）

e.en: His rude comment {disgraces} the entire family name.
e.zh: 他无礼的言论让整个家族蒙羞。

e.en: Cheating in exams {disgraces} both the student and school.
e.zh: 考试作弊会让学生和学校都蒙羞。

e.en: Sudden policy changes tend to {disgruntle} long-term employees.
e.zh: 突如其来的政策变动往往会让老员工心生不满。

e.en: Don't {disgruntle} your customers with hidden fees.
e.zh: 不要用隐藏收费惹恼你的顾客。

disgruntled.t: adj. 不满的；愤愤不平的

e.en: A {disgruntled} customer left a one-star review online.
e.zh: 一位不满的顾客在网上留了一星差评。

e.en: The {disgruntled} employee finally quit after being passed over.
e.zh: 那位心怀不满的员工在被忽视后终于辞职了。

e.en: There's growing {disgruntlement} among staff about the new schedule.
e.zh: 员工对新排班的不满情绪日益增长。

e.en: Her {disgruntlement} was obvious from her short replies.
e.zh: 从她简短的回复就能看出她的不悦。

disguise.t:
v. 伪装；掩饰
n. 伪装

e.en: The spy wore a clever {disguise} to enter the embassy.
e.zh: 那名间谍乔装巧妙以进入大使馆。

e.en: She tried to {disguise} her accent during the interview.
e.zh: 她试图在面试中掩饰自己的口音。

e.en: The actor {disguised} himself as a delivery driver for fun.
e.zh: 那位演员为了好玩把自己装扮成送货司机。

e.en: The phishing email was {disguised} as a bank notification.
e.zh: 那封钓鱼邮件伪装成了银行通知。

disguises.t:
v. 伪装（第三人称单数）
n. 伪装（复数）

e.en: The detective uses different {disguises} for undercover work.
e.zh: 那位侦探卧底时会使用不同的伪装。

e.en: She {disguises} her nerves with confident body language.
e.zh: 她用自信的肢体语言掩饰自己的紧张。

e.en: He's {disguising} the medicine taste with strawberry syrup.
e.zh: 他用草莓糖浆掩盖药的味道。

e.en: The app is {disguising} ads as regular news articles.
e.zh: 这款应用把广告伪装成普通新闻文章。

disgust.t:
n. 厌恶；反感
v. 使厌恶

e.en: She looked at the moldy bread with obvious {disgust}.
e.zh: 她看着发霉的面包,脸上写满了厌恶。

e.en: Some viral videos {disgust} more people than they entertain.
e.zh: 有些热门视频令人反感的程度远超娱乐价值。

e.en: Fans were {disgusted} by the team's unsportsmanlike conduct.
e.zh: 球迷们对球队不讲体育道德的行为感到厌恶。

e.en: She felt {disgusted} after reading the hateful comments.
e.zh: 看完那些恶毒评论后,她感到非常恶心。

e.en: He pushed the plate away {disgustedly} after one bite.
e.zh: 他咬了一口就嫌恶地把盘子推开了。

e.en: She shook her head {disgustedly} at the news report.
e.zh: 她看着新闻报道厌恶地摇了摇头。

disgusting.t: adj. 令人作呕的；讨厌的

e.en: That moldy leftover in the fridge smells absolutely {disgusting}.
e.zh: 冰箱里那块发霉的剩菜闻起来太恶心了。

e.en: It's {disgusting} how some people litter in public parks.
e.zh: 有些人在公园乱扔垃圾,真令人作呕。

e.en: The kitchen floor was {disgustingly} sticky after the party.
e.zh: 派对结束后厨房地板黏得令人作呕。

e.en: He's {disgustingly} rich but never tips his servers.
e.zh: 他富得流油,却从不给服务员小费。

dish.t:
n. 盘子；菜肴
v. 盛于盘中

e.en: This pasta {dish} is the restaurant's most popular item.
e.zh: 这道意面是这家餐厅最受欢迎的菜品。

e.en: Could you wash that dirty {dish} in the sink?
e.zh: 你能把水槽里那个脏盘子洗了吗?

e.en: She answered the door in casual {dishabille}, slightly embarrassed.
e.zh: 她衣冠不整地去开门,有些尴尬。

e.en: The painting depicts a noblewoman in elegant {dishabille}.
e.zh: 这幅画描绘了一位贵妇人慵懒的居家装扮。

disharmonious.t: adj. 不和谐的；不协调的

e.en: The team meeting felt {disharmonious} after the budget argument.
e.zh: 预算争论后,团队会议气氛显得很不和谐。

e.en: Those clashing colors create a {disharmonious} look on screen.
e.zh: 那些冲突的颜色在屏幕上显得很不协调。

e.en: There's noticeable {disharmony} between the two co-founders lately.
e.zh: 两位联合创始人最近之间的不和很明显。

e.en: Office {disharmony} can seriously hurt overall team productivity.
e.zh: 办公室的不和会严重损害整个团队的生产力。

e.en: Replace your {dishcloth} weekly to avoid spreading bacteria.
e.zh: 每周更换抹布,以避免细菌滋生。

e.en: She wiped the counter with a damp {dishcloth}.
e.zh: 她用一块湿抹布擦了擦台面。

e.en: Don't let one rejection {dishearten} your job search.
e.zh: 别让一次拒绝就让你的求职之路灰心丧气。

e.en: Negative comments online can {dishearten} new content creators.
e.zh: 网上的负面评论会让新晋创作者意志消沉。

e.en: She felt {disheartened} after failing the driving test again.
e.zh: 再次没通过驾照考试后,她感到很沮丧。

e.en: The team looked {disheartened} after losing the championship.
e.zh: 输掉冠军赛后,整个队伍看起来都垂头丧气。

e.en: It's {disheartening} to see good restaurants close down.
e.zh: 看到好餐厅一家家关门真让人沮丧。

e.en: The {disheartening} report showed sales had dropped sharply.
e.zh: 那份令人沮丧的报告显示销售额大幅下滑。

dishes.t:
n. 碗碟；菜肴（复数）
v. 盛菜（第三人称单数）

e.en: Please load the {dishes} into the dishwasher after dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐后请把碗碟放进洗碗机。

e.en: The chef prepared three new {dishes} for the seasonal menu.
e.zh: 主厨为季节菜单准备了三道新菜。

e.en: The strong wind will {dishevel} your neatly styled hair.
e.zh: 强风会把你梳得整齐的头发吹得乱糟糟。

e.en: Don't {dishevel} the bed I just made up.
e.zh: 别把我刚铺好的床弄乱。

disheveled.t: adj. 头发凌乱的；不整洁的

e.en: He arrived at the meeting looking tired and {disheveled}.
e.zh: 他到会议时看起来又累又邋遢。

e.en: Her {disheveled} hair suggested she'd been sleeping moments ago.
e.zh: 她凌乱的头发说明她刚刚还在睡觉。

e.en: The reporter looked {dishevelled} after covering the storm overnight.
e.zh: 记者通宵报道暴风雨后看起来狼狈不堪。

e.en: He showed up {dishevelled}, clearly having dressed in haste.
e.zh: 他衣冠不整地出现,显然是匆忙穿好就来了。

dishevelment.t: n. 头发或衣着的凌乱

e.en: His state of {dishevelment} made colleagues worry about him.
e.zh: 他蓬头垢面的样子让同事们很为他担心。

e.en: The actor's {dishevelment} suited his struggling artist character.
e.zh: 演员邋遢的造型很符合他饰演的落魄艺术家。

e.en: Being {dishonest} in your resume can cost you the job.
e.zh: 在简历上撒谎可能会让你失去这份工作。

e.en: She refused to work with such a {dishonest} business partner.
e.zh: 她拒绝和这样不诚实的商业伙伴合作。

e.en: His small daily {dishonesties} eventually destroyed their marriage.
e.zh: 他日常的种种小谎言最终毁掉了他们的婚姻。

e.en: The audit uncovered numerous {dishonesties} in the financial reports.
e.zh: 审计发现财务报告中存在大量不诚实之处。

e.en: He {dishonestly} claimed credit for his teammate's work.
e.zh: 他不诚实地把队友的功劳据为己有。

e.en: The company {dishonestly} advertised features that didn't actually exist.
e.zh: 该公司不诚实地宣传了实际上并不存在的功能。

e.en: Workplace {dishonesty} usually gets discovered sooner or later.
e.zh: 职场上的不诚实迟早都会被发现。

e.en: She was fired for {dishonesty} on her expense reports.
e.zh: 她因在报销单上弄虚作假而被解雇。

dishonor.t:
n. 耻辱；不名誉
v. 使蒙羞

e.en: Cheating in the Olympics brings {dishonor} to your country.
e.zh: 在奥运会上作弊会给你的国家带来耻辱。

e.en: He refused to {dishonor} his late father's good name.
e.zh: 他不愿玷污已故父亲的好名声。

e.en: Lying to your teammates is a {dishonorable} thing to do.
e.zh: 对队友撒谎是一件不光彩的事。

e.en: He received a {dishonorable} discharge from the military.
e.zh: 他被军队不光彩地开除了。

e.en: The soldier was {dishonorably} discharged after the incident.
e.zh: 那名士兵在事件发生后被不光彩地除名。

e.en: He behaved {dishonorably} by abandoning his sick partner.
e.zh: 他抛弃了生病的伴侣,行为很不光彩。

dishonored.t: adj. 蒙羞的；（支票）被拒付的

e.en: The bank {dishonored} the check due to insufficient funds.
e.zh: 由于余额不足,银行拒付了那张支票。

e.en: He felt he had {dishonored} his coach by quitting early.
e.zh: 他觉得自己提前退出有负教练的期望。

dishonour.t:
n. 耻辱（英式拼写）
v. 使蒙羞

e.en: Losing the match brought no {dishonour} to the team.
e.zh: 输掉比赛并没有给球队带来耻辱。

e.en: He would never {dishonour} the family business with fraud.
e.zh: 他绝不会用欺诈玷污家族企业。

dishonourable.t: adj. 不光彩的；不诚实的

e.en: Spreading those rumors was a truly {dishonourable} thing to do.
e.zh: 散布那些谣言实在是一件不光彩的事。

e.en: The judge called his actions cowardly and {dishonourable}.
e.zh: 法官称他的行为既懦弱又卑鄙。

dishonoured.t:
adj. 蒙羞的；拒付的（支票）
v. 使蒙羞

e.en: The athlete {dishonoured} the sport by accepting bribes.
e.zh: 那名运动员接受贿赂,玷污了这项运动。

e.en: She felt {dishonoured} when her promise was made public.
e.zh: 当她的承诺被公开时,她感到颜面尽失。

e.en: Fill the {dishpan} with warm soapy water before scrubbing.
e.zh: 擦洗前先在洗碗盆里装满温肥皂水。

e.en: She soaked the greasy pots in the {dishpan} overnight.
e.zh: 她把油腻的锅放在洗碗盆里浸泡了一夜。

e.en: Throw that smelly {dishrag} in the wash immediately.
e.zh: 赶紧把那块发臭的抹布扔进洗衣机。

e.en: He wiped the spilled milk with a clean {dishrag}.
e.zh: 他用一块干净的抹布擦掉洒出来的牛奶。

e.en: Grab a clean {dishtowel} to dry these wine glasses.
e.zh: 拿块干净的抹布把这些酒杯擦干。

e.en: Her embroidered {dishtowel} was a gift from her grandmother.
e.zh: 她那块绣花擦碗布是奶奶送的礼物。

e.en: They registered for elegant {dishware} on their wedding list.
e.zh: 他们在婚礼礼物清单上登记了一套精美的餐具。

e.en: All the {dishware} is dishwasher and microwave safe.
e.zh: 所有餐具都可以放入洗碗机和微波炉使用。

e.en: Load the {dishwasher} carefully so the spray reaches everything.
e.zh: 把碗碟摆放好,这样洗碗机的水才能喷到每一件。

e.en: He worked as a {dishwasher} while attending culinary school.
e.zh: 他上烹饪学校时做过洗碗工。

e.en: Modern {dishwashers} use far less water than handwashing does.
e.zh: 现代洗碗机用水量比手洗要少得多。

e.en: The restaurant hired two new {dishwashers} for the busy season.
e.zh: 餐厅在旺季新雇了两名洗碗工。

dishwashing.t:
n. 洗碗
adj. 洗碗用的

e.en: This {dishwashing} liquid cuts grease without drying your hands.
e.zh: 这款洗洁精能去油但不会让手变干。

e.en: He hates {dishwashing} more than any other household chore.
e.zh: 他比任何家务都更讨厌洗碗。

e.en: The hotel coffee tasted like weak gray {dishwater}.
e.zh: 酒店的咖啡尝起来就像淡得发灰的洗碗水。

e.en: Pour the dirty {dishwater} down the drain, not outside.
e.zh: 把脏洗碗水倒进下水道,别倒到外面。

e.en: Her new boyfriend is genuinely {dishy} and surprisingly funny.
e.zh: 她的新男友真的很帅,而且出奇地幽默。

e.en: The lead actor in that drama is incredibly {dishy}.
e.zh: 那部剧的男主角真是帅得不行。

disillusion.t:
v. 使理想破灭
n. 幻灭

e.en: I hate to {disillusion} you, but Santa isn't real.
e.zh: 我也不想让你失望,但圣诞老人是不存在的。

e.en: The political scandal began to {disillusion} young voters everywhere.
e.zh: 这场政治丑闻开始让各地年轻选民幻想破灭。

disillusioned.t: adj. 理想破灭的；不再抱幻想的

e.en: She felt {disillusioned} after years of broken promises at work.
e.zh: 在工作中经历多年空头承诺后，她感到心灰意冷。

e.en: Many voters grew {disillusioned} with both political parties.
e.zh: 许多选民对两个政党都感到失望。

disillusioning.t:
adj. 令人幻灭的
v. 使幻灭

e.en: The internship was a {disillusioning} look at the industry.
e.zh: 那次实习让她看清了这个行业的真实面目。

e.en: Meeting the celebrity proved deeply {disillusioning} for the fan.
e.zh: 与那位明星见面让粉丝大失所望。

e.en: His {disillusionment} with startups led him to teach instead.
e.zh: 对创业的幻灭让他转而去当老师。

e.en: There is growing {disillusionment} among young employees.
e.zh: 年轻员工中弥漫着越来越多的幻灭感。

e.en: Life brings small {disillusionments} that gradually shape who we are.
e.zh: 生活中的种种小幻灭逐渐塑造了我们。

e.en: Her diary recorded the {disillusionments} of her first year abroad.
e.zh: 她的日记记录了出国第一年的种种幻灭。

disillusions.t:
v. 使幻灭
n. 幻灭

e.en: Working in politics quickly {disillusions} most idealistic graduates.
e.zh: 从政很快就让大多数理想化的毕业生看清现实。

e.en: Reality often {disillusions} those who expect overnight success.
e.zh: 现实常常让指望一夜成功的人幻灭。

disincentive.t: n. 抑制因素；起阻碍作用的事物

e.en: High taxes can act as a {disincentive} to small businesses.
e.zh: 高税收可能成为小企业的一种抑制因素。

e.en: The long commute is a real {disincentive} to taking the job.
e.zh: 漫长的通勤让人不太愿意接受这份工作。

e.en: He showed a clear {disinclination} to discuss his past.
e.zh: 他明显不愿意谈论自己的过去。

e.en: Her {disinclination} to travel surprised her friends.
e.zh: 她不爱旅行这一点让朋友们感到意外。

disinclined.t: adj. 不愿意的；不感兴趣的

e.en: I'm {disinclined} to accept the offer without more details.
e.zh: 在没有更多细节前，我不太愿意接受这个提议。

e.en: He felt {disinclined} to argue with his boss again.
e.zh: 他不太想再和老板争论了。

e.en: Please {disinfect} the kitchen counter before preparing food.
e.zh: 备餐前请给厨房台面消毒。

e.en: Hospitals {disinfect} every room between patients.
e.zh: 医院在每位病人之间都会对房间消毒。

disinfectant.t:
n. 消毒剂
adj. 消毒的

e.en: Wipe the door handles with {disinfectant} every morning.
e.zh: 每天早上用消毒剂擦一遍门把手。

e.en: This spray is a powerful {disinfectant} against most viruses.
e.zh: 这款喷雾对大多数病毒都有很强的消毒效果。

e.en: Regular {disinfection} of toys helps prevent illness in daycare.
e.zh: 定期对玩具消毒有助于预防托儿所的疾病传播。

e.en: The hospital follows strict {disinfection} protocols.
e.zh: 这家医院严格执行消毒规程。

e.en: The central bank welcomed signs of gradual {disinflation}.
e.zh: 央行对通胀逐渐放缓的迹象表示欢迎。

e.en: Economists debated whether {disinflation} would lead to recession.
e.zh: 经济学家就通胀下行是否会引发衰退展开了辩论。

disinformation.t: n. 虚假信息；蓄意散布的假情报

e.en: Social media platforms struggle to contain political {disinformation}.
e.zh: 社交媒体平台难以遏制政治虚假信息的传播。

e.en: The article exposed a coordinated {disinformation} campaign online.
e.zh: 这篇文章揭露了一场有组织的网络虚假信息运动。

e.en: It's {disingenuous} to claim you didn't see the email.
e.zh: 声称没看到那封邮件未免太虚伪了。

e.en: His apology sounded {disingenuous} to everyone in the meeting.
e.zh: 在场的人都觉得他的道歉很假。

e.en: The CEO {disingenuously} claimed not to know about the layoffs.
e.zh: 那位首席执行官假惺惺地声称对裁员一事毫不知情。

e.en: She smiled {disingenuously} as she dodged the reporter's question.
e.zh: 她虚伪地笑着避开了记者的问题。

e.en: Voters were tired of the politician's obvious {disingenuousness}.
e.zh: 选民们对那位政客明显的虚伪感到厌倦。

e.en: Her {disingenuousness} eventually cost her the team's trust.
e.zh: 她的虚伪最终让她失去了团队的信任。

e.en: He threatened to {disinherit} his son after the argument.
e.zh: 那次争吵后，他威胁要剥夺儿子的继承权。

e.en: Few parents actually {disinherit} their children over lifestyle choices.
e.zh: 很少有父母真的会因为生活方式而剥夺子女的继承权。

disinherited.t:
adj. 被剥夺继承权的
v. 剥夺继承权

e.en: She was {disinherited} after marrying against her family's wishes.
e.zh: 她因违背家人意愿结婚而被剥夺了继承权。

e.en: The {disinherited} brother sued to challenge the will.
e.zh: 那位被剥夺继承权的兄弟提起诉讼挑战遗嘱。

e.en: Alcohol causes {disinhibition}, which is why people say more than they mean.
e.zh: 酒精会让人放松抑制，所以人们常会说漏嘴。

e.en: Online {disinhibition} explains why strangers post such harsh comments.
e.zh: 网络上的去抑制效应解释了陌生人为何会发那么刻薄的评论。

e.en: The old paperback began to {disintegrate} after years in storage.
e.zh: 那本旧平装书存放多年后开始散架。

e.en: Their friendship started to {disintegrate} once trust was broken.
e.zh: 信任一旦破裂，他们的友谊也开始瓦解。

disintegrated.t:
adj. 瓦解的
v. 崩解

e.en: The spacecraft {disintegrated} on reentry into the atmosphere.
e.zh: 航天器在重返大气层时解体了。

e.en: Their marriage {disintegrated} slowly over many years.
e.zh: 他们的婚姻在多年里慢慢崩溃了。

disintegrating.t:
adj. 正在崩解的
v. 瓦解

e.en: The {disintegrating} bridge was finally closed for safety reasons.
e.zh: 那座日益破败的桥最终因安全原因被关闭。

e.en: Reporters described a {disintegrating} ceasefire in the region.
e.zh: 记者们描述了该地区正在瓦解的停火协议。

e.en: The film documents the {disintegration} of a once-loving family.
e.zh: 这部电影记录了一个昔日恩爱家庭的破裂。

e.en: Engineers worried about the slow {disintegration} of the dam's wall.
e.zh: 工程师们担心水坝坝体的缓慢崩解。

e.en: Authorities had to {disinter} the body for further forensic tests.
e.zh: 当局不得不将尸体掘出以进行进一步的法医检验。

e.en: The historian hoped to {disinter} forgotten letters from the archive.
e.zh: 那位历史学家希望从档案中挖出被遗忘的信件。

e.en: He showed complete {disinterest} in the new project.
e.zh: 他对这个新项目完全不感兴趣。

e.en: Her sudden {disinterest} in football puzzled her teammates.
e.zh: 她突然对足球失去兴趣让队友们感到困惑。

disinterested.t: adj. 公正无私的；不感兴趣的

e.en: We need a {disinterested} third party to mediate the dispute.
e.zh: 我们需要一个公正中立的第三方来调解纠纷。

e.en: A judge must remain {disinterested} throughout the trial.
e.zh: 法官在整个审判过程中必须保持中立。

disinterestedly.t: adv. 无私地；不偏不倚地

e.en: The referee acted {disinterestedly}, ignoring pressure from both sides.
e.zh: 裁判公正地履行职责，不受双方压力影响。

e.en: She reviewed the contract {disinterestedly} despite knowing the parties.
e.zh: 尽管认识双方当事人，她仍公正地审阅了合同。

e.en: A good auditor's {disinterestedness} protects the integrity of the report.
e.zh: 优秀审计师的中立无私维护了报告的公信力。

e.en: Scientists value {disinterestedness} when reviewing each other's work.
e.zh: 科学家在互相评审工作时看重客观无私的态度。

e.en: Years of {disinvestment} left the neighborhood without basic services.
e.zh: 多年的撤资让这个社区连基本服务都没有了。

e.en: The fund announced {disinvestment} from fossil fuel companies.
e.zh: 该基金宣布从化石燃料公司撤资。

e.en: The mechanic had to {disjoin} the two pipes to fix the leak.
e.zh: 机械师不得不把两根管子拆开才能修好漏点。

e.en: You can {disjoin} the panels by loosening these four screws.
e.zh: 拧松这四颗螺丝就能把面板拆开。

disjoint.t:
v. 使脱节
adj. 不相交的

e.en: In math class we learned that two sets can be {disjoint}.
e.zh: 数学课上我们学到两个集合可以是不相交的。

e.en: The two teams worked on completely {disjoint} parts of the system.
e.zh: 这两个团队负责系统中完全不相关的部分。

e.en: His speech was {disjointed} and hard to follow.
e.zh: 他的发言很零散，很难听明白。

e.en: The film felt {disjointed}, jumping between unrelated scenes.
e.zh: 这部电影显得支离破碎，在毫不相关的场景间跳跃。

e.en: The two arguments felt entirely {disjunct} from each other.
e.zh: 这两个论点彼此完全脱节。

e.en: Researchers found a {disjunct} population of the rare frog.
e.zh: 研究人员发现了这种稀有青蛙的一个孤立种群。

e.en: There's a clear {disjunction} between his words and actions.
e.zh: 他的言辞和行为之间存在明显的脱节。

e.en: In logic, a {disjunction} is true if either statement holds.
e.zh: 在逻辑学中，只要任一陈述成立，析取式就为真。

disjunctive.t: adj. 分离的；转折的（语法）

e.en: The word "or" usually signals a {disjunctive} relationship.
e.zh: "or" 这个词通常表示一种选择关系。

e.en: The contract used {disjunctive} language to list possible outcomes.
e.zh: 合同使用选择性表述列出了各种可能的结果。

e.en: There's a growing {disjuncture} between management and frontline staff.
e.zh: 管理层和一线员工之间的脱节日益明显。

e.en: The report highlighted a {disjuncture} between policy and practice.
e.zh: 报告指出了政策与实践之间的脱节。

e.en: My laptop's hard {disk} is almost full again.
e.zh: 我笔记本的硬盘又快满了。

e.en: The dentist showed me an X-ray of the herniated {disk}.
e.zh: 牙医给我看了椎间盘突出的 X 光片。

e.en: He found an old {diskette} with files from the 1990s.
e.zh: 他找到一张装着九十年代文件的旧软盘。

e.en: No modern computer can read this 3.5-inch {diskette} anymore.
e.zh: 现代电脑已经无法读取这种 3.5 英寸软盘了。

disks.t: n. 磁盘；圆盘（disk 的复数）

e.en: The server uses six {disks} in a RAID configuration.
e.zh: 这台服务器使用六块硬盘组成 RAID 阵列。

e.en: She arranged the ceramic {disks} in a neat pattern.
e.zh: 她把陶瓷圆片整齐地排成一个图案。

dislike.t:
v. 不喜欢
n. 反感

e.en: I {dislike} crowded subway stations during rush hour.
e.zh: 我讨厌高峰时段挤满人的地铁站。

e.en: She made no effort to hide her {dislike} of the new policy.
e.zh: 她毫不掩饰对新政策的厌恶。

disliked.t:
v. 不喜欢（过去式）
adj. 不受欢迎的

e.en: He always {disliked} group projects in school.
e.zh: 他在学校里一直不喜欢小组作业。

e.en: The {disliked} manager was finally transferred to another team.
e.zh: 那位不受欢迎的经理终于被调到了别的团队。

dislikes.t:
v. 不喜欢（第三人称单数）
n. 厌恶之事

e.en: My cat clearly {dislikes} strangers entering the apartment.
e.zh: 我家猫显然不喜欢陌生人进屋。

e.en: Tell me about your food {dislikes} before I order dinner.
e.zh: 在我点晚餐前，告诉我你不喜欢吃什么。

e.en: Despite {disliking} mornings, she takes a 6 a.m. yoga class.
e.zh: 尽管讨厌早晨，她还是去上早上六点的瑜伽课。

e.en: He kept {disliking} every restaurant his friends suggested.
e.zh: 朋友们推荐的每家餐厅他都看不上。

e.en: Be careful not to {dislocate} your shoulder while lifting weights.
e.zh: 举重时小心别把肩膀脱臼了。

e.en: Sudden policy changes can {dislocate} entire local economies.
e.zh: 政策的突然变化可能会扰乱整个地方经济。

dislocated.t:
adj. 脱臼的；错位的
v. 使脱臼（过去式）

e.en: He {dislocated} his knee in the second half of the match.
e.zh: 他在下半场比赛中把膝盖弄脱臼了。

e.en: The war left thousands of families {dislocated} from their homes.
e.zh: 战争使成千上万的家庭流离失所。

e.en: The doctor confirmed a partial {dislocation} of her elbow.
e.zh: 医生确认她的肘部出现部分脱位。

e.en: Automation has caused widespread economic {dislocation} in some towns.
e.zh: 自动化在一些城镇造成了广泛的经济动荡。

e.en: Try to {dislodge} the food stuck between your teeth with floss.
e.zh: 试着用牙线把卡在牙缝里的食物弄出来。

e.en: The challenger couldn't {dislodge} the champion from first place.
e.zh: 挑战者未能把卫冕冠军从第一的位置上拉下来。

e.en: Heavy rain {dislodged} several rocks from the cliff face.
e.zh: 大雨把崖壁上的几块石头冲了下来。

e.en: The startup eventually {dislodged} the long-time market leader.
e.zh: 这家初创公司最终把长期的市场领导者挤下了宝座。

dislodges.t: v. 驱离；挪开（第三人称单数）

e.en: A strong cough sometimes {dislodges} whatever is stuck in your throat.
e.zh: 用力咳嗽有时能把卡在喉咙里的东西咳出来。

e.en: The new app {dislodges} older tools from users' home screens.
e.zh: 这款新应用把旧工具从用户的主屏幕上挤了下去。

dislodging.t: v. 驱离；挪开（现在分词）

e.en: The plumber spent an hour {dislodging} hair from the drain.
e.zh: 水管工花了一个小时把头发从排水口里弄出来。

e.en: {Dislodging} an incumbent senator is notoriously difficult.
e.zh: 想把在任参议员拉下马是出了名的难。

e.en: He was fired for being {disloyal} to the company.
e.zh: 他因对公司不忠而被解雇。

e.en: Sharing client secrets is a {disloyal} act.
e.zh: 泄露客户机密是不忠的行为。

e.en: The manager punished any sign of {disloyalty} harshly.
e.zh: 经理严厉惩罚任何不忠的迹象。

e.en: Her {disloyalty} to the team shocked everyone.
e.zh: 她对团队的不忠让所有人震惊。

e.en: Sales numbers this quarter were absolutely {dismal}.
e.zh: 本季度的销售数据糟糕透了。

e.en: The weather has been cold and {dismal} all week.
e.zh: 整个星期天气都又冷又阴沉。

e.en: The new product performed {dismally} in early reviews.
e.zh: 新产品在早期评测中表现得一塌糊涂。

e.en: He failed {dismally} on his driving test.
e.zh: 他驾照考试惨败。

e.en: Engineers had to {dismantle} the engine to find the leak.
e.zh: 工程师们不得不拆解引擎才能找到漏点。

e.en: Activists want to {dismantle} the outdated tax system.
e.zh: 活动人士希望废除过时的税收制度。

dismantled.t:
v. 拆除（过去式）
adj. 被拆除的

e.en: They {dismantled} the old factory piece by piece.
e.zh: 他们一块一块地拆掉了那座旧工厂。

e.en: The committee {dismantled} several outdated regulations.
e.zh: 委员会废除了几项过时的规定。

e.en: The treaty requires the {dismantlement} of all nuclear warheads.
e.zh: 条约要求拆除所有核弹头。

e.en: Workers oversaw the careful {dismantlement} of the bridge.
e.zh: 工人们监督着大桥的仔细拆除。

dismantling.t:
v. 拆除（现在分词）
n. 拆卸

e.en: They are {dismantling} the stage after the concert.
e.zh: 演唱会结束后他们正在拆台。

e.en: The new CEO began {dismantling} bureaucratic layers immediately.
e.zh: 新任CEO立刻着手拆除官僚层级。

dismay.t:
n. 沮丧；惊愕
v. 使沮丧

e.en: To my {dismay}, the flight was cancelled again.
e.zh: 令我沮丧的是,航班又被取消了。

e.en: The news of the layoffs filled staff with {dismay}.
e.zh: 裁员的消息让员工们倍感沮丧。

e.en: Fans were {dismayed} by the team's poor performance.
e.zh: 球迷们对球队糟糕的表现感到沮丧。

e.en: She looked {dismayed} when she saw the bill.
e.zh: 看到账单时她一脸沮丧。

dismaying.t: adj. 令人沮丧的；令人惊愕的

e.en: The survey results were quite {dismaying} to leadership.
e.zh: 调查结果让领导层颇为沮丧。

e.en: It's {dismaying} how quickly prices have risen.
e.zh: 物价上涨之快令人沮丧。

e.en: The bug reappeared {dismayingly} soon after the patch.
e.zh: 补丁发布后,bug很快又出现,令人沮丧。

e.en: Turnout was {dismayingly} low at the public meeting.
e.zh: 公众会议的出席率低得令人沮丧。

dismays.t: v. 使沮丧（第三人称单数）

e.en: It {dismays} me to see so much food wasted.
e.zh: 看到这么多食物被浪费让我很沮丧。

e.en: The lack of progress {dismays} the entire team.
e.zh: 毫无进展让整个团队都很失望。

e.en: Critics fear the merger will {dismember} the smaller firm.
e.zh: 批评者担心合并会肢解这家小公司。

e.en: The killer tried to {dismember} the evidence to hide it.
e.zh: 凶手试图肢解证据以掩盖罪行。

dismembered.t:
v. 肢解（过去式）
adj. 被肢解的

e.en: Investigators discovered a {dismembered} mannequin in the warehouse.
e.zh: 调查员在仓库里发现了一具被拆解的人体模型。

e.en: The empire was eventually {dismembered} by rival powers.
e.zh: 那个帝国最终被敌对势力分割瓜分。

e.en: The insurance covers accidental {dismemberment} on the job.
e.zh: 该保险覆盖工作中意外造成的肢体损伤。

e.en: Historians wrote about the {dismemberment} of the old kingdom.
e.zh: 历史学家记述了旧王国的瓜分。

dismiss.t: v. 驳回；解雇；不予理会

e.en: Don't {dismiss} her ideas just because she's new.
e.zh: 不要因为她是新人就否定她的想法。

e.en: The judge will {dismiss} the case for lack of evidence.
e.zh: 由于证据不足,法官将驳回此案。

e.en: His sudden {dismissal} from the company shocked colleagues.
e.zh: 他突然被公司解雇让同事们震惊。

e.en: The court ordered the {dismissal} of all charges.
e.zh: 法院下令撤销所有指控。

e.en: The wave of {dismissals} hit the engineering team hardest.
e.zh: 这波解雇潮对工程团队打击最大。

e.en: Several wrongful {dismissals} ended up in court last year.
e.zh: 去年有几起不当解雇案进入了法庭。

e.en: The teacher {dismissed} the class ten minutes early.
e.zh: 老师提前十分钟下课了。

e.en: Critics initially {dismissed} the app as a gimmick.
e.zh: 评论家起初把这款应用视为噱头而不予理会。

dismisses.t: v. 驳回；解雇（第三人称单数）

e.en: He often {dismisses} feedback without really considering it.
e.zh: 他经常不加思考就否定反馈意见。

e.en: The CEO {dismisses} rumors of an upcoming acquisition.
e.zh: CEO否认了即将进行收购的传言。

dismissing.t: v. 驳回；解雇（现在分词）

e.en: Stop {dismissing} concerns about user privacy so quickly.
e.zh: 别再这么轻易地否定用户对隐私的担忧了。

e.en: The judge is {dismissing} the lawsuit on procedural grounds.
e.zh: 法官以程序问题为由驳回了诉讼。

e.en: His {dismissive} tone really annoyed the junior staff.
e.zh: 他不屑一顾的语气让年轻员工很恼火。

e.en: She gave a {dismissive} wave and walked away.
e.zh: 她不屑地挥了挥手就走开了。

e.en: He shrugged {dismissively} when asked about the complaints.
e.zh: 被问及那些投诉时,他不屑地耸了耸肩。

e.en: She {dismissively} closed the tab without reading further.
e.zh: 她不耐烦地关掉了标签页,没再继续看。

dismount.t:
v. 下马；卸下
n. 下马动作

e.en: Riders must {dismount} before crossing the bridge.
e.zh: 骑车者过桥前必须下车。

e.en: The gymnast nailed her {dismount} from the beam.
e.zh: 那位体操运动员完成了平衡木的下法,稳稳落地。

e.en: We're taking the kids to {Disney} World this summer.
e.zh: 今年夏天我们要带孩子去迪士尼乐园。

e.en: {Disney} just announced three new streaming series.
e.zh: 迪士尼刚刚宣布了三部新的流媒体剧集。

e.en: The hotel had a {Disneyesque} fairy-tale facade.
e.zh: 那家酒店有着迪士尼风格的童话外观。

e.en: Critics called the new park overly {Disneyesque}.
e.zh: 评论家称新公园过于迪士尼化。

e.en: We waited two hours for a ride at {Disneyland}.
e.zh: 我们在迪士尼乐园排了两小时才玩到一个项目。

e.en: Tokyo {Disneyland} is one of the most visited parks.
e.zh: 东京迪士尼乐园是游客最多的乐园之一。

e.en: The protest was a clear act of civil {disobedience}.
e.zh: 那次抗议是明显的公民不服从行为。

e.en: Repeated {disobedience} will result in detention.
e.zh: 屡次违纪将被留校察看。

e.en: The puppy is cute but extremely {disobedient}.
e.zh: 这只小狗很可爱,但极不听话。

e.en: He was a {disobedient} student who never did homework.
e.zh: 他是个不守规矩、从不做作业的学生。

e.en: Soldiers who {disobey} direct orders face court-martial.
e.zh: 违抗直接命令的士兵将面临军事法庭审判。

e.en: Don't {disobey} the safety rules in the lab.
e.zh: 不要违反实验室的安全规定。

disorder.t:
n. 紊乱；失调（疾病）
v. 使混乱

e.en: She was diagnosed with an anxiety {disorder} last year.
e.zh: 她去年被诊断出焦虑症。

e.en: The room was in complete {disorder} after the party.
e.zh: 派对结束后房间一片狼藉。

e.en: His desk looked {disordered}, with papers scattered everywhere.
e.zh: 他的桌子凌乱不堪,纸张散落一地。

e.en: She struggled with {disordered} eating throughout college.
e.zh: 她在大学期间一直与饮食失调作斗争。

disorderly.t: adj. 混乱的；扰乱治安的

e.en: He was arrested for {disorderly} conduct outside the bar.
e.zh: 他因在酒吧外行为不检被逮捕。

e.en: The crowd became {disorderly} when the concert was canceled.
e.zh: 演唱会取消后人群变得骚乱起来。

e.en: Sleep {disorders} affect millions of adults worldwide.
e.zh: 睡眠障碍影响着全球数百万成年人。

e.en: The clinic specializes in treating digestive {disorders}.
e.zh: 这家诊所专门治疗消化系统疾病。

e.en: The project failed largely due to sheer {disorganisation}.
e.zh: 这个项目失败,很大程度上是因为彻底的混乱无序。

e.en: Customers complained about the {disorganisation} at the front desk.
e.zh: 顾客抱怨前台管理混乱。

e.en: Last-minute changes can {disorganise} the entire schedule.
e.zh: 最后一刻的变动会打乱整个日程。

e.en: Don't let small interruptions {disorganise} your workflow.
e.zh: 别让小的干扰打乱你的工作流程。

e.en: His notes were so {disorganised} that nobody could follow them.
e.zh: 他的笔记乱七八糟,没人能看懂。

e.en: The event felt rushed and {disorganised}.
e.zh: 这场活动感觉仓促而混乱。

e.en: The startup suffered from chronic {disorganization} in its early days.
e.zh: 这家初创公司早期一直深陷管理混乱。

e.en: Customers noticed the {disorganization} of the warehouse immediately.
e.zh: 顾客一眼就看出仓库管理混乱。

e.en: A surprise audit can totally {disorganize} a small office.
e.zh: 突击审计会彻底打乱一个小办公室的运转。

e.en: Don't let one bad meeting {disorganize} your week.
e.zh: 别因为一次糟糕的会议就打乱你的整周。

disorganized.t: adj. 杂乱无章的；没条理的

e.en: My closet is so {disorganized} I can't find anything.
e.zh: 我的衣柜乱得我什么都找不到。

e.en: The team felt {disorganized} without a clear leader.
e.zh: 没有明确的领导,团队感觉混乱无序。

disorient.t: v. 使迷失方向；使困惑

e.en: Bright flashing lights can {disorient} the driver at night.
e.zh: 夜间闪烁的强光会让驾驶员失去方向感。

e.en: Sudden time-zone changes really {disorient} my sleep schedule.
e.zh: 突然换时区会彻底打乱我的作息。

disorientate.t: v. 使迷失方向（英式拼写）

e.en: Loud noises can {disorientate} someone with hearing loss.
e.zh: 嘈杂声会让听力受损的人迷失方向。

e.en: The thick fog began to {disorientate} the hikers.
e.zh: 浓雾开始让徒步者辨不清方向。

disorientated.t: adj. 迷失方向的；晕头转向的

e.en: She felt {disorientated} after waking from the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后醒来,她感到晕头转向。

e.en: The patient was clearly {disorientated} when paramedics arrived.
e.zh: 急救人员到达时,病人明显神志不清。

e.en: The VR game was thrilling but a bit {disorientating}.
e.zh: 那款VR游戏很刺激,但有点让人晕头转向。

e.en: Working night shifts can be deeply {disorientating} at first.
e.zh: 刚开始上夜班会让人非常没有方向感。

e.en: Jet lag often causes {disorientation} for the first few days.
e.zh: 时差通常会让人在头几天里晕头转向。

e.en: Patients reported dizziness and {disorientation} after the medication.
e.zh: 病人服药后报告出现头晕和定向障碍。

disoriented.t: adj. 迷失方向的；困惑的

e.en: He felt {disoriented} after the concussion last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末脑震荡后他感觉头脑混乱。

e.en: Tourists often look {disoriented} in the subway maze.
e.zh: 游客在地铁迷宫里常常一脸茫然。

e.en: The mirrored hallway was both beautiful and {disorienting}.
e.zh: 那条镜面走廊既美丽又让人迷失方向。

e.en: Switching from remote to office work was {disorienting}.
e.zh: 从远程办公转回办公室让人感觉很不适应。

disown.t: v. 与……断绝关系；不认（亲属）

e.en: His parents threatened to {disown} him over the scandal.
e.zh: 由于这桩丑闻,他的父母威胁要与他断绝关系。

e.en: The author tried to {disown} her early novels.
e.zh: 那位作家试图与她早期的小说划清界限。

e.en: Don't {disparage} colleagues behind their backs.
e.zh: 不要在同事背后贬低他们。

e.en: Critics often {disparage} blockbuster films as shallow.
e.zh: 评论家常贬低大片肤浅。

e.en: Critics {disparaged} the film for its weak ending.
e.zh: 评论家批评这部电影结尾乏力。

e.en: He {disparaged} her efforts in front of the whole team.
e.zh: 他当着全队的面贬低她的努力。

e.en: Her constant {disparagement} of coworkers hurt team morale.
e.zh: 她不断贬低同事，损害了团队士气。

e.en: The review contained nothing but {disparagement} of the author.
e.zh: 那篇评论里全是对作者的贬损。

e.en: His public {disparagements} of rivals damaged his reputation.
e.zh: 他对对手的公开贬损损害了自己的名声。

e.en: Ignore the petty {disparagements} from anonymous online accounts.
e.zh: 别理会匿名网友那些琐碎的贬低之词。

disparages.t: v. 贬低（第三人称单数）

e.en: He often {disparages} ideas before fully understanding them.
e.zh: 他常常没听完别人的想法就加以贬低。

e.en: The article {disparages} small startups as unserious players.
e.zh: 这篇文章贬低小型创业公司，说它们不够专业。

e.en: She made {disparaging} remarks about his cooking skills.
e.zh: 她对他的厨艺说了些贬低的话。

e.en: Avoid {disparaging} comments in your performance review.
e.zh: 在绩效评估中要避免使用贬低性的言辞。

e.en: He spoke {disparagingly} of his old company on the podcast.
e.zh: 他在播客中贬低地谈论自己的前公司。

e.en: She smiled {disparagingly} at the amateur attempt.
e.zh: 她带着轻蔑的笑容看着那业余的尝试。

disparate.t: adj. 迥然不同的；无共同点的

e.en: The team brought together {disparate} skills and backgrounds.
e.zh: 团队汇集了截然不同的技能与背景。

e.en: The app pulls data from {disparate} sources into one dashboard.
e.zh: 这款应用将各种来源的数据汇总到一个仪表盘上。

e.en: There's a huge {disparity} in pay between the two roles.
e.zh: 这两个岗位的薪酬差距非常大。

e.en: The report highlights the {disparity} in healthcare access.
e.zh: 报告指出了医疗服务获取上的不平等。

e.en: The judge ruled with admirable {dispassion}.
e.zh: 法官以令人钦佩的冷静作出了裁决。

e.en: She analyzed the breakup with surprising {dispassion}.
e.zh: 她出人意料地冷静分析了这段感情的结束。

dispassionate.t: adj. 冷静的；不带偏见的

e.en: We need a {dispassionate} review of the evidence.
e.zh: 我们需要对证据进行冷静客观的审视。

e.en: His {dispassionate} tone helped calm the heated debate.
e.zh: 他平静的语气让激烈的辩论冷静下来。

e.en: She described the accident {dispassionately} to police.
e.zh: 她平静地向警方描述了事故经过。

e.en: Try to evaluate the offer {dispassionately} before deciding.
e.zh: 在做决定前，试着冷静客观地评估这份报价。

dispatch.t:
v. 派遣；发送
n. 急件；调度

e.en: We {dispatch} orders within 24 hours of payment.
e.zh: 我们在付款后24小时内发货。

e.en: The {dispatch} from the front line shocked the newsroom.
e.zh: 来自前线的电讯报道震惊了新闻编辑室。

e.en: The {dispatcher} routed the nearest ambulance to the scene.
e.zh: 调度员把最近的救护车派往现场。

e.en: A taxi {dispatcher} answered within seconds of the call.
e.zh: 出租车调度员在电话接通后几秒就应答了。

dispel.t: v. 驱散；消除（疑虑、恐惧）

e.en: The CEO held a meeting to {dispel} layoff rumors.
e.zh: 首席执行官召开会议以消除裁员传闻。

e.en: A short demo can {dispel} most doubts about the product.
e.zh: 一段简短的演示就能打消对产品的大部分疑虑。

dispensable.t: adj. 可有可无的；非必需的

e.en: In the new workflow, paper forms are {dispensable}.
e.zh: 在新的工作流程里，纸质表单是可有可无的。

e.en: No employee should feel completely {dispensable}.
e.zh: 没有哪位员工应该觉得自己完全可有可无。

e.en: Several cannabis {dispensaries} opened on Main Street last year.
e.zh: 去年大街上开了好几家大麻药房。

e.en: Rural {dispensaries} struggle to keep common medicines in stock.
e.zh: 乡村药房很难保持常用药品的库存。

e.en: The clinic's {dispensary} closes at six on weekdays.
e.zh: 诊所的药房工作日六点关门。

e.en: He works at a medical marijuana {dispensary} downtown.
e.zh: 他在市中心一家医用大麻药房工作。

e.en: She received special {dispensation} to skip the prerequisite.
e.zh: 她获得特别许可，可以跳过先修课程。

e.en: Under the new {dispensation}, remote work became standard.
e.zh: 在新的制度下，远程办公成为常态。

e.en: This machine can {dispense} both coffee and hot chocolate.
e.zh: 这台机器既能出咖啡，也能出热巧克力。

e.en: Let's {dispense} with the small talk and get to business.
e.zh: 我们就别寒暄了，直接进入正题吧。

e.en: The pharmacist {dispensed} the prescription within minutes.
e.zh: 药剂师几分钟内就配好了处方药。

e.en: She {dispensed} with formalities and called him by his first name.
e.zh: 她省去了客套，直接叫他的名字。

dispenser.t: n. 分配器；自动售货机

e.en: Please refill the soap {dispenser} in the bathroom.
e.zh: 请给洗手间的皂液器加满。

e.en: The hand sanitizer {dispenser} is mounted by the entrance.
e.zh: 洗手液分发器安装在入口旁边。

dispenses.t: v. 分发（第三人称单数）

e.en: This ATM {dispenses} cash in three different currencies.
e.zh: 这台自动取款机可以提取三种不同的货币。

e.en: The senior engineer {dispenses} advice generously to interns.
e.zh: 那位资深工程师慷慨地向实习生传授经验。

e.en: The robot is {dispensing} pills with perfect accuracy.
e.zh: 这台机器人正在精准地分发药片。

e.en: She walked in, {dispensing} hugs to everyone at the party.
e.zh: 她走进派对，给每个人都来了个拥抱。

e.en: Police ordered the immediate {dispersal} of the crowd.
e.zh: 警方命令人群立即散开。

e.en: Wind plays a key role in seed {dispersal} for many plants.
e.zh: 对许多植物来说，风在种子传播中起着关键作用。

e.en: The park has seen several {dispersals} of protest groups this week.
e.zh: 本周公园里已多次驱散抗议人群。

e.en: Researchers tracked the {dispersals} of young wolves from the pack.
e.zh: 研究人员追踪了幼狼离开狼群后的扩散路径。

e.en: Crews sprayed a chemical {dispersant} on the oil spill.
e.zh: 工作人员向漏油区喷洒了化学分散剂。

e.en: The {dispersant} breaks the slick into smaller droplets.
e.zh: 分散剂把油膜分解成更小的油滴。

e.en: Police asked the protesters to {disperse} peacefully.
e.zh: 警方要求抗议者和平散去。

e.en: The fog will {disperse} once the sun comes up.
e.zh: 太阳一出来，雾就会散去。

e.en: The crowd quickly {dispersed} after the concert ended.
e.zh: 演唱会结束后人群很快散去。

e.en: Our team is {dispersed} across five different time zones.
e.zh: 我们的团队分布在五个不同的时区。

disperses.t: v. 驱散（第三人称单数）

e.en: A good fan {disperses} heat evenly across the room.
e.zh: 一台好的风扇能让热量在整个房间均匀散开。

e.en: The tour guide {disperses} the group at the museum entrance.
e.zh: 导游在博物馆门口让大家自由活动。

e.en: The smoke is slowly {dispersing} into the night air.
e.zh: 烟雾正在夜空中慢慢散去。

e.en: Police were {dispersing} the crowd with loudspeakers.
e.zh: 警察正用扩音器驱散人群。

e.en: The prism causes a beautiful {dispersion} of light.
e.zh: 棱镜让光发生了美丽的色散。

e.en: Data shows wide {dispersion} in test scores this semester.
e.zh: 数据显示本学期考试成绩离散程度很大。

e.en: Glass has a {dispersive} effect that splits white light.
e.zh: 玻璃具有色散作用，能把白光分开。

e.en: The material's {dispersive} properties make it ideal for lenses.
e.zh: 这种材料的色散特性使它非常适合制作镜片。

e.en: Repeated rejections can {dispirit} even the most determined writer.
e.zh: 接连的拒绝会让最坚定的作家也丧失斗志。

e.en: Don't let one bad review {dispirit} the whole team.
e.zh: 别让一条差评让整个团队都泄气。

e.en: The players looked {dispirited} after the third loss in a row.
e.zh: 球员们在连续第三场失利后显得十分沮丧。

e.en: She felt {dispirited} by the slow progress of the project.
e.zh: 项目进展缓慢，让她感到心灰意冷。

dispiritedly.t: adv. 沮丧地；垂头丧气地

e.en: He shuffled {dispiritedly} back to his desk after the meeting.
e.zh: 开完会后，他垂头丧气地拖着脚步回到工位。

e.en: She stared {dispiritedly} at the empty inbox.
e.zh: 她沮丧地盯着空空如也的收件箱。

e.en: The constant rain made for a {dispiriting} weekend trip.
e.zh: 连绵不断的雨让这次周末旅行变得令人沮丧。

e.en: It's {dispiriting} to see your work ignored again and again.
e.zh: 看到自己的工作一次次被无视，实在让人灰心。

e.en: New AI tools may {displace} some routine office jobs.
e.zh: 新的人工智能工具可能会取代一些常规的办公岗位。

e.en: The flood will {displace} thousands of families this week.
e.zh: 这场洪水本周将使数千个家庭流离失所。

displaced.t: adj. 流离失所的；被取代的

e.en: The war has {displaced} millions of people from their homes.
e.zh: 战争使数百万人流离失所。

e.en: Streaming services have largely {displaced} traditional cable.
e.zh: 流媒体服务在很大程度上取代了传统有线电视。

dissertation.t: n. 学位论文；专题论述

e.en: She is finishing her PhD {dissertation} on machine learning.
e.zh: 她正在完成关于机器学习的博士论文。

e.en: His {dissertation} took five years to complete and defend.
e.zh: 他的论文花了五年时间才完成并答辩。

e.en: Oversimplifying the issue does a {disservice} to readers.
e.zh: 过度简化这个问题对读者是一种伤害。

e.en: You'd be doing yourself a {disservice} by quitting now.
e.zh: 现在放弃对你自己是一种损害。

e.en: The regime cracked down harshly on any sign of {dissidence}.
e.zh: 该政权对任何异见迹象都进行严厉镇压。

e.en: Open {dissidence} can be dangerous in authoritarian states.
e.zh: 在威权国家公开持异见可能很危险。

dissident.t:
n. 持不同政见者
adj. 持异议的

e.en: The {dissident} writer was forced into exile abroad.
e.zh: 那位持不同政见的作家被迫流亡海外。

e.en: She became a famous {dissident} during the regime's crackdown.
e.zh: 在该政权的打压期间,她成为了著名的异见人士。

dissidents.t: n. 持不同政见者（复数）

e.en: Several {dissidents} were arrested at the peaceful protest.
e.zh: 几名异见人士在和平抗议中被逮捕。

e.en: The country has long imprisoned political {dissidents}.
e.zh: 该国长期监禁政治异见人士。

e.en: The two products are surprisingly {dissimilar} despite the brand.
e.zh: 尽管同一品牌,这两款产品却出奇地不同。

e.en: Their writing styles are not entirely {dissimilar}.
e.zh: 他们的写作风格并非完全不同。

e.en: The {dissimilarity} between the twins surprised everyone.
e.zh: 这对双胞胎之间的差异让所有人都感到惊讶。

e.en: Researchers measured the {dissimilarity} between the two datasets.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了两个数据集之间的差异度。

e.en: Spies must {dissimulate} their true intentions at all times.
e.zh: 间谍必须时刻掩饰自己的真实意图。

e.en: He tried to {dissimulate} his nervousness during the speech.
e.zh: 演讲时他试图掩饰自己的紧张。

e.en: Her smile was pure {dissimulation} hiding deep anger.
e.zh: 她的微笑纯粹是掩饰,藏着深深的怒气。

e.en: Politics often rewards skillful {dissimulation} over honesty.
e.zh: 政治往往奖励高明的伪装而非诚实。

e.en: The fog will {dissipate} once the sun rises higher.
e.zh: 太阳升高后雾气就会消散。

e.en: His anger began to {dissipate} after a long walk.
e.zh: 长时间散步后,他的怒气开始消散。

dissipated.t:
adj. 放荡的
v. 消散（过去式）

e.en: The crowd {dissipated} quickly once the rain started.
e.zh: 雨一开始,人群就迅速散去了。

e.en: Her enthusiasm {dissipated} after the third rejection email.
e.zh: 收到第三封拒信后,她的热情消失殆尽。

e.en: Heat {dissipation} is critical for high-performance laptops.
e.zh: 散热对高性能笔记本电脑至关重要。

e.en: The {dissipation} of the storm brought welcome calm.
e.zh: 风暴的消散带来了令人欣慰的平静。

e.en: The {dissipative} forces gradually slowed the spinning wheel.
e.zh: 耗散力逐渐让旋转的轮子慢了下来。

e.en: Engineers added a {dissipative} layer to absorb vibration.
e.zh: 工程师加了一层耗散材料来吸收振动。

e.en: The brand tried to {dissociate} itself from the scandal.
e.zh: 该品牌试图与这起丑闻划清界限。

e.en: Heat causes the molecules to {dissociate} into ions.
e.zh: 高温使这些分子分解成离子。

dissociated.t:
adj. 分离的
v. 划清界限（过去式）

e.en: He {dissociated} himself from his former business partner.
e.zh: 他与过去的生意伙伴撇清了关系。

e.en: During the trauma she felt completely {dissociated} from reality.
e.zh: 创伤发生时她感觉与现实完全脱节。

dissociation.t: n. 分离；解离（化学/心理）

e.en: Therapy helped her cope with episodes of {dissociation}.
e.zh: 治疗帮助她应对解离发作。

e.en: The {dissociation} of water produces hydrogen and hydroxide ions.
e.zh: 水的电离会产生氢离子和氢氧根离子。

dissociative.t: adj. 分离性的；解离性的

e.en: She was diagnosed with a {dissociative} disorder last year.
e.zh: 她去年被诊断出患有解离性障碍。

e.en: Some anesthetics have strong {dissociative} effects on patients.
e.zh: 某些麻醉药对患者有很强的解离效应。

dissolute.t: adj. 放荡的；生活不检点的

e.en: The novel describes the {dissolute} lifestyle of the young aristocrats.
e.zh: 小说描写了年轻贵族放荡的生活方式。

e.en: After his fortune ran out, he abandoned his {dissolute} habits.
e.zh: 钱花光后,他改掉了那些放荡的习惯。

e.en: The {dissolution} of the company surprised the investors.
e.zh: 公司的解散让投资者大感意外。

e.en: They filed papers for the {dissolution} of their marriage.
e.zh: 他们递交了离婚解除婚姻关系的文件。

e.en: Stir the sugar until it fully {dissolves} in the tea.
e.zh: 搅拌糖,直到它完全溶在茶里。

e.en: The court agreed to {dissolve} their partnership amicably.
e.zh: 法院同意友好解除他们的合伙关系。

dissolved.t:
adj. 溶解的
v. 解散（过去式）

e.en: The salt {dissolved} quickly in the warm water.
e.zh: 盐很快就溶解在温水里。

e.en: Parliament was {dissolved} ahead of the general election.
e.zh: 议会在大选前被解散了。

dissolves.t: v. 溶解；解散（第三人称单数）

e.en: This tablet {dissolves} on your tongue within seconds.
e.zh: 这种药片放在舌头上几秒就化了。

e.en: Time {dissolves} even the strongest grudges eventually.
e.zh: 时间最终会化解再深的怨恨。

dissolving.t: v. 正在溶解；正在解散

e.en: She watched the sugar slowly {dissolving} in her coffee.
e.zh: 她看着糖慢慢在咖啡里化开。

e.en: The board is {dissolving} the committee next month.
e.zh: 董事会下个月将解散这个委员会。

e.en: The cognitive {dissonance} between his words and actions was obvious.
e.zh: 他言行之间的认知失调显而易见。

e.en: The composer used sharp {dissonance} to create tension.
e.zh: 作曲家用刺耳的不协和音来营造紧张感。

dissonant.t: adj. 不和谐的；不一致的

e.en: The film's score is full of {dissonant} chords.
e.zh: 这部电影的配乐充满了不协和的和弦。

e.en: Her cheerful tone felt {dissonant} with the somber news.
e.zh: 她欢快的语气与沉重的消息显得格格不入。

e.en: Friends tried to {dissuade} him from quitting his job.
e.zh: 朋友们试图劝他不要辞职。

e.en: Nothing could {dissuade} her from going on the trip.
e.zh: 什么都无法劝阻她踏上这次旅行。

e.en: The story traces her {distaff} ancestry back four generations.
e.zh: 这个故事追溯了她母系四代的血脉。

e.en: In the museum we saw a wooden spinning {distaff}.
e.zh: 我们在博物馆看到了一根木制的纺纱杆。

e.en: Critics {distain} the film for its shallow plot.
e.zh: 评论家因情节肤浅而贬低这部电影。

e.en: He spoke with open {distain} about the proposal.
e.zh: 他对这个提议毫不掩饰地表示轻蔑。

e.en: The injury affected the {distal} end of the bone.
e.zh: 伤势影响到了骨头的远端。

e.en: Doctors examined the {distal} joint of her finger.
e.zh: 医生检查了她手指的远端关节。

e.en: The nerve runs {distally} along the forearm to the wrist.
e.zh: 这条神经沿前臂向远端延伸至手腕。

e.en: The fracture is located {distally} on the femur.
e.zh: 骨折部位位于股骨的远端。

distance.t:
n. 距离；远方
v. 疏远

e.en: The {distance} between the two cities is about 300 kilometers.
e.zh: 两座城市之间的距离大约是 300 公里。

e.en: He tried to {distance} himself from the controversy.
e.zh: 他试图与这场争议保持距离。

e.en: She gradually {distanced} herself from her toxic friends.
e.zh: 她渐渐疏远了那些有害的朋友。

e.en: The CEO {distanced} the company from the controversial ad.
e.zh: CEO 让公司与那条有争议的广告划清界限。

distances.t:
n. 距离（复数）
v. 疏远

e.en: Runners train to handle longer {distances} every week.
e.zh: 跑者每周训练以应对更长的距离。

e.en: She {distances} herself whenever the topic comes up.
e.zh: 每次话题被提起,她都会刻意保持距离。

e.en: Social {distancing} became routine during the pandemic.
e.zh: 在疫情期间,保持社交距离成了日常。

e.en: He's been {distancing} himself from the project lately.
e.zh: 他最近一直在与这个项目保持距离。

e.en: We could hear the {distant} sound of thunder.
e.zh: 我们能听到远处传来的雷声。

e.en: She seemed cold and {distant} during the meeting.
e.zh: 她在会议上显得冷淡而疏远。

e.en: They are {distantly} related through their grandmothers.
e.zh: 他们通过祖母那边有远亲关系。

e.en: He smiled {distantly}, lost in his own thoughts.
e.zh: 他心不在焉地笑了笑,沉浸在自己的思绪里。

e.en: She wrinkled her nose in {distaste} at the smell.
e.zh: 她闻到那股味道,皱起鼻子表示厌恶。

e.en: He has a clear {distaste} for office politics.
e.zh: 他对办公室政治有着明显的反感。

distasteful.t: adj. 令人反感的；讨厌的

e.en: Many viewers found the joke {distasteful} and offensive.
e.zh: 许多观众觉得这个笑话令人反感且冒犯。

e.en: Firing loyal employees was a {distasteful} task for him.
e.zh: 解雇忠诚的员工对他来说是件令人不快的事。

e.en: She frowned {distastefully} at the messy kitchen.
e.zh: 她厌恶地皱着眉看着乱糟糟的厨房。

e.en: He spoke {distastefully} about the company's new policy.
e.zh: 他对公司的新政策语带反感地谈论着。

e.en: The puppy was vaccinated against {distemper} last week.
e.zh: 小狗上周接种了犬瘟热疫苗。

e.en: The old walls were painted with traditional {distemper}.
e.zh: 那面旧墙刷的是传统的胶画颜料。

e.en: Too much air can {distend} the patient's stomach painfully.
e.zh: 气体过多会使病人的胃痛苦地胀大。

e.en: The balloon began to {distend} as we pumped it.
e.zh: 我们打气时气球开始膨胀起来。

e.en: The child's belly was visibly {distended} from malnutrition.
e.zh: 那孩子的肚子因营养不良明显鼓胀着。

e.en: Doctors noticed {distended} veins on the patient's neck.
e.zh: 医生注意到病人脖子上的静脉怒张。

e.en: The patient complained of bloating and abdominal {distension}.
e.zh: 病人主诉腹胀和腹部膨隆。

e.en: Severe {distension} of the bladder requires immediate attention.
e.zh: 膀胱严重膨胀需要立即处理。

e.en: The {distent} stomach worried the veterinarian immediately.
e.zh: 鼓胀的胃立刻让兽医担心起来。

e.en: She felt her abdomen become {distent} after the meal.
e.zh: 饭后她感到腹部胀了起来。

e.en: Bowel {distention} can be a sign of obstruction.
e.zh: 肠道膨胀可能是阻塞的征兆。

e.en: The scan revealed slight {distention} of the gallbladder.
e.zh: 扫描显示胆囊有轻微膨胀。

distil.t: v. 蒸馏；提炼（英式拼写）

e.en: They {distil} fresh seawater into drinkable water on the boat.
e.zh: 他们在船上把新鲜海水蒸馏成可饮用水。

e.en: Good editors {distil} long reports into a single page.
e.zh: 好的编辑能把长报告浓缩成一页。

e.en: The book tries to {distill} decades of research into clear advice.
e.zh: 这本书试图把几十年的研究浓缩成清晰的建议。

e.en: They {distill} their own gin in a small copper still.
e.zh: 他们用一个小铜蒸馏器自己酿杜松子酒。

e.en: The chemist analyzed the {distillate} for impurities.
e.zh: 化学家分析这种蒸馏液有无杂质。

e.en: The book is a {distillate} of his lifetime experience.
e.zh: 这本书是他一生经验的精华。

e.en: The chapter is a neat {distillation} of his philosophy.
e.zh: 这一章是他哲学思想的精炼总结。

e.en: Whiskey production requires careful {distillation} of fermented grains.
e.zh: 威士忌的生产需要对发酵谷物进行精心蒸馏。

e.en: Several {distillations} are needed to achieve high purity.
e.zh: 要达到高纯度需要进行多次蒸馏。

e.en: His essays are {distillations} of years of teaching experience.
e.zh: 他的文章是多年教学经验的精华。

displacement.t:
n. 位移；取代
n. (人口) 流离失所

e.en: Climate change is causing widespread {displacement} of communities.
e.zh: 气候变化正导致众多社区被迫迁离。

e.en: The engine has a {displacement} of two liters.
e.zh: 这台发动机的排量为两升。

displaces.t: v. 取代；使移位（第三人称单数）

e.en: A heavier ship {displaces} more water than a lighter one.
e.zh: 船越重，排开的水就越多。

e.en: Each new feature {displaces} something else from the homepage.
e.zh: 每加一个新功能，主页上就得挤掉别的东西。

displacing.t: v. 取代；使离开原位（现在分词）

e.en: Gentrification is {displacing} long-time residents from the neighborhood.
e.zh: 中产化正在把街区里的老住户挤走。

e.en: The boat sat low, {displacing} a lot of water.
e.zh: 船吃水很深，排开了大量的水。

display.t:
v. 显示；展示
n. 显示器；展览

e.en: The store will {display} the new phones starting Monday.
e.zh: 这家店将从周一开始展示新款手机。

e.en: The laptop has a sharp 4K {display}.
e.zh: 这款笔记本配有清晰的4K显示屏。

e.en: Her photos are {displayed} in a small downtown gallery.
e.zh: 她的照片在市中心一家小画廊展出。

e.en: The error message {displayed} for only a second.
e.zh: 那条错误提示只显示了一秒钟。

displaying.t: v. 显示；展示（现在分词）

e.en: The screen kept {displaying} the same loading icon.
e.zh: 屏幕一直显示着同一个加载图标。

e.en: He's {displaying} real leadership during this crisis.
e.zh: 在这次危机中他展现出了真正的领导力。

displays.t:
v. 显示（第三人称单数）
n. 显示器（复数）

e.en: The museum {displays} artifacts from across Asia.
e.zh: 这家博物馆展出来自亚洲各地的文物。

e.en: Modern OLED {displays} offer deeper blacks than LCDs.
e.zh: 现代OLED显示屏的黑色比液晶屏更深邃。

e.en: Raising prices now would {displease} long-time customers.
e.zh: 现在涨价会让老顾客不满。

e.en: He chose his words carefully so as not to {displease} his boss.
e.zh: 他措辞谨慎，以免惹恼老板。

e.en: The manager looked {displeased} with the quarterly results.
e.zh: 经理对季度业绩显得很不满意。

e.en: She was clearly {displeased} by the late delivery.
e.zh: 对于送货迟到，她显然很不高兴。

e.en: He expressed his {displeasure} with the new dress code.
e.zh: 他对新着装规定表达了不满。

e.en: Fans voiced their {displeasure} on social media after the trade.
e.zh: 球员交易后，球迷在社交媒体上表达了不满。

e.en: The CEO listed his {displeasures} with the marketing plan.
e.zh: 首席执行官列出了他对营销方案不满的几处地方。

e.en: Small {displeasures} can pile up into real workplace tension.
e.zh: 一些小小的不快累积起来会变成真正的职场紧张。

e.en: Children {disport} themselves happily in the shallow waves.
e.zh: 孩子们在浅浪中开心地嬉戏玩耍。

e.en: Otters often {disport} along the riverbank at dusk.
e.zh: 水獭常在黄昏时分在河岸边嬉戏。

disposable.t:
adj. 一次性的；可任意支配的
n. 一次性用品

e.en: Most cafes still hand out {disposable} cups for takeaway coffee.
e.zh: 大多数咖啡店仍然提供一次性外带咖啡杯。

e.en: Young families have less {disposable} income these days.
e.zh: 如今年轻家庭的可支配收入越来越少。

disposal.t:
n. 处理；丢弃
n. 支配权

e.en: Proper {disposal} of old batteries protects the environment.
e.zh: 妥善处理旧电池有助于保护环境。

e.en: The hotel has a free shuttle at your {disposal}.
e.zh: 酒店提供免费班车供您使用。

e.en: The city installed new waste {disposals} in every park.
e.zh: 市政府在每个公园都安装了新的垃圾处理设施。

e.en: Recent asset {disposals} helped the company reduce its debt.
e.zh: 近期的资产处置帮助公司削减了债务。

dispose.t:
v. 处理；丢弃
v. 安排；使倾向于

e.en: Please {dispose} of the packaging in the recycling bin.
e.zh: 请把包装扔进回收箱。

e.en: Long walks always {dispose} her toward a calmer mood.
e.zh: 长时间散步总能让她心情变得平静。

disposed.t:
adj. 有意向的
v. 处理（过去式）

e.en: He {disposed} of the old laptop at the e-waste center.
e.zh: 他把旧笔记本电脑送到了电子垃圾回收中心。

e.en: She seemed kindly {disposed} toward the new intern.
e.zh: 她对那位新实习生看起来颇有好感。

disposer.t: n. 处理者；（厨房）垃圾处理器

e.en: Our kitchen sink has a built-in food waste {disposer}.
e.zh: 我们的厨房水槽装有内置的食物垃圾处理器。

e.en: The court named him sole {disposer} of the estate.
e.zh: 法院指定他为遗产的唯一处置人。

disposes.t: v. 处理；处置（第三人称单数）

e.en: The app automatically {disposes} of expired cache files.
e.zh: 该应用会自动清理过期的缓存文件。

e.en: Regular exercise {disposes} people to better sleep.
e.zh: 经常运动会让人更容易睡得好。

disposing.t: v. 处理；安排（现在分词）

e.en: The factory was fined for illegally {disposing} of chemicals.
e.zh: 该工厂因非法处置化学品而被罚款。

e.en: She spent the morning {disposing} of unwanted clothes.
e.zh: 她整个上午都在处理不要的衣服。

disposition.t:
n. 性情；倾向
n. 安排；处置

e.en: The puppy has a friendly {disposition} around strangers.
e.zh: 这只小狗对陌生人很友善。

e.en: The judge will rule on the {disposition} of the assets.
e.zh: 法官将就资产的处置作出裁决。

e.en: Psychologists study {dispositional} traits like optimism and patience.
e.zh: 心理学家研究乐观、耐心等性格特质。

e.en: The court issued a {dispositional} order for the minor.
e.zh: 法院对该未成年人发出了处置令。

e.en: Twins can have surprisingly different {dispositions} from birth.
e.zh: 双胞胎从出生起性情就可能截然不同。

e.en: The will outlines the {dispositions} of all family property.
e.zh: 遗嘱列明了所有家庭财产的处置安排。

dispositive.t: adj. 决定性的（法律用语）

e.en: The DNA evidence proved {dispositive} in the murder case.
e.zh: 在这宗谋杀案中,DNA证据具有决定性作用。

e.en: Her testimony was not {dispositive} but it helped the jury.
e.zh: 她的证词虽非决定性,但对陪审团有所帮助。

dispossess.t: v. 剥夺；没收（财产、土地）

e.en: The new law makes it harder to {dispossess} tenants.
e.zh: 新法律使驱逐租户变得更加困难。

e.en: Colonial powers tried to {dispossess} indigenous communities of their land.
e.zh: 殖民势力曾试图剥夺原住民社区的土地。

dispossessed.t: adj. 被剥夺财产的；流离失所的

e.en: The novel tells the story of a {dispossessed} family.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述了一个被剥夺家园的家庭的故事。

e.en: War {dispossessed} thousands of farmers across the region.
e.zh: 战争使该地区数千名农民失去了家园。

e.en: The film documents the {dispossession} of native communities.
e.zh: 这部影片记录了原住民社区被剥夺家园的历史。

e.en: Forced {dispossession} left many families without homes.
e.zh: 强制剥夺财产让许多家庭无家可归。

e.en: Scientists found clear {disproof} of the old hypothesis.
e.zh: 科学家找到了推翻旧假说的明确证据。

e.en: Her experiment offered a definitive {disproof} of the theory.
e.zh: 她的实验对这一理论给出了决定性的反驳。

e.en: There's a clear {disproportion} between effort and reward here.
e.zh: 这里付出和回报之间明显不成比例。

e.en: The painting's odd {disproportion} makes the figure look unsettling.
e.zh: 画中怪异的比例失调让人物显得令人不安。

disproportional.t: adj. 不成比例的；不相称的

e.en: The penalty seemed {disproportional} to the small mistake.
e.zh: 对这个小错误的惩罚似乎不成比例。

e.en: Critics say the tax burden is {disproportional} across income groups.
e.zh: 批评者认为各收入群体的税负并不成比例。

disproportionality.t: n. 不成比例；不均衡性

e.en: Researchers noted the {disproportionality} in school discipline rates.
e.zh: 研究人员注意到学校处分比例的不成比例现象。

e.en: The report highlights racial {disproportionality} in arrests.
e.zh: 报告强调了逮捕中存在的种族比例失衡。

disproportionate.t: adj. 不成比例的；过度的

e.en: Streaming takes a {disproportionate} share of household bandwidth.
e.zh: 流媒体占用了家庭带宽中过大的份额。

e.en: Small businesses bear a {disproportionate} burden under the new rule.
e.zh: 在新规之下,小企业承担了过重的负担。

disproportionately.t: adv. 不成比例地；过度地

e.en: The pandemic affected low-income workers {disproportionately}.
e.zh: 疫情对低收入工人造成的影响过于严重。

e.en: Older users are {disproportionately} targeted by phone scams.
e.zh: 老年用户尤其容易成为电话诈骗的目标。

e.en: A single counterexample is enough to {disprove} the theory.
e.zh: 一个反例就足以推翻这个理论。

e.en: She set out to {disprove} the rumor about her resignation.
e.zh: 她决心要驳斥关于她辞职的谣言。

disputable.t: adj. 有争议的；可辩驳的

e.en: Whether the policy actually works is highly {disputable}.
e.zh: 这项政策是否真的有效非常值得商榷。

e.en: The survey's conclusions remain {disputable} among experts.
e.zh: 这项调查的结论在专家之间仍有争议。

e.en: The mediator listened carefully to each {disputant} in turn.
e.zh: 调解员依次仔细倾听每位争议方的陈述。

e.en: Both sides hired lawyers as the {disputant} count grew.
e.zh: 随着争议方人数增加,双方都聘请了律师。

e.en: Medieval scholars trained for years in formal {disputation}.
e.zh: 中世纪学者要花数年时间训练正式辩论。

e.en: The meeting devolved into noisy {disputation} over the budget.
e.zh: 会议演变成了围绕预算的吵闹争论。

disputatious.t: adj. 好争辩的；爱抬杠的

e.en: Her {disputatious} uncle argues at every family dinner.
e.zh: 她那爱争论的叔叔在每次家庭聚餐都要吵一番。

e.en: The committee grew {disputatious} as deadlines approached.
e.zh: 随着最后期限临近,委员会变得争吵不断。

dispute.t:
n. 争议；纠纷
v. 争论；质疑

e.en: Neighbors are in a {dispute} over the garden fence.
e.zh: 邻居之间因花园围栏闹起了纠纷。

e.en: Few experts {dispute} that the climate is warming.
e.zh: 几乎没有专家会否认气候正在变暖。

disputed.t:
adj. 有争议的
v. 争论（过去式）

e.en: The two villages share a long-{disputed} stretch of river.
e.zh: 这两个村子共有一段长期存在争议的河段。

e.en: She {disputed} the bank charge and got a refund.
e.zh: 她对银行收费提出异议并获得了退款。

disputes.t:
n. 争议（复数）
v. 争论（第三人称单数）

e.en: Online {disputes} between neighbors often spill into court.
e.zh: 邻里间的网上纠纷常常会闹上法庭。

e.en: He {disputes} the claim that remote work hurts productivity.
e.zh: 他不认同远程工作会损害生产力的说法。

disputing.t: v. 争论；质疑（现在分词）

e.en: There's no {disputing} that streaming has changed the music industry.
e.zh: 无可否认,流媒体已经改变了音乐产业。

e.en: They spent hours {disputing} who should pay the bill.
e.zh: 他们花了好几个小时争论谁该买单。

disqualification.t: n. 取消资格；丧失资格

e.en: A positive drug test means automatic {disqualification} from the race.
e.zh: 药检阳性意味着自动取消比赛资格。

e.en: The referee announced his {disqualification} after the foul.
e.zh: 那次犯规之后,裁判宣布取消他的资格。

disqualified.t: adj. 被取消资格的；不合格的

e.en: The runner was {disqualified} for stepping out of her lane.
e.zh: 那名跑者因踩出跑道而被取消资格。

e.en: His criminal record {disqualified} him from the security job.
e.zh: 他的犯罪记录使他失去了那份保安工作的资格。

disqualifies.t: v. 取消资格（第三人称单数）

e.en: Missing the deadline {disqualifies} you from the scholarship.
e.zh: 错过截止日期会让你失去申请奖学金的资格。

e.en: A conflict of interest {disqualifies} the judge from this case.
e.zh: 利益冲突使该法官无法审理此案。

disqualify.t: v. 取消…的资格；使不合格

e.en: Cheating will instantly {disqualify} a player from the tournament.
e.zh: 作弊会让选手立即被取消参赛资格。

e.en: A late application can {disqualify} you from consideration.
e.zh: 申请逾期可能会让你失去被考虑的资格。

disqualifying.t: v. 取消资格（现在分词）

e.en: Lying on the form is a {disqualifying} offense.
e.zh: 在表格上撒谎属于会被取消资格的违规行为。

e.en: The committee is {disqualifying} entries that miss the word limit.
e.zh: 委员会正在取消超出字数限制的参赛作品的资格。

disquiet.t:
n. 不安；忧虑
v. 使不安

e.en: News of the layoffs spread {disquiet} through the office.
e.zh: 裁员的消息让办公室里弥漫着不安。

e.en: The strange silence began to {disquiet} the hikers.
e.zh: 那诡异的寂静让徒步者们感到不安。

disquieting.t: adj. 令人不安的；令人忧虑的

e.en: The report contained several {disquieting} findings about water quality.
e.zh: 报告中关于水质有几项令人不安的发现。

e.en: There's something {disquieting} about that empty old house.
e.zh: 那座空荡荡的老房子让人觉得有些不安。

disquisition.t: n. 长篇论述；专题论文

e.en: He launched into a long {disquisition} on coffee beans.
e.zh: 他开始就咖啡豆长篇大论起来。

e.en: The professor's {disquisition} on free will captivated the class.
e.zh: 教授关于自由意志的长篇论述吸引了全班同学。

disraeli.t: n. 迪斯雷利（英国前首相）

e.en: Benjamin {Disraeli} served twice as British Prime Minister.
e.zh: 本杰明·迪斯雷利曾两度出任英国首相。

e.en: Students read a famous speech by {Disraeli} in history class.
e.zh: 学生们在历史课上阅读了迪斯雷利的一篇著名演讲。

disregard.t:
v. 忽视，漠视
n. 漠视

e.en: Please {disregard} the previous email — I sent the wrong file.
e.zh: 请忽略之前那封邮件,我发错了文件。

e.en: Drivers who {disregard} speed limits put everyone at risk.
e.zh: 无视限速的司机会让所有人陷入危险。

disregards.t: v. 忽视，漠视（第三人称单数）

e.en: The new policy completely {disregards} feedback from frontline staff.
e.zh: 新政策完全无视一线员工的反馈。

e.en: He often {disregards} safety rules at the construction site.
e.zh: 他在工地上常常无视安全规定。

disrepair.t: n. 年久失修，破损状态

e.en: The old bridge has fallen into serious {disrepair}.
e.zh: 那座老桥已经严重失修。

e.en: Years of neglect left the school building in {disrepair}.
e.zh: 多年的疏于维护让校舍变得破败不堪。

disreputable.t: adj. 名声不好的，不体面的

e.en: Avoid {disreputable} websites that ask for your bank details.
e.zh: 避开那些索要银行信息的不正规网站。

e.en: The neighborhood used to be a {disreputable} part of town.
e.zh: 那一带过去是城里名声不好的地方。

e.en: The scandal brought the entire industry into {disrepute}.
e.zh: 这场丑闻让整个行业声誉扫地。

e.en: Repeated cheating dragged the league into {disrepute}.
e.zh: 屡次作弊让该联赛声名狼藉。

disrespect.t:
n. 不尊重，无礼
v. 轻视

e.en: Interrupting elders is seen as a sign of {disrespect}.
e.zh: 打断长辈说话被视为不尊重的表现。

e.en: No {disrespect} intended, but I disagree with your plan.
e.zh: 无意冒犯,但我不同意你的计划。

e.en: She felt {disrespected} when her ideas were ignored in meetings.
e.zh: 开会时她的想法被无视,让她感到不被尊重。

e.en: Fans complained that the announcer {disrespected} the visiting team.
e.zh: 球迷抱怨解说员对客队不够尊重。

e.en: It's {disrespectful} to take phone calls during a funeral.
e.zh: 在葬礼上接电话是不礼貌的。

e.en: His {disrespectful} tone got him in trouble with the manager.
e.zh: 他无礼的语气惹恼了经理。

e.en: The customer spoke {disrespectfully} to the young waiter.
e.zh: 那位顾客对年轻服务员说话很不客气。

e.en: Don't treat your teammates {disrespectfully} during practice.
e.zh: 训练时不要对队友无礼。

e.en: Patients are asked to {disrobe} behind the curtain before exams.
e.zh: 在体检前,患者被要求到帘子后面脱去衣物。

e.en: The actor had to {disrobe} for a brief scene in the film.
e.zh: 演员在影片的一个短镜头中需要脱去衣服。

e.en: Heavy snow may {disrupt} flights at the airport tomorrow.
e.zh: 明天的大雪可能会扰乱机场的航班。

e.en: Streaming services continue to {disrupt} traditional television.
e.zh: 流媒体服务持续冲击着传统电视行业。

e.en: The storm {disrupted} flights across the entire east coast.
e.zh: 风暴扰乱了整个东海岸的航班。

e.en: Streaming services {disrupted} the traditional music industry.
e.zh: 流媒体服务颠覆了传统音乐产业。

e.en: Tesla became a major {disrupter} in the auto industry.
e.zh: 特斯拉成为汽车行业的重要颠覆者。

e.en: The startup positioned itself as a {disrupter} of legacy banking.
e.zh: 这家初创公司将自己定位为传统银行业的颠覆者。

e.en: AI tools are {disrupting} how designers work today.
e.zh: 人工智能工具正在颠覆当今设计师的工作方式。

e.en: Stop {disrupting} the meeting with side conversations.
e.zh: 别再用私下交谈打断会议了。

e.en: The outage caused major {disruption} to online services.
e.zh: 这次故障对在线服务造成了严重干扰。

e.en: Digital {disruption} has transformed nearly every industry.
e.zh: 数字化颠覆几乎改变了每一个行业。

e.en: Supply chain {disruptions} delayed shipments for months.
e.zh: 供应链中断导致货物延误了数月。

e.en: Frequent {disruptions} during class made learning difficult.
e.zh: 课堂上频繁的干扰让学习变得困难。

disruptive.t: adj. 颠覆性的，破坏性的

e.en: The iPhone was a {disruptive} technology when launched.
e.zh: iPhone 推出时是一项颠覆性技术。

e.en: His {disruptive} behavior got him sent to the principal.
e.zh: 他扰乱秩序的行为让他被送到校长那里。

e.en: The {disruptiveness} of remote work surprised many CEOs.
e.zh: 远程办公的颠覆性让许多 CEO 感到意外。

e.en: Teachers complained about the child's constant {disruptiveness}.
e.zh: 老师们抱怨这孩子总是扰乱秩序。

e.en: Airbnb is the classic {disruptor} of the hotel industry.
e.zh: Airbnb 是酒店业的典型颠覆者。

e.en: Every market eventually faces a new {disruptor}.
e.zh: 每个市场最终都会面临新的颠覆者。

disrupts.t: v. 扰乱（第三人称单数）

e.en: Caffeine often {disrupts} my sleep at night.
e.zh: 咖啡因常常扰乱我的夜间睡眠。

e.en: The new app {disrupts} how people book travel.
e.zh: 这款新应用颠覆了人们预订旅行的方式。

e.en: Don't {diss} my favorite band in front of me.
e.zh: 别当着我的面贬低我最喜欢的乐队。

e.en: The rapper released a {diss} track aimed at his rival.
e.zh: 那位说唱歌手发布了一首针对对手的贬损歌曲。

e.en: Customer {dissatisfaction} with the app reached record levels.
e.zh: 用户对该应用的不满达到了创纪录的水平。

e.en: She expressed her {dissatisfaction} with the new policy.
e.zh: 她对新政策表达了不满。

e.en: The survey revealed many {dissatisfactions} among employees.
e.zh: 调查揭示了员工中存在许多不满。

e.en: Small daily {dissatisfactions} eventually drove him to quit.
e.zh: 日常的种种不满最终促使他辞职。

e.en: Customers were {dissatisfied} with the slow delivery times.
e.zh: 顾客对缓慢的送货速度很不满意。

e.en: He felt {dissatisfied} with his career and decided to switch.
e.zh: 他对自己的职业感到不满,决定转行。

e.en: Vague answers tend to {dissatisfy} curious customers.
e.zh: 含糊的回答往往会让好奇的顾客感到不满。

e.en: Cutting features will only {dissatisfy} loyal users.
e.zh: 削减功能只会让忠实用户失望。

e.en: Critics will {dissect} every line of the new novel.
e.zh: 评论家会仔细剖析这部新小说的每一行。

e.en: Biology students learn to {dissect} a frog in class.
e.zh: 生物学生在课上学习解剖青蛙。

e.en: Analysts {dissected} the CEO's speech word by word.
e.zh: 分析师逐字剖析了 CEO 的演讲。

e.en: The students {dissected} a fish during lab session.
e.zh: 学生们在实验课上解剖了一条鱼。

e.en: Fans spent hours {dissecting} the show's finale online.
e.zh: 粉丝们花了数小时在网上分析剧集结局。

e.en: The professor was {dissecting} a specimen for the class.
e.zh: 教授正在为全班解剖一个标本。

e.en: Frog {dissection} is a classic high school biology lesson.
e.zh: 青蛙解剖是经典的高中生物课。

e.en: Her {dissection} of the argument exposed several flaws.
e.zh: 她对这个论点的剖析揭示了几处缺陷。

e.en: The lab performs hundreds of {dissections} each semester.
e.zh: 该实验室每学期进行数百次解剖。

e.en: His detailed {dissections} of films attract millions of viewers.
e.zh: 他对电影的详细解析吸引了数百万观众。

dissects.t: v. 解剖（第三人称单数）

e.en: The podcast {dissects} major political events each week.
e.zh: 该播客每周剖析重大政治事件。

e.en: The surgeon carefully {dissects} the tissue around the nerve.
e.zh: 外科医生小心地剥离神经周围的组织。

dissemble.t: v. 掩饰（真实感情或意图）

e.en: Skilled politicians often {dissemble} when asked tough questions.
e.zh: 老练的政客在被问及棘手问题时常会掩饰真意。

e.en: He tried to {dissemble} his disappointment with a smile.
e.zh: 他试图用微笑来掩饰自己的失望。

e.en: She {dissembled} her true feelings during the interview.
e.zh: 她在面试中掩饰了自己的真实感受。

e.en: The witness {dissembled} when asked about the evening's events.
e.zh: 证人在被问及当晚事件时含糊其辞。

e.en: The novel's villain is a charming {dissembler}.
e.zh: 小说中的反派是个迷人的伪装者。

e.en: Voters eventually saw through the clever {dissembler}.
e.zh: 选民最终看穿了那个狡猾的伪善者。

dissembles.t: v. 掩饰（第三人称单数）
